rationale_evidence.anchor: 88.10 — Information is task-dependent ... Evidence can contain substantial information about X while containing almost no information about D. InformationValue=f(Information,Question). There is no universal scalar called 'how informative this document is.'
rationale_evidence.statement: States information value is task-dependent, InformationValue=f(Information,Question); there is no universal 'informativeness' scalar independent of the question asked.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 88.12 — This is important for KnowledgeOS ... A 500-page architecture document is not necessarily more useful than a one-page ADR. What decision-relevant information does each artifact contain?
rationale_evidence.statement: Draws the practical KnowledgeOS lesson: document size is irrelevant; the question is what decision-relevant information each artifact contains (a 500-page document need not beat a one-page ADR).

rationale_evidence.anchor: 88.40 — Retrieval is also an information channel ... R(Q) for a query Q. X_R⊂X. D=f(X_R). Retrieval itself can create information loss.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues retrieval R(Q) returning a subset X_R⊂X is itself an information channel and can create information loss affecting decisions D=f(X_R).

rationale_evidence.anchor: 88.54 — But entropy reduction alone is insufficient ... E_1 reduces uncertainty about an irrelevant variable. E_2 slightly reduces uncertainty directly affecting the decision. I(E_1;D)<I(E_2;D) may hold even if H(X|E_1) falls substantially.
rationale_evidence.statement: Warns entropy reduction alone is insufficient: reducing uncertainty about an irrelevant variable can have lower decision-relevant mutual information I(E_1;D) than a small reduction directly relevant to D.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 88.71 — Information bottleneck for AI agents ... An AI agent may receive only a context window C⊂K. C is an information bottleneck. The agent cannot reason from information it never receives.
rationale_evidence.statement: Extends the information-bottleneck framing to AI agents: a context window C⊂K is itself an information bottleneck since the agent cannot reason from information it never receives.

rows.statement: The discovery's core structural result: BC-7's invariants (I-1 single mutation owner, I-2 HANDOFF+human START, I-3 sticky STOPPED, G-1 closure is a governance act, G-2 single writer for the Authority State) are all mechanically enforced, while almost every invariant outside BC-7 (R-34 producer!=acceptor, INV-ATTR-2 separation, AIP-11 frozen-artifact supersession, AIP-14 Product Primacy) is declared only, with no enforcement mechanism.
invariants: I-2 HANDOFF and human START jointly required
G-1 closure is a governance act
G-2 Authority State has exactly one writer

rows.anchor: this verification lane has no START on the record, so this report is produced off-record, the second occurrence at the "Verification #3" slot in this estate.
rows.statement: Finding X-2: this verification's own workflow lane has no recorded START, meaning the report is produced off-record -- the second occurrence of the same lifecycle-gap pattern at a 'Verification #3' slot across this estate, classified as a platform gap (bearing on C-10/knowledge-distribution and G-3) rather than a defect of Correction #2.

rows.anchor: Correction #2 finished its work and said so in the artifact, but its lane never handed off -- it still held mutation ownership when this act arrived.
rows.statement: A recurring delivery/record gap pattern is recorded: an artifact states it is delivered, but the lane that produced it never performed the corresponding HANDOFF transition, so the workflow record lags the actual work; Governance performs the handoff now rather than back-dating it.

rows.anchor: X-2 is a live blocker ... the work item's mutationOwner is None: seq 14 handed off to a lane that then never STARTed, so ownership was released and never taken up. Consequently no lane can hand off
rows.statement: A workflow lane that is HANDED_OFF to but never STARTed leaves mutationOwner as None, mechanically blocking every subsequent lane's handoff (Inv C requires the current mutation owner to hand off) -- a live, measured blocker rather than a theoretical one, confirmed by probing a scratch copy of the record.
invariants: Inv C: only the current mutation owner can hand off

experiment.hypothesis: the record is blocked because mutationOwner is None
experiment.setup: probe a scratch copy of the workflow record with a hand-off attempt
experiment.assumptions: the engine's stated invariant Inv C governs handoff
experiment.method: attempt a handoff on a scratch copy, observe refusal
experiment.result: refused: only the current mutation owner can hand off (Inv C)
experiment.interpretation: nothing further can START until the gap is disposed
experiment.limitations: live file untouched, so this is a controlled probe not a live mutation

rows.anchor: Option A -- transcribing the missing START -- is not available to Governance. A transcription records a human act that was given. No such act exists in this lane's record, and Governance may not supply one.
rows.statement: Governance determines it cannot itself transcribe a missing human START act, because a transcription records a fact (that a human act occurred) which only the PO/ARB can supply; Governance instead retains the report as evidence produced off-record, leaving option A open to the PO/ARB at any time.

rows.anchor: restoring append-only history is itself a history edit, two lanes were writing this file the same day, and a restoration performed without authority would repeat the very defect it repairs.
rows.statement: Governance declines to restore 73 deleted lines from an append-only session log, reasoning that restoring append-only history is itself a history-edit and could repeat the defect it would fix; it instead recommends preserving current history with an explicit recovery-commit pointer.
invariants: append-only history should not be silently restored/rewritten

rows.anchor: The record is not broken. It is exactly ONE HUMAN ACT short.
rows.statement: Diagnosis: the entire workflow chain is blocked by exactly one missing human START act; once the PO/ARB affirms it occurred, Governance transcribes the START (preserving on the record's face that the artifact predates the transition) and the blocked handoff chain unblocks in one move.

rows.anchor: There is an important distinction between the role model and the workflow state machine. The roles tell us who may act; the lifecycle tells us what happens and in what order.
rows.statement: A foundational distinction is drawn between the role model (who may act) and the workflow state machine (what happens and in what order), presented as two separate but related layers of the governed AI engineering lifecycle.

rows.anchor: A deliverable being produced is not the same thing as its lifecycle being closed.
rows.statement: A critical rule surfaced from the BC-7 history: a deliverable being produced (content exists) is not the same thing as its lifecycle being closed (the governed record reflects it) -- the earliest statement in this batch of the delivery/record gap pattern that recurs dozens of times in later documents.

rows.anchor: A lane cannot hand off work the record does not show it ever started. ... Governance will not manufacture the START, and will not record the bootstrap form from: null
rows.statement: Governance refuses a directed HANDOFF because the predecessor lane, though it produced a delivered artifact, was never STARTed on the record and therefore holds no mutation ownership; refuses both manufacturing a START and using a null-predecessor bootstrap form, because either would falsely assert something about the record.

rows.anchor: the START sits at seq 25, later in the log than the work it authorized. This is recorded deliberately and is not an error to be tidied ... no historical ordering is invented
rows.statement: A governance transcription convention is established: when a human act is confirmed after the fact, its transition is recorded at its true (later) sequence position, not back-dated to appear before the work it authorized -- the record states explicitly that the artifact predates the transcription.
invariants: no earlier sequence position is claimed, occupied, or altered

rows.anchor: A later act is not automatically a supersession. Act B may be an amendment superseding Act A, a re-issue that crossed with it, or a duplicate. ... Until Governance disposes, a0b61305 remains the recorded DECIDED text
rows.statement: A general governance principle: a later act arriving on an already-DECIDED slot is not automatically read as superseding it; until Governance explicitly disposes of the relationship (amendment, re-issue, or duplicate), the earlier recorded DECIDED text remains authoritative.

rows.anchor: acts and records have crossed four times -- seq-16 and seq-22 transcriptions, the seq-21 producer designation, the S4b missing START, and now two D1 acts.
rows.statement: A cumulative pattern is named explicitly: the record and the governed acts on this work item have crossed (diverged and required reconciliation) four separate times, treated as a recurring structural pattern each disposed individually by Governance rather than absorbed silently.

rows.anchor: Handing off from S5 would set S5 to HANDED_OFF, misrepresenting an OUTSTANDING verification as concluded. ... a lane with no recorded handoff can never legally START. ... Registering an assignment now would create a permanently unreachable lane.
rows.statement: Governance declines to register a new workflow lane for D5, because the current mutation owner (S5, an outstanding/refused verification) would need to hand off, which would misrepresent that verification as concluded; instead D5 proceeds as a PO/ARB-directed act, deferring the lane-creation question until S5's disposition is settled.

rows.anchor: HANDED_OFF means the lane RELEASED MUTATION OWNERSHIP. It does NOT mean the verification was performed. a lane that refused on independence now reads, in the state column, indistinguishably from lanes that finished their work.
rows.statement: A workflow-engine state-vocabulary risk is named: the HANDED_OFF state denotes only that mutation ownership was released, not that any verification, consumption, or acceptance occurred -- so a lane that refused on independence grounds becomes indistinguishable, in the raw state column, from a lane that actually finished its work, requiring explicit clarification for any later reader.

rows.anchor: Governance corrects its own repeated statement ... "no new lane can be made reachable" ... WITHDRAWN -- this was too strong. It was reachable via exactly the handoff that occurred. The accurate statement was always "not reachable without releasing S5's ownership."
rows.statement: Governance retracts its own earlier repeated claim that 'no new lane can be made reachable' while S5 held mutation ownership, correcting it to the more precise and less absolute 'not reachable without releasing S5's ownership' -- releasing ownership via handoff was mechanically always available and was not itself a defect.

lineage_claims.quote: WITHDRAWN -- this was too strong

rows.statement: RA-2: session-resolve.php computes the same runtime path as workflow-state.php's default, independently, without consulting it — a second path default the durability decision's own follow-up list does not name, meaning reconciling only one default would be insufficient.

rows.anchor: Every invariant BC-7 owns is mechanically enforced. Almost every invariant outside BC-7 is declared only.
rows.statement: A structural result from the KOS-AIP04-DISCOVERY-001 role-model discovery: the estate's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable (BC-7, the workflow engine) and weak exactly where it is prose (everywhere else); since separation itself is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2), naming more precise roles buys no additional assurance.

rows.anchor: HANDOFF ≠ ACTIVE / HUMAN START + HANDOFF = ACTIVE
rows.statement: States 'no role activates itself' as a central architectural principle: every role follows REGISTERED → (predecessor HANDOFF) → CREATED → (human START) → ACTIVE → HANDOFF/STOP/COMPLETE, with no prose or prompt able to substitute for the mechanism.
invariants: Role is resolved from the authoritative workflow assignment, not from the physical terminal, process, prompt, or conversational claim.
A terminal is an execution context; it is not an authority context.

rows.anchor: the enumerated invariant inventory ... fully support the asymmetry within the baseline's corpus (5/5 mechanical within BC-7; 6/6 declared-only outside). The phrase 'almost every' is in fact a hedge, not an over-claim.
rows.statement: Partially confirms P3-F3: re-derives the 5/5 mechanically-enforced vs 6/6 declared-only invariant counts directly from the baseline's own inventory and finds the disputed phrasing already hedged, while agreeing the corpus sampling is incomplete given P3-F1's findings.

rows.anchor: HPA framing (binding discipline...): (1) mechanism ≠ invariant — the implementation (workflow-state.php, scripts) is history; the invariant it protects ('state is reconstructable from authoritative history') is the candidate material; (2) no premature unification
rows.statement: Binding governance discipline carried from a 2026-08-22 ruling: (1) mechanism ≠ invariant -- an implementation such as workflow-state.php is treated as historical evidence, while the invariant it protects (e.g. 'state is reconstructable from authoritative history') is the candidate material; (2) no premature unification -- evidence/assessment/observation/decision/authority/workflow-state/projection/diagnostic must each be recorded with their own semantics, since similar structures do not imply the same DDD concept.

rows.anchor: ⭐ The single most consequential DDD finding in this baseline: EKS's governance — the part that carries authority, ownership, and lineage — is modelled with the least rigour of anything in EKS. Its document-assurance ... is modelled with the most. The modelling investment is inversely proportional to the invariant weight.
rows.statement: There are no domain types in EKS's governance subsystem (no WorkItem/Grant/Session/Transition class, no value object, no repository interface -- only a JSON schema-by-convention and functions over associative arrays), while the assurance subsystem (scripts/lib/EngineeringKnowledge/) is a real hexagonal tactical model with ~60 domain classes and 252 passing tests -- flagged as the single most consequential DDD finding: modelling investment is inversely proportional to invariant weight (the highest-stakes part is modelled least rigorously).

rows.anchor: (6) WORK HAPPENS ⛔ ENTIRELY OUTSIDE THE MECHANISM. Nothing observes it. Nothing gates it. Nothing links an artifact to the grant that permitted it. ... (8) COMPLETE ... ⛔ the WORK ITEM remains OPEN — forever
rows.statement: The one fully-implemented governed flow (human act -> grant registered -> lane registered -> handoff -> human START -> ACTIVE -> work -> handoff to review -> COMPLETE) has a gap at its center: step 6, 'work happens', is entirely outside the mechanism -- nothing observes it, gates it, or links an artifact to the grant that permitted it -- and even after COMPLETE, the work item itself remains OPEN forever (only the session becomes COMPLETED).

rows.anchor: 'workflow' is a label, not a definition ... init accepts --workflow=<any string>. No workflow definition registry, schema, or catalogue exists anywhere in EKS. ... 'Workflow' in EKS is a naming convention, not a process model.
rows.statement: The `workflow` field carries no machine meaning: `init` accepts any string, no workflow-definition registry/schema/catalogue exists, and 14 distinct values appear across 18 records (5 sharing 'architecture-decision', 13 used exactly once); every work item is procedurally identical -- only its declared roles[] differ -- so 'workflow' in EKS is a naming convention, not a process model.

rows.anchor: Where authority is actually enforced ... Nowhere against engineering work. In exactly four places against the record itself ... EKS enforces the well-formedness of its own record. It enforces nothing about engineering.
rows.statement: Authority is enforced nowhere against engineering work; in exactly four places against the record itself: (1) only governance may write a grant; (2) a grant must carry a humanActRef; (3) only the current mutation owner may hand off; (4) only governance/human may record COMPLETE or CONTINUATION. Each is a precondition on a write to the JSON file, evaluated by a CLI the actor chose to run, with the writer role supplied as a command-line flag. 'EKS enforces the well-formedness of its own record. It enforces nothing about engineering' -- no file edit, commit, push, merge, deploy, document creation, or architectural change is gated by any grant, ownership, or transition.

rows.anchor: Executable vs documented-only governance ... Registry-first workflow | 🔴 documented only ... ES-001…ES-006 (all clauses) | 🔴 documented only, and PROPOSED ... The smallest automation set justified by evidence: ZERO new hooks.
rows.statement: Executable-vs-documented governance table: nine core workflow-record disciplines plus read-purity/one-interpreter rules plus the closed verdict vocabulary are executable and tested (29+17+252 tests respectively); knowledge-schema conformance/placement/identifier-collision/reference-integrity are executable but only advisory or non-blocking; but the registry-first workflow, ES-001..006 in full, the promotion ladder, the 14-phase Operating Loop, EP-01/02/03, the six-role operating model, and work-item acceptance/closure are ALL documented-only. EKS's own STANDARDS_INDEX.md states 'the smallest automation set justified by evidence: ZERO new hooks' -- recorded here as a deliberate decision, not a defect, while noting the enforcement-scope consequence follows from it inescapably.

rows.anchor: V-3 (AST-016, ARCHITECTURE/SPECIFICATION GAP, unresolved) ... fails safe (over-reports 'not ready'). ... KOS_MECHANISM_PATH: an environment variable that substitutes the workflow interpreter at runtime. ... 'It is NOT a hardened boundary and must not be described as one'
rows.statement: Two open governance findings carried in the registry: V-3 (AST-016) -- workflow-state.php gates START on a predecessor-handoff fact but exposes it through no read command, so a delegating consumer cannot distinguish a recorded handoff from an absent one (fails safe, over-reports 'not ready'; must be resolved before AST-016 is wired into SESSION_START); and KOS_MECHANISM_PATH, an environment variable substituting the workflow interpreter at runtime, explicitly documented as 'NOT a hardened boundary' -- the resolver reports which interpreter answered but performs no legitimacy assessment, registry comparison, warning, or refusal on that basis.

rows.anchor: 23 / 30 concurrent-append trials silently lost a transition
rows.statement: Erratum E-1: the prior claim that dense/monotonic seq numbers make omission mechanically detectable is WITHDRAWN. MIGRATION-PLAN SS1.3 AMD3 CL-1 reproduced concurrent-append trials: 23/30 silently lost a transition (the losing process exited 0 reporting {ok:true,seq:2}) while every survivor stayed dense and monotonic (the clobbering writer reuses the lost writer's sequence number); the write is atomic per write (tmp+rename) but the read-modify-write is NOT atomic (no lock, lease, CAS or version check). Corrects P3 SS8.1.

experiment.hypothesis: dense, monotonic seq numbers prove completeness of the append log
experiment.setup: concurrent-append trials against workflow-state.php's read-modify-write append path
experiment.assumptions: atomic per-write (tmp+rename) was believed to imply atomic read-modify-write
experiment.method: reproduced concurrent appends and inspected resulting seq sequences (per MIGRATION-PLAN SS1.3 AMD3 CL-1)
experiment.result: 23 of 30 trials silently lost a transition while every survivor was dense and monotonic
experiment.interpretation: density/monotonicity of seq is NOT a completeness proof; read-modify-write lacks locking/CAS/versioning
experiment.limitations: reported second-hand via the MIGRATION-PLAN, not independently re-run in this document
experiment.conclusion: the current persistence mechanism does not provide completeness merely from dense sequence numbers

rows.anchor: States: REGISTER . HANDOFF . START . CONTINUATION . STOP . COMPLETE . FAIL . CANCEL
rows.statement: AST-015 workflow lifecycle states: REGISTER, HANDOFF, START, CONTINUATION, STOP, COMPLETE, FAIL, CANCEL.

rows.anchor: Mechanically enforced invariants ... all contract-pinned by tests
rows.statement: Mechanically enforced (contract-pinned by tests): I-1 exactly one mutation owner; I-2 HANDOFF and human START (neither alone yields ACTIVE); I-3 STOPPED is sticky (only CONTINUATION exits); G-1 closure is a governance act (COMPLETE refuses non-governance writers); G-2 Authority State has exactly one writer (grant writer rule R5a/R5b).

rows.anchor: Every invariant BC-7 (the workflow engine) owns is mechanically enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is declared only
rows.statement: Headline structural finding -- the invariant asymmetry: assurance is strong where it is executable (BC-7) and weak where it is prose (outside BC-7). 'The platform mechanically protects orchestration, and protects knowledge/verification/communication only by declaration.' Stated as the single most important structural property of AIP's current architecture.

rows.anchor: Core workflows ... Integrations
rows.statement: Four core workflows: registry-first construction (register->approve->implement->verify); governed lane workflow (REGISTER->...->COMPLETE/FAIL/CANCEL with mutation-owner/START-stickiness invariants); the operating loop (Business capability -> ... -> KnowledgeOS promotion check); construction discipline (one objective, one approved plan, one completion review, one stopping point). Integrations: hooks wired via settings.json at five runtime moments; tests pin the workflow-engine contracts; persistence = runtime workflow records + session logs + docs/ governed artifacts; the registry is consumed at START/ON_DEMAND, human docs generated from it never the reverse; drafting studio consumes frozen templates by reference (no parallel copies).

rows.anchor: FINDING F1 — self-continuation vs the engine's CONTINUATION gate ... Case 4's YES/NO is correct only when the session is already ACTIVE under an existing authorization
rows.statement: Records F1: the protocol's self-continuation field can be misread as authorizing a START or exit from STOPPED unless scoped explicitly to an already-ACTIVE session under existing authorization; recommends an added clarifying sentence for the adopted protocol (later applied as v1.1 amendment).

rows.anchor: This protocol consumes workflow information. It does NOT replace — and does NOT add to — the workflow engine. | The protocol answers 'Who should act?' | The workflow engine decides 'Who is allowed to act?'
rows.statement: Formalizes the boundary between the protocol and the workflow engine: the protocol consumes Current State and active-grant context, authors none of it, and never passes ownership (ownership passes only on START per G-3).

rows.anchor: a subagent spawned from a parent session reports the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (distinct OS PID only) -- so a subagent is the parent session and fails the independence bar.
rows.statement: Records an empirical probe finding (AST-018 candidate-declaration precedent, 2026-08-22): a subagent spawned from a parent session reports the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so a subagent is indistinguishable from its parent for independence purposes and therefore always fails an independence bar -- a fresh reviewer must be a genuinely new top-level session started by the PO/ARB, never a subagent.

rows.anchor: IMPLEMENTED != VERIFIED != ADOPTED != AUTHORIZED (§38) -- this review establishes readiness for the fourth-to-third transition and leaves ADOPTED and AUTHORIZED untouched.
rows.statement: Confirms and applies the four-state lifecycle model (IMPLEMENTED, VERIFIED, ADOPTED, AUTHORIZED as four distinct, non-collapsible states, §38) as load-bearing governance vocabulary: a PASS review moves work from VERIFIED toward being ready for the ADOPTED decision, but does not itself adopt or authorize, and the adoption decision belongs solely to the PO/ARB.

rows.anchor: F-2 | Decision required (scope boundary) | The work item now carries a fourth asset -- AST-019/ActivateCommissionedFreshSession -- that is IMPLEMENTED ... but NOT VERIFIED (producer bar) and outside the verification report ... The adoption decision must name its scope explicitly.
rows.statement: Finds that an additional asset (AST-019) landed on the same work item after the original three-layer verification was completed, and warns that adopting 'the work item' without explicitly excluding this unverified fourth asset would silently sweep an unverified capability into adoption -- the adoption decision must name its scope explicitly.

rows.statement: Identifies a governance-model gap: because AST-019's implementing session never registered a lane or recorded its runtime identity, the producer-verifier separation principle cannot be mechanically enforced for its future verification (no producer identity exists to exclude), and the operating model as written has no lane-shape at all for a human-authorized amendment slice landing on a STOPPED work item.

rows.anchor: F-4 ... every lane on this work item ... was created by hand-composed AST-015 append calls in governance-recording capacity, not through appoint ... appoint auto-generates a thin executionContext ... and cannot carry the disclosure depth the estate's own precedent requires
rows.statement: Observes that in practice every lane transition on this work item was created by hand-composed governance-recording rather than the documented `appoint` mechanism, because `appoint` cannot yet carry the disclosure depth (enumerated bars, prior participation, exposure, preservation conditions, non-actions) the estate's own precedent requires -- meaning the operating model's documented §8 path is not the path actually taken, pending either a disclosure passthrough for `appoint` or sanctioning hand-composition as the disclosure-heavy path.

rows.anchor: F-6 ... The §29 CASE 6 presentation ... is unreachable from the record when the review lane closes with STOP ... manufacturing a CONTINUATION to make the tooling render more nicely is self-directed workflow manipulation with no human direction behind it.
rows.statement: Finds a structural gap where the workflow engine's own 'ready for adoption' presentation (CASE 6) can only render from a COMPLETED lane, never from one closed via STOP -- yet the declared review sequence and every precedent prescribe closing review lanes with STOP -- and explicitly refuses to repair this by manufacturing an unauthorized CONTINUATION merely to make the tooling render more nicely, naming that as self-directed workflow manipulation with no human direction behind it.

rows.anchor: The human speaks BUSINESS LANGUAGE. The system handles TECHNICAL WORKFLOW MECHANICS. The human never operates the workflow engine.
rows.statement: States the operating model's one-line core principle, operationalized across all 40 sections: the human speaks business language and makes business/authority decisions; the system (Governance/Communication capabilities via the canonical workflow mechanism) performs all mechanical consequences; the human is never required to understand workflow UUIDs, REGISTER/HANDOFF/START, mutationOwner, predecessor, transition JSON, or internal resolver codes.

The Communication Engineer is NOT a permanent person -- it is a transferable operational responsibility.
rows.statement: Defines the Governance Engineer (dedicated human-facing responsibility for intake, classification, substantive governance decisions, escalation, and adoption presentation) and the Communication Engineer (a transferable operational responsibility any authorized actor may perform for routine coordination, but never for substantive governance decisions) as responsibilities rather than new workflow roles, services, or positions -- citing the six-role operating model adopted 2026-08-19 as the source of this non-equivalence rule.

rows.anchor: CONTINUE / PERMISSION_REQUIRED / FRESH_SESSION_REQUIRED / GOVERNANCE_DECISION_REQUIRED / STOP ... a business rendering of the existing governed/application result model -- never a second workflow-state vocabulary, never a new state machine.
rows.statement: Defines the five business-level session-completion outcomes (CONTINUE, PERMISSION_REQUIRED, FRESH_SESSION_REQUIRED, GOVERNANCE_DECISION_REQUIRED, STOP), explicitly constrained to be a business-language rendering of the existing governed/application result model rather than a new second workflow-state vocabulary or state machine.

rows.anchor: MATCH -> ACTOR_MATCH -> 'This is the assigned session. You may continue.' MISMATCH -> ACTOR_MISMATCH -> 'This is not the session assigned to this work.' ... Do not: create another appointment, replace the appointed actor, impersonate the appointed actor, self-register, or treat the mismatch as authorization.
rows.statement: Defines the fresh-session-with-existing-appointment protocol: compare expected actor to current runtime identity yielding MATCH ('you may continue') or MISMATCH ('not the assigned session' with recovery options), and explicitly forbids five self-serving responses to a mismatch (creating another appointment, replacing the appointed actor, impersonating it, self-registering, or treating the mismatch itself as authorization).

rows.anchor: Provide a session UUID, choose runtime process identity, determine mutationOwner, determine predecessor, construct REGISTER, construct HANDOFF, construct START, edit workflow JSON, invoke workflow-state.php, inspect workflow records to route the work, diagnose INV-B, diagnose G-3, understand token/tokenRef, manually calculate authorization. If the human is forced to do any of these ... the implementation has failed the human-facing contract.
rows.statement: Enumerates 14 hard acceptance criteria the human must never be forced to perform (session UUIDs, mutationOwner/predecessor, constructing REGISTER/HANDOFF/START, editing workflow JSON, diagnosing invariants, understanding tokenRef, manually calculating authorization), declaring the implementation failed if any occur in a normal workflow.

rows.statement: Defines the boundaries of the three existing mechanisms this operating model is layered over without replacing: AST-015 (single workflow authority, no parallel store), AST-017 (read-only, on-demand governed-state resolution, never creates assignments or fabricates authority), and AST-018 (next-actor orchestration answering 'what should happen next', explicitly forbidden from becoming a second workflow engine, identity authority, adoption authority, or migration engine).

rows.statement: Records a new finding F-8: the mechanical workflow engine has no vocabulary at all for ADOPTED or AUTHORIZED -- both concepts exist only in governance documents, so no mechanism query can answer whether an artifact is authorized; explicitly deferred as a future-increment observation rather than repaired opportunistically, since inventing a new state would breach the no-scope-expansion and AST-015-boundary rules.

Its main write path is exercised only by its own test suite. Establishing whether that path is trustworthy is the substance of this verification.

rows.anchor: Using an unverified capability to manufacture the authority to verify that capability makes the verification worthless. A PASS would rest on the subject's own correctness -- the thing in question.
rows.statement: States the circularity bar as a general governance principle: a candidate must never use the very capability it is appointed to verify (or any unauthorized capability) to manufacture its own activation, because doing so would make the eventual verification verdict rest on the subject's own unproven correctness -- self-identified independently by the candidate before any instruction forbade it.

rows.statement: The PO/ARB accepts the candidate's ordering deviation as non-disqualifying for this appointment only, explicitly distinguishing a one-off disposition from a general policy ruling and leaving the REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_POLICY placeholder unresolved -- a concrete application of ES-006.1's 'no promotion from one occurrence' discipline.

rows.statement: Rejects a proposed pair of new capabilities (ResolveCandidateDeclaration, ActivateDeclaredActor) by demonstrating both already exist as AST-019's check/activate operations realizing a domain concept already named in the registry (BindRuntimeToRequestedResponsibility) -- concluding the apparent 'dead end' was not a missing concept but an unverified one, so the remedy is verification, not invention, applying ES-005.4's canonical-discovery-before-creation rule.

rows.anchor: AST-018 appoint ... does not merely write the same transitions -- it records the eligibility check as a governed act ... A hand-composed AST-015 append reproduces the transitions but not the recorded eligibility check, and it silently falsifies the assumption on which AST-018's own independence guard rests.
rows.statement: Discovers a subtle defect class: reproducing a governed mechanism's output transitions by hand (rather than invoking the mechanism itself) can be formally valid at the transition-log level while silently skipping the substantive check the mechanism exists to perform, and can falsify the assumptions later guards built on that mechanism rely on -- distinguishing 'the transitions are valid' from 'the mechanism was actually exercised.'

What IS defective is exactly one thing: the appointment's provenance. The eligibility facts were established ... but were never recorded by the mechanism whose job that is.
rows.statement: Sharply distinguishes a mechanism's refusal-on-lane-existence (a re-appointment guard, correctly firing here) from a substantive finding about independence (which was never actually violated), locating the true defect as a provenance gap: real eligibility facts existed but were never recorded by the specific mechanism responsible for recording them.

rows.anchor: analyze() never returns a 'fold' key, and writeActivation() reads $a['fold'] (line 401). The mutation owner is therefore forced to null on every activation. ... leaves a permanent orphan assignment -- after its own read-only check reported READY.
rows.statement: Verdict FAIL for AST-019: a single missing array key (analyze() omits 'fold') forces the write path's mutationOwner to always be null; on the one reachable production scenario where the real owner is non-null, this produces a factually wrong predecessor, gets refused by AST-015's HANDOFF guard, and leaves a permanent orphan REGISTER transition in the append-only store -- occurring even though the capability's own read-only 'check' sibling had reported READY just before.

experiment.hypothesis: AST-019's production write path correctly derives mutationOwner/predecessor/from from the current workflow fold in every reachable state, including when a prior lane already owns the item
experiment.setup: build four hermetic workflow stores through AST-015 only, including one deliberately driven into the state where a non-null mutationOwner coexists with a NEXT_ACTOR_REQUIRED commission (lane AAA COMPLETED, lane BBB STARTed then FAILed, which does not clear the owner)
experiment.inputs: four hermetic AST-015-only stores (fresh item; COMPLETED predecessor with null owner; COMPLETED+FAILed with live owner; failure-injection variants)
experiment.method: independently re-run GO-01..GO-25 and the full WorkflowEngine regression, then directly invoke AST-019's activate command against each hermetic store and read back the authoritative fold
experiment.result: the null-owner cases activate correctly; the live-owner case: check reports READY, activate returns INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE with a PHP undefined-array-key warning, and leaves an orphan REGISTER with predecessor recorded as null
experiment.interpretation: analyze() never populates a 'fold' key that writeActivation() depends on, so $owner is unconditionally null regardless of the true fold state
experiment.limitations: the defect was reachable but had never yet been armed in any of the 23 real production workflow records at time of writing
experiment.conclusion: VERIFICATION COMPLETED WITH RESULT FAIL; AST-019 remains NOT ADOPTED / NOT AUTHORIZED

rows.anchor: GO-01 ... GO-25 all pass (25 tests / 270 assertions), and they cannot detect this -- no contract test reaches the write path with a non-null mutationOwner (§12, O-1). This is the commission's own warning made concrete: reported numbers are not evidence.
rows.statement: Explains precisely why a 25/25-passing, 270-assertion-green contract suite structurally cannot detect the blocking defect: every existing test case happens to exercise the write path only in states where the buggy forced-null value happens to coincide with the true value (empty item, or a COMPLETED predecessor which legitimately clears the owner), while every genuinely non-null-owner scenario is refused earlier by an unrelated guard (GO-13) -- a general lesson that 100% green does not imply coverage of the actual failure surface.

rows.statement: Independently connects the ASD-001 governance-process defect (S0387, a human process bypassing the appointment engine and hand-deriving ownership) with the AST-019 code defect F-1 (the code attempting to derive ownership and silently failing) as the same underlying defect class approached from two directions -- both instances of getting ownership provenance wrong -- treating this convergence as corroboration rather than coincidence.

rationale_evidence.anchor: X-2 is a live blocker ... the work item's mutationOwner is None: seq 14 handed off to a lane that then never STARTed, so ownership was released and never taken up. Consequently no lane can hand off
rationale_evidence.statement: A workflow lane that is HANDED_OFF to but never STARTed leaves mutationOwner as None, mechanically blocking every subsequent lane's handoff (Inv C requires the current mutation owner to hand off) -- a live, measured blocker rather than a theoretical one, confirmed by probing a scratch copy of the record.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The record is not broken. It is exactly ONE HUMAN ACT short.
rationale_evidence.statement: Diagnosis: the entire workflow chain is blocked by exactly one missing human START act; once the PO/ARB affirms it occurred, Governance transcribes the START (preserving on the record's face that the artifact predates the transition) and the blocked handoff chain unblocks in one move.

rationale_evidence.anchor: acts and records have crossed four times -- seq-16 and seq-22 transcriptions, the seq-21 producer designation, the S4b missing START, and now two D1 acts.
rationale_evidence.statement: A cumulative pattern is named explicitly: the record and the governed acts on this work item have crossed (diverged and required reconciliation) four separate times, treated as a recurring structural pattern each disposed individually by Governance rather than absorbed silently.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Handing off from S5 would set S5 to HANDED_OFF, misrepresenting an OUTSTANDING verification as concluded. ... a lane with no recorded handoff can never legally START. ... Registering an assignment now would create a permanently unreachable lane.
rationale_evidence.statement: Governance declines to register a new workflow lane for D5, because the current mutation owner (S5, an outstanding/refused verification) would need to hand off, which would misrepresent that verification as concluded; instead D5 proceeds as a PO/ARB-directed act, deferring the lane-creation question until S5's disposition is settled.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Every invariant BC-7 owns is mechanically enforced. Almost every invariant outside BC-7 is declared only.
rationale_evidence.statement: A structural result from the KOS-AIP04-DISCOVERY-001 role-model discovery: the estate's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable (BC-7, the workflow engine) and weak exactly where it is prose (everywhere else); since separation itself is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2), naming more precise roles buys no additional assurance.

rationale_evidence.anchor: the enumerated invariant inventory ... fully support the asymmetry within the baseline's corpus (5/5 mechanical within BC-7; 6/6 declared-only outside). The phrase 'almost every' is in fact a hedge, not an over-claim.
rationale_evidence.statement: Partially confirms P3-F3: re-derives the 5/5 mechanically-enforced vs 6/6 declared-only invariant counts directly from the baseline's own inventory and finds the disputed phrasing already hedged, while agreeing the corpus sampling is incomplete given P3-F1's findings.

rationale_evidence.anchor: ⭐ The single most consequential DDD finding in this baseline: EKS's governance — the part that carries authority, ownership, and lineage — is modelled with the least rigour of anything in EKS. Its document-assurance ... is modelled with the most. The modelling investment is inversely proportional to the invariant weight.
rationale_evidence.statement: There are no domain types in EKS's governance subsystem (no WorkItem/Grant/Session/Transition class, no value object, no repository interface -- only a JSON schema-by-convention and functions over associative arrays), while the assurance subsystem (scripts/lib/EngineeringKnowledge/) is a real hexagonal tactical model with ~60 domain classes and 252 passing tests -- flagged as the single most consequential DDD finding: modelling investment is inversely proportional to invariant weight (the highest-stakes part is modelled least rigorously).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Where authority is actually enforced ... Nowhere against engineering work. In exactly four places against the record itself ... EKS enforces the well-formedness of its own record. It enforces nothing about engineering.
rationale_evidence.statement: Authority is enforced nowhere against engineering work; in exactly four places against the record itself: (1) only governance may write a grant; (2) a grant must carry a humanActRef; (3) only the current mutation owner may hand off; (4) only governance/human may record COMPLETE or CONTINUATION. Each is a precondition on a write to the JSON file, evaluated by a CLI the actor chose to run, with the writer role supplied as a command-line flag. 'EKS enforces the well-formedness of its own record. It enforces nothing about engineering' -- no file edit, commit, push, merge, deploy, document creation, or architectural change is gated by any grant, ownership, or transition.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Executable vs documented-only governance ... Registry-first workflow | 🔴 documented only ... ES-001…ES-006 (all clauses) | 🔴 documented only, and PROPOSED ... The smallest automation set justified by evidence: ZERO new hooks.
rationale_evidence.statement: Executable-vs-documented governance table: nine core workflow-record disciplines plus read-purity/one-interpreter rules plus the closed verdict vocabulary are executable and tested (29+17+252 tests respectively); knowledge-schema conformance/placement/identifier-collision/reference-integrity are executable but only advisory or non-blocking; but the registry-first workflow, ES-001..006 in full, the promotion ladder, the 14-phase Operating Loop, EP-01/02/03, the six-role operating model, and work-item acceptance/closure are ALL documented-only. EKS's own STANDARDS_INDEX.md states 'the smallest automation set justified by evidence: ZERO new hooks' -- recorded here as a deliberate decision, not a defect, while noting the enforcement-scope consequence follows from it inescapably.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Every invariant BC-7 (the workflow engine) owns is mechanically enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is declared only
rationale_evidence.statement: Headline structural finding -- the invariant asymmetry: assurance is strong where it is executable (BC-7) and weak where it is prose (outside BC-7). 'The platform mechanically protects orchestration, and protects knowledge/verification/communication only by declaration.' Stated as the single most important structural property of AIP's current architecture.

rationale_evidence.anchor: the refusal is CORRECT as a re-appointment guard, and it is NOT a finding that 84c0f6f6 lacks independence. Conflating the two would be the real error. ... What IS defective is exactly one thing: the appointment's provenance. The eligibility facts were established ... but were never recorded by the mechanism whose job that is.
rationale_evidence.statement: Sharply distinguishes a mechanism's refusal-on-lane-existence (a re-appointment guard, correctly firing here) from a substantive finding about independence (which was never actually violated), locating the true defect as a provenance gap: real eligibility facts existed but were never recorded by the specific mechanism responsible for recording them.

sources.note: Step 101: pivots from architectural theory to empirical conformance measurement. Three-architectures distinction (intended/implemented/runtime), five-state conformance vocabulary with mandatory evidence, multidimensional conformance vectors (rejecting single-score evaluation), architecture archaeology and dependency-graph drift detection, a bidirectional requirement<->runtime evidence graph, the Traceability!=Correctness distinction, mismatch-diagnosis discipline (implementation-wrong vs architecture-obsolete vs both-incomplete) forbidding documentation laundering, bounded recursive self-analysis, and a queryable machine-readable self-architecture-model. Conceptual forerunner of the actual EP-01 EKS+PKS+AIP landscape study.

rows.anchor: We now change mode. The first 100 steps established the architectural theory and closure. Step 101 begins the empirical phase: Intended Architecture -> Implemented Architecture -> Running Architecture. The central question is no longer 'is this architecture conceptually sound' but 'does our actual K
rows.statement: Announces Step 101's mode shift from architectural theory (Steps 1-100) to the empirical conformance question: does the actual system implement the defined architecture.

lineage_claims.quote: The first 100 steps established the architectural theory and closure.

rows.anchor: 101.1 — Three architectures ... A. Intended architecture A_I. B. Implemented architecture A_C. C. Runtime architecture A_R(t). A_I =? A_C =? A_R(t).
rows.statement: Defines the three-architectures distinction: A_I (intended, per docs/ADRs/principles/governance), A_C (implemented, per actual repositories/config/code), A_R(t) (runtime, actually deployed/behaving), and the conformance question A_I =? A_C =? A_R(t).

rows.anchor: 101.2 — Why this matters ... a common architecture failure looks like A_I≠A_C while everybody assumes A_I=A_C. An even more dangerous situation: A_I=A_C but A_C≠A_R. The documentation is correct. The code is correct. The deployment is not.
rows.statement: Warns of two failure patterns: assuming A_I=A_C when A_I≠A_C, and the more dangerous A_I=A_C but A_C≠A_R (correct docs, correct code, incorrect deployment).

rows.anchor: 101.3 — Experiment 1: documented component missing ... Architecture declares EvidenceService. Repository contains no implementation. Expected classification: SpecifiedButMissing. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 1: a declared-but-unimplemented EvidenceService is classified SpecifiedButMissing; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.4 — Experiment 2: undocumented component exists ... Repository contains LegacyKnowledgeImporter. Architecture does not mention it. Expected: ImplementedButUndocumented. This is architecture drift. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 2: an undocumented existing component (LegacyKnowledgeImporter) is ImplementedButUndocumented — architecture drift; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.5 — Experiment 3: wrong implementation ... Architecture requires PolicyEngine to enforce AuthorizationInvariant. Code contains a policy engine, but authorization is bypassable. Expected: ImplementedIncorrectly. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 3: a policy engine that exists but leaves authorization bypassable is ImplementedIncorrectly; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.6 — Experiment 4: partially implemented concept ... Architecture defines Evidence with provenance, source, timestamp, confidence, classification. Implementation contains only source. Expected: PartiallyImplemented. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 4: an Evidence implementation retaining only 'source' of five required fields is PartiallyImplemented; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.7 — Five-state conformance vocabulary ... Implemented, PartiallyImplemented, SpecifiedButMissing, ImplementedIncorrectly, NotYetVerified. Much more useful than simply saying 'the architecture is implemented.'
rows.statement: Defines the five-state conformance vocabulary (Implemented, PartiallyImplemented, SpecifiedButMissing, ImplementedIncorrectly, NotYetVerified), far more useful than a bare 'implemented' claim.

rows.anchor: 101.8 — But we need evidence ... Every classification should have Evidence. ConformanceFinding=(Requirement,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Status).
rows.statement: Defines ConformanceFinding=(Requirement,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Status), requiring every conformance classification to carry supporting evidence.

type_signature.domain: Requirement x Expected x Observed x Evidence

rows.anchor: 101.9 — Experiment 5 ... Reviewer says 'the evidence model is implemented.' No repository location, code reference, schema or test is provided. Expected: NotYetVerified. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 5: an unsupported reviewer claim (no repo location/code reference/schema/test) must be classified NotYetVerified; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.10 — Architecture claims become evidence-backed claims ... 'Evidence service exists' becomes Claim: EvidenceCapabilityImplemented supported by RepositoryEvidence+SchemaEvidence+TestEvidence.
rows.statement: Reframes architecture claims as evidence-backed claims (RepositoryEvidence+SchemaEvidence+TestEvidence) rather than bare assertions.

rows.anchor: 101.11 — Architecture requirement traceability ... Requirement→ArchitectureRule→Component→Code→Test→RuntimeEvidence. This becomes our central conformance chain.
rows.statement: Defines the central conformance chain Requirement→ArchitectureRule→Component→Code→Test→RuntimeEvidence.

rows.anchor: 101.12 — Experiment 6 ... Requirement exists. Architecture rule exists. Implementation exists. No test exists. Expected: ImplementedButUnverified. Not Assured. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 6: an implemented but untested capability is ImplementedButUnverified, not Assured; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.13 — Conformance is multidimensional ... A component can be Implemented=True but Verified=False. Similarly Implemented=True but GovernanceCompliant=False. Therefore a single status is insufficient.
rows.statement: States a single conformance status is insufficient: Implemented=True can coexist with Verified=False or GovernanceCompliant=False.

rows.anchor: 101.14 — Conformance vector ... C(x)=(Implementation,Semantic,Security,Privacy,Governance,Verification,Runtime). Each dimension may have its own status.
rows.statement: Defines a seven-dimension conformance vector C(x)=(Implementation,Semantic,Security,Privacy,Governance,Verification,Runtime), each with independent status.

rows.anchor: 101.15 — Experiment 7 ... Component AgentRegistry. Implementation=PASS, Semantic=PASS, Security=PASS, Privacy=UNKNOWN, Runtime=UNKNOWN. Expected: overall result cannot simply be 100% Correct. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 7: mixed per-dimension statuses (some PASS, some UNKNOWN) for AgentRegistry mean the overall result cannot simply be 100% Correct; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.16 — This changes how we evaluate KnowledgeOS ... We should not produce one simplistic score such as Architecture=87%. Instead, we need a conformance matrix.
rows.statement: Rejects single-score architecture evaluation (e.g. Architecture=87%) in favor of a conformance matrix.

rows.anchor: 101.17 — Architecture Conformance Matrix ... Knowledge registry, Evidence model, Provenance, Governance, Agent control, Policy enforcement, AI context boundary, Runtime assurance, Evolution control -- each with Specification/Implementation/Verification/Runtime/Status columns, many marked TBD/?. The
rows.statement: Presents a sample Architecture Conformance Matrix (nine capabilities x Specification/Implementation/Verification/Runtime/Status), with unresolved '?' cells explicitly framed as an acceptable engineering state ('we don't know yet').

rows.anchor: 101.18 — Architecture archaeology ... examine Repositories, DirectoryStructure, SourceCode, Configuration, DatabaseSchemas, CI/CD, AgentHarnesses, Hooks, RuntimeArtifacts, Documentation. Then reconstruct A_C.
rows.statement: Defines 'architecture archaeology': reconstructing A_C from repositories, directory structure, source code, config, schemas, CI/CD, agent harnesses, hooks, runtime artifacts, documentation.

rows.anchor: 101.19 — The repository becomes architectural evidence ... a domain/application/infrastructure/governance/agents/evidence/verification folder structure suggests one architecture; controllers/services/utils/misc suggests something very different. But naming alone is not proof.
rows.statement: Notes directory structure suggests architectural intent but naming alone is not proof of actual conformance.

rows.anchor: 101.20 — Experiment 8 ... Directory is named domain/ but contains database-specific code and HTTP controllers. Expected: the folder name does not prove domain separation. Result: PASS. This is particularly relevant to our DDD work.
rows.statement: Experiment 8: a domain/ folder containing database-specific code and HTTP controllers shows folder naming does not prove domain separation — explicitly relevant to the project's own DDD work; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.21 — Architecture must be inferred from dependencies ... examine DependencyGraph. For each component C_i→C_j. Then compare the actual graph against the allowed architecture graph.
rows.statement: Proposes inferring actual architecture from the code dependency graph, compared against the allowed architecture graph.

rows.anchor: 101.22 — Experiment 9 ... Architecture requires Domain ↛ Infrastructure. Code contains Domain→InfrastructureDatabase. Expected: architectural dependency violation. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 9: a Domain→InfrastructureDatabase dependency violating the required Domain ↛ Infrastructure rule is an architectural dependency violation; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.23 — Architecture constraints become graph properties ... ForbiddenEdge(D,I)=True. Automated analysis can search E_runtime/code ∩ E_forbidden. If ≠∅, we have drift.
rows.statement: Formalizes architecture constraints as graph properties: ForbiddenEdge(D,I)=True detectable via E_runtime/code ∩ E_forbidden ≠ ∅.

type_signature.domain: actual edge set E, forbidden edge set

rows.anchor: 101.24 — Experiment 10 ... Allowed graph: Application→Domain. Actual graph: Application→Domain and Application→Database. If direct database access is forbidden, Violation=True. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 10: an extra Application→Database edge beyond the allowed Application→Domain graph is Violation=True if direct DB access is forbidden; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.25 — This is where architecture becomes executable ... 'Infrastructure must remain behind the application boundary' becomes a DependencyRule. Code→StaticAnalysis→ConformanceEvidence. This is precisely the type of mechanism KnowledgeOS should manage.
rows.statement: States a natural-language architecture rule can become an executable DependencyRule via Code→StaticAnalysis→ConformanceEvidence, exactly the mechanism KnowledgeOS should manage.

rows.anchor: 101.26 — Step 101 is therefore not about adding more abstractions ... We have enough architectural concepts. Now we need Evidence of implementation. The next work should become increasingly repository-specific.
rows.statement: States Step 101 marks a shift from adding architectural abstractions to gathering Evidence of implementation, becoming increasingly repository-specific.

rows.anchor: 101.27 — The first empirical question ... For every major KnowledgeOS capability: where exactly is this implemented? Not 'we intended to,' not 'Claude understands it,' not 'the architecture document describes it,' but where is the executable implementation?
rows.statement: States the first empirical question for every capability: 'where is the executable implementation?' — rejecting intention, AI understanding, or documentation as substitutes.

rows.anchor: 101.28 — The second question ... For every implementation: what architectural requirement does it satisfy? Implementation→Requirement. If there is no requirement: OrphanImplementation.
rows.statement: Defines the second empirical question (Implementation→Requirement), with no matching requirement yielding OrphanImplementation.

rows.anchor: 101.29 — Experiment 11 ... Repository contains a sophisticated KnowledgeIndexer. No architecture requirement references it. Expected: potential architectural orphan. Result: PASS. It may be useful, but we need to understand its architectural role.
rows.statement: Experiment 11: a sophisticated but requirement-unreferenced KnowledgeIndexer is a potential architectural orphan needing role clarification; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.30 — The third question ... For every requirement: where is the implementation? Requirement→Implementation. If none exists: ArchitectureGap.
rows.statement: Defines the third empirical question (Requirement→Implementation), with no implementation yielding ArchitectureGap.

rows.anchor: 101.31 — Experiment 12 ... 'Every AI action must be attributable.' No agent identity mechanism exists. Expected: SpecifiedButMissing. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 12: an AI-attributability requirement with no agent identity mechanism is SpecifiedButMissing; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.32 — The fourth question ... For every implementation: how do we know it works? Implementation→Verification. No verification: AssuranceGap.
rows.statement: Defines the fourth empirical question (Implementation→Verification), with none yielding AssuranceGap.

rows.anchor: 101.33 — The fifth question ... For every verified component: does production actually use it? Verification→Deployment→Runtime. This is where many architectures fail.
rows.statement: Defines the fifth empirical question (Verification→Deployment→Runtime), noting this is where many architectures fail in practice.

rows.anchor: 101.34 — Experiment 13 ... Policy engine is thoroughly tested. Production configuration bypasses it. Expected: VerifiedImplementation ≠ VerifiedRuntimeArchitecture. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 13: a thoroughly tested policy engine bypassed by production config shows VerifiedImplementation ≠ VerifiedRuntimeArchitecture; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.35 — The conformance chain ... Requirement→Architecture→Implementation→Verification→Deployment→Runtime→Observation. And backwards: Observation→Evidence→Implementation→Architecture→Requirement.
rows.statement: States the bidirectional conformance chain forward (Requirement→...→Observation) and backward (Observation→Evidence→Implementation→Architecture→Requirement).

rows.anchor: 101.36 — Architecture evidence graph ... G=(V,E) where nodes include Requirement, Principle, ADR, Component, CodeArtifact, Test, Deployment, RuntimeObservation. Edges: implements, verifies, dependsOn, deployedAs, observedBy.
rows.statement: Defines the architecture evidence graph G=(V,E) with typed nodes (Requirement/Principle/ADR/Component/CodeArtifact/Test/Deployment/RuntimeObservation) and typed edges (implements/verifies/dependsOn/deployedAs/observedBy).

rows.anchor: 101.37 — Experiment 14 ... One architecture rule has NoImplementationEdge. Expected: architecture gap. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 14: an architecture rule with NoImplementationEdge is an architecture gap; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.38 — Experiment 15 ... One implementation has NoRequirementEdge. Expected: potential orphan capability. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 15: an implementation with NoRequirementEdge is a potential orphan capability; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.39 — Experiment 16 ... One production runtime component has NoArchitectureEdge. Expected: unknown architectural component. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 16: a runtime component with NoArchitectureEdge is an unknown architectural component; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.40 — This gives us a measurable architecture ... we can eventually calculate Coverage_Requirement, Coverage_Implementation, Coverage_Verification, Coverage_Runtime, Coverage_Evidence.
rows.statement: Proposes calculable coverage metrics (Coverage_Requirement, Coverage_Implementation, Coverage_Verification, Coverage_Runtime, Coverage_Evidence) instead of a subjective 'architecture looks good'.

rows.anchor: 101.41 — But coverage is not correctness ... Coverage=100% does not prove Correctness=100%. It means all requirements have some mapped artifacts. The artifacts could still be wrong.
rows.statement: States Coverage ≠ Correctness: full coverage means mapped artifacts exist for every requirement, not that those artifacts are correct.

rows.anchor: 101.42 — Experiment 17 ... Every requirement maps to implementation. Implementation contains a security flaw. Expected: Traceability=100% but Correctness<100%. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 17: 100% traceability with an underlying security flaw shows Traceability=100% but Correctness<100%; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.43 — This gives us four distinct dimensions ... Traceability, Implementation, Verification, RuntimeConformance. They must not be collapsed.
rows.statement: States four distinct, non-collapsible dimensions: Traceability, Implementation, Verification, RuntimeConformance.

rows.anchor: 101.44 — Architecture conformance vector ... For a requirement r: C(r)=(T,I,V,R) where T=traceability, I=implementation, V=verification, R=runtime conformance.
rows.statement: Defines the per-requirement conformance vector C(r)=(T,I,V,R) over traceability/implementation/verification/runtime conformance.

rows.anchor: 101.45 — Example ... C(r)=(1,1,1,0). Meaning traceable, implemented, verified, not confirmed in runtime. That is a much more honest architectural status than 'Done.'
rows.statement: Worked example: C(r)=(1,1,1,0) — traceable, implemented, verified, but unconfirmed at runtime — a more honest status than a bare 'Done'.

rows.anchor: 101.46 — Step 101 practical objective ... construct KnowledgeOS Architecture Conformance Model with every significant architectural claim mapped to evidence.
rows.statement: States the practical goal of the empirical phase: constructing a full KnowledgeOS Architecture Conformance Model mapping every significant claim to evidence.

rows.anchor: 101.47 — What we should NOT do ... We should not now redesign KnowledgeOS simply because some implementation does not match the theory. Instead: Observed→Classify→Understand→Decide. Only then ChangeArchitecture if justified.
rows.statement: Prescribes the correct response order to observed mismatches: Observed→Classify→Understand→Decide, with ChangeArchitecture only if justified — forbidding premature redesign.

rows.anchor: 101.48 — Architecture versus implementation mismatch ... Case A: Implementation is wrong (A_C≠A_I and A_I still valid). Case B: Architecture is obsolete (A_C reflects the actual desired system better than A_I). Case C: Both are incomplete. This distinction must be made explicitly.
rows.statement: Defines three mismatch-diagnosis cases: Case A (implementation wrong, A_I still valid), Case B (architecture obsolete, A_C better reflects desired system), Case C (both incomplete) — must be distinguished explicitly.

rows.anchor: 101.49 — Experiment 18 ... Implementation diverges from architecture. Team immediately changes architecture document to match implementation. Expected: potential documentation laundering. Result: PASS. We must first establish whether the implementation change was legitimate.
rows.statement: Experiment 18: immediately editing the architecture document to match a divergent implementation is potential documentation laundering; legitimacy of the implementation change must be established first; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.50 — The governance question returns ... this connects directly with the Softwareeinführungsprozess and IT Change Management work. An architectural divergence may itself require ChangeGovernance. ArchitectureDrift→ChangeClassification→GovernancePath.
rows.statement: Routes architecture drift through ChangeClassification→GovernancePath, explicitly linking to the project's Softwareeinführungsprozess/IT Change Management work.

lineage_claims.target: Softwareeinführungsprozess and IT Change Management work
lineage_claims.quote: This connects directly with the Softwareeinführungsprozess and IT Change Management work.

rows.anchor: 101.51 — Experiment 19 ... Production architecture changes without Architecture Board review. Expected: potential governance violation if the change falls within the board's authority. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 19: a production architecture change without Architecture Board review is a potential governance violation if within board authority; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.52 — This is where KnowledgeOS connects to the organization ... Architecture↔Implementation↔Runtime and Runtime→GovernanceIssue. The system becomes capable of detecting when engineering reality diverges from organizational intent.
rows.statement: States that connecting Architecture↔Implementation↔Runtime with Runtime→GovernanceIssue lets the system detect when engineering reality diverges from organizational intent.

rows.anchor: 101.53 — KnowledgeOS architecture itself ... KnowledgeOS should be able to analyze KnowledgeOS. KnowledgeOS→KnowledgeOSArchitecture→KnowledgeOSEvidence. The platform becomes its own first customer.
rows.statement: States KnowledgeOS should recursively analyze itself (KnowledgeOS→KnowledgeOSArchitecture→KnowledgeOSEvidence), becoming its own first customer.

rows.anchor: 101.54 — Experiment 20 ... KnowledgeOS claims 'our agent governance is compliant.' KnowledgeOS analyzes its own repository. It discovers AgentAction has no complete authorization chain. Expected: self-assessment detects the gap. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 20: KnowledgeOS's self-analysis of its own repository discovering an incomplete AgentAction authorization chain confirms self-assessment detects real gaps; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.55 — Recursive architecture assurance ... System→KnowledgeOfSystem→AssuranceOfSystem. That is one of the most interesting properties of the architecture.
rows.statement: States the recursive assurance chain System→KnowledgeOfSystem→AssuranceOfSystem as one of the architecture's most interesting properties.

rows.anchor: 101.56 — But recursion must have boundaries ... otherwise KnowledgeOS→KnowledgeOS→KnowledgeOS→... could become infinite. Therefore self-analysis should have explicit scope.
rows.statement: Warns unbounded recursive self-analysis (KnowledgeOS→KnowledgeOS→...) could become infinite; self-analysis needs explicit scope.

rows.anchor: 101.57 — Experiment 21 ... System attempts to recursively analyze every generated artifact forever. Expected: resource exhaustion. Result: PASS. Step 98's resource constraints return.
rows.statement: Experiment 21: unbounded recursive analysis of every generated artifact leads to resource exhaustion, reinvoking Step 98's resource constraints; result PASS.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 98's resource constraints return.

rows.anchor: 101.58 — Self-description ... KnowledgeOS should have an explicit ArchitectureModel_self. This is not merely documentation. It is a machine-readable representation of its own architectural expectations.
rows.statement: States KnowledgeOS should maintain a machine-readable ArchitectureModel_self representing its own architectural expectations, not just documentation.

rows.anchor: 101.59 — Experiment 22 ... Architecture model says EvidenceService must exist. Repository scanner finds EvidenceService. Expected: automatic conformance candidate. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 22: a repository scanner finding an EvidenceService matching the architecture model is an automatic conformance candidate; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.60 — But machine-readable architecture cannot replace human architecture ... the formal model may omit strategic intent, organizational context, trade-offs, rationale. MachineModel ≠ CompleteArchitectureKnowledge. Both are required.
rows.statement: States MachineModel ≠ CompleteArchitectureKnowledge: the formal model omits strategic intent/context/trade-offs/rationale, so both machine and human architecture knowledge are required.

rows.anchor: 101.61 — Architecture as a knowledge system ... the architecture itself is a KnowledgeOS knowledge domain. It contains Principles, Constraints, Decisions, Components, Dependencies, Evidence, Tests, RuntimeObservations.
rows.statement: States architecture itself is a KnowledgeOS knowledge domain containing Principles, Constraints, Decisions, Components, Dependencies, Evidence, Tests, RuntimeObservations — a recursive conclusion.

rows.anchor: 101.62 — Experiment 23 ... Architecture diagram exists only as an image. No machine-readable dependency model. Expected: limited automated conformance capability. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 23: an image-only architecture diagram (no machine-readable model) has limited automated conformance capability; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.63 — Architecture must therefore become queryable ... 'which components implement this architectural rule?' or 'which rules are currently unverifiable?' or 'which runtime components violate the architecture?' or 'which ADRs are affected by this code change?' These are KnowledgeOS queries.
rows.statement: Lists four canonical KnowledgeOS-native queryable-architecture questions (implementing components, unverifiable rules, violating runtime components, ADRs affected by a code change).

rows.anchor: 101.64 — Experiment 24 ... Query: 'which architectural invariants are affected by changing the Evidence schema?' Expected: KnowledgeOS returns the dependency chain. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 24: KnowledgeOS returning the dependency chain in response to an invariant-impact query about an Evidence schema change; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 101.65 — This is the real software target ... What do we believe? Why do we believe it? Who decided? Who is authorized? What implementation realizes the decision? What tests verify it? What is actually running? Does runtime conform? What changed? What must be reverified? That is an actual software p
rows.statement: Lists ten canonical KnowledgeOS product-defining queries (belief, justification, decision-maker, authorization, implementation, verification, runtime, conformance, change, reverification needs) as the concrete software product definition.

rows.anchor: 101.66 — Step 101 verdict ... We have crossed the boundary from Architectural Theory to Architecture Conformance Engineering. The theoretical architecture remains COHERENT but the implementation status is NOT YET PROVEN until we perform the repository/runtime assessment. That is not a weakness. It i
rows.statement: Records the Step 101 verdict: crossing from Architectural Theory to Architecture Conformance Engineering, with theory remaining COHERENT and implementation status NOT YET PROVEN — the correct engineering conclusion, not a weakness.

rows.anchor: The most important conclusion at Step 101 ... We should not continue endlessly inventing theoretical architecture. STOP DESIGNING IN THE ABSTRACT and START MEASURING KNOWLEDGEOS AGAINST THE MODEL. That is how we will eventually earn 'KnowledgeOS architecture is correct' -- not because we believe it
rows.statement: States the conclusion that further abstract design should stop in favor of measuring KnowledgeOS against the model; the claim 'architecture is correct' will be earned only when requirements/implementation/tests/governance records/runtime evidence all converge, not by belief.

rows.anchor: C1. step-001 (140653) -- Operational Independence ... Ind_rho(e_i,e_j,G,C) -> {Independent,Dependent,Unknown} ... section15 the statistical correction: OperationallyIndependent does-not-imply StatisticallyIndependent
rows.statement: Step-001 (file 140653) formalizes Operational Independence: Ind_rho(e_i,e_j,G,C) -> {Independent, Dependent, Unknown}, where G is a provenance/dependency graph, C is context, rho is an independence policy; a deterministic rule (a chain relation between two evidence items forces Dependent, 'no LLM required'); a common-ancestor relation implies independence is normally Unknown, not Confirmed; different sources do not imply independence; a six-component independence evidence vector I(e_i,e_j)=(i_S,i_A,i_P,i_M,i_T,i_C) (source/acquisition/provenance/method/temporal independence plus common-ancestor status) each valued in {Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown}, explicitly refusing a scalar IndependenceScore because it 'would obscure why'; states the law 'Independence must be established, not assumed'; and adds a critical statistical correction: operationally-established independence does not imply statistical independence, so Bayesian multiplication's requirement P(E1,E2|H)=P(E1|H)P(E2|H) is a separate, stronger condition -- 'exactly why Evidence Architecture and Statistical Inference Policy must remain separate.'

rows.anchor: C2. step-002 (140919) -- Evidence Identity / Equivalence Calculus ... Identity != Semantic Equivalence != Same Observation != Independence. Five relations section5 ... section4 critical invariant: Semantic equivalence must NOT imply deduplication.
rows.statement: Step-002 (file 140919) opens with Identity != Semantic Equivalence != Same Observation != Independence and formalizes five relations between evidence items: same-evidence-object (=_I), same-proposition (=_P), same-underlying-observation (=_O), dependency (prec, e2 produced using e1), and operational independence under policy rho (perp_rho); states the critical invariant that semantic equivalence must NOT imply deduplication; works seven cases including 'different values, same observation' yielding a DERIVATION_CONFLICT status distinguishing independent-observation-count from derived-interpretation-count; builds a multi-relational lineage graph G_E=(V,L_1..L_n) with typed edge sets (DerivedFrom, ExtractedFrom, TransformedFrom, SummarizedFrom, CopiedFrom, ObservedFrom, ReviewedFrom); states CommonCause != SameObservation and CommonCause != AutomaticDependence; argues the corpus's eight relationship labels (IDENTICAL, SAME_OBSERVATION, DERIVED, SEMANTICALLY_EQUIVALENT, COMMON_SOURCE, INDEPENDENT, CONTRADICTORY, UNKNOWN) should not collapse into a single enum since they coexist; and distinguishes a fact about provenance from an inference about provenance, warning KnowledgeOS should never silently promote the second into the first.

rows.anchor: C3. step-003 (141118) -- Evidence Assessment Algebra ... EA=(S+,S-,U,Q,V,D,X,Pi) ... Notice what is not here: Truth. ... section4 Aggregation must occur after normalization ... section12 not every useful assessment is monotonic
rows.statement: Step-003 (file 141118) defines the Evidence Assessment tuple EA=(S+,S-,U,Q,V,D,X,Pi) -- Supporting, Opposing, Uncertainty, Quality, Validity/temporal, Dependency, Context/applicability, Provenance -- explicitly noting Truth is absent from the tuple; refuses S=S+-S- as an aggregate since '0.9 minus 0.8 does not mean 0.1' (there is substantial evidence on both sides); requires aggregation to occur only after a normalization step N_rho handling identity/provenance/semantic/relevance/temporal/dependency/polarity resolution; distinguishes Quality!=Relevance, Reliability!=Validity, ProvenanceQuality!=SourceAuthority; introduces an aggregation equivalence class [e]_~O (same underlying observation aggregated once unless policy states otherwise); and corrects a naive monotonicity claim: not every useful assessment is monotonic -- SupportAggregation may be monotonic with respect to additional supporting evidence while a CompleteAssessment need not be, seeding closure-04a's signed monotonicity and step-004's axiom 6. Establishes the chain Evidence->Assessment->Conclusion->Decision (never Evidence->Decision directly) and four bounded contexts (Evidence/Assessment/Knowledge/Decision Context).
missing: a selected universal aggregation operator, left deliberately open
