rows.anchor: C4. step-004 (142250) -- The Evidence Aggregation Axioms ... Axioms 1-16 ... section19 kernel invariants A1-A4 ... vs policy properties A5-A8. section20 the Evidence Constitution E-K1...E-K10 ... section21 nine-framework comparison table ... There is probably no single universal KnowledgeOS evidence algebra.
rows.statement: Step-004 (file 142250) states 16 evidence-aggregation axioms: (1) Determinism (LLM variability != epistemic randomness), (2) permutation invariance, (3) duplicate invariance ('This should be a kernel invariant'), (4) derived-evidence non-inflation, (5) irrelevance invariance, (6) supporting monotonicity with three qualifiers (admissible, independent, supporting evidence) and an explicit disclaimer that it scopes only the S+/S- components, never the final conclusion, (7) contradiction preservation, (8) conflict sensitivity, (9) dependency sensitivity, (10) unknown dependency stays unknown, (11) corroboration (value deliberately left as policy territory), (12) temporal sensitivity (Stale != Delete), (13) context sensitivity ('Evidence has no universal relevance'), (14) provenance preservation, (15) no evidence creation (empty evidence set yields NoEvidence, not 0.5 or Confirmed), (16) no certainty creation (StrongEvidence does not imply Truth). Separates four kernel invariants A1-A4 (identity preservation, provenance preservation, contradiction preservation, no automatic independence) from four policy properties A5-A8 (corroboration rule, saturation, decision threshold, probability interpretation), and states a ten-item Evidence Constitution E-K1..E-K10 covering identity, no-duplicate-inflation, provenance preservation, dependency awareness, unknown-is-not-independent, contradiction preservation, context dependence, Stale!=Deleted, no-truth-by-aggregation, and no-decision-by-aggregation. Compares nine aggregation frameworks (Maximum/Mean/Weighted-sum/Saturating/Bayesian/Dempster-Shafer/Possibility/Argumentation/Graph-based) and concludes there is probably no single universal KnowledgeOS evidence algebra, proposing a fixed kernel plus pluggable assessment calculi C_admissible = {rho | Agg_rho satisfies A_kernel}.

rows.anchor: C5. step-005 (142333) -- What Is the Mathematical Object Being Aggregated ... section21 KERNEL/POLICY partition (verbatim sets): KERNEL = {Evidence, Proposition, Provenance, Lineage, Dependency, Context, TemporalValidity, Polarity, AssessmentBasis}; POLICY = {Aggregation, Inference, Thresholds, ProbabilityModels, BeliefModels, DecisionRules}.
rows.statement: Step-005 (file 142333) states Evidence != Support != Belief != Probability != Truth, and argues the contribution function c_rho(e,P,C) must deliberately not be typed into [0,1], since '0.8 has no epistemic meaning until its semantics are specified' -- a direct answer to an earlier morning file's problem 4 (094259). Distinguishes seven semantic domains (Reliability, Relevance, Evidential support, Probability, Belief, Plausibility, Information gain) and argues the kernel must not choose one calculus over another. States the single most citable boundary statement in the batch: the KERNEL/POLICY partition, KERNEL = {Evidence, Proposition, Provenance, Lineage, Dependency, Context, TemporalValidity, Polarity, AssessmentBasis} versus POLICY = {Aggregation, Inference, Thresholds, ProbabilityModels, BeliefModels, DecisionRules} -- 'the kernel stores the dimensions, the policy determines how they combine.' Also distinguishes Assessment != Acceptance and EvidenceValue != EvidenceStrength, closing with the verdict 'substantially resolved'.

rows.anchor: C6. step-006 (142514) -- Information Gain and Value of Evidence ... Evidence Strength != Information Gain != Decision Value ... section13 q*=argmax U_rho(q|K_t,I_t,P) -- potentially one of the most important equations in the whole KnowledgeOS theory. ... section24 safeguard: refuses Moksha = Delta=0
rows.statement: Step-006 (file 142514) distinguishes Evidence Strength != Information Gain != Decision Value; defines information gain IG(e;P)=H(P)-H(P|e) but then explicitly refuses IG=EntropyReduction as a universal law, instead defining a discrepancy-reduction measure IG_D(e), an expected discrepancy reduction EDR(e) made more fundamental than entropy reduction ('KnowledgeOS is trying to move K_t toward I_t, not H(K_t) to 0'), and a value-of-evidence function VOE_rho and utility U_rho(e)=Benefit-Cost with explicitly policy-dependent weights; states q*=argmax_q U_rho(q|K_t,I_t,P) as potentially one of the most important equations in the whole theory; formalizes the guidance triad Zero(K_t,I_t)->Delta_t, Lord(Delta_t)->Q, Sarathi(Q,constraints)->a_t; and provides an explicit safeguard against an earlier morning file's (085756) Moksha-as-maximal-information claim, refusing Moksha=Delta=0 and stating Delta=0 always means only relative to the specified ideal state.

rows.anchor: C7. step-007 (142709) -- Knowledge State Transition Algebra ... K_t=(A_t,E_t,R_t,C_t,H_t,Gamma_t) ... section11 eight transition operations O_K ... with a PARTIAL map delta:K x O_K -harpoon-> K ... section33 invariants K1-K8
rows.statement: Step-007 (file 142709) defines the Knowledge State tuple K_t=(A_t,E_t,R_t,C_t,H_t,Gamma_t) (Assertions, Evidence, Relations, Conflicts, History, validity conditions), states K_t != H_t and Superseded != Deleted, and mediates Evidence-does-not-imply-Knowledge via an epistemic event rather than evidence directly. Defines eight transition operations O_K = {Introduce, Corroborate, Qualify, Contradict, Supersede, Resolve, Retract, Invalidate} as a PARTIAL function delta:K x O_K -> K (partial because, e.g., Resolve(C) is invalid if C is not an active conflict); states TemporalChange != LogicalContradiction, Retract(A) != Delete(A), Invalidation != Retraction; rejects a single linear lifecycle in favor of a multidimensional epistemic-state vector Sigma_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity); models event sourcing K_t=Fold(delta,H_t,K_0) and K_t=F(K_0,H_t,rho,omega) with rho=policy version and omega=ontology/model version; states Knowledge-time != Source-time != Validity-time; takes a paraconsistent stance allowing P and not-P representable without trivializing the whole state; and closes with eight invariants K1-K8 (Evidence does not imply Accepted Knowledge; Superseded/Retracted != Deleted; P and not-P coexist without collapse; three distinct time coordinates; reconstructibility; policy versioning; semantic versioning; state-transition function). Leaves deliberately unresolved: 'when exactly is a conclusion allowed to modify the Knowledge State?' -- handed to step-008.
missing: exact rule for when a conclusion may modify the Knowledge State

rows.statement: Step-025a-1 (file 181325) opens with an honesty flag: an attempted first prototype execution did not successfully complete, so the author explicitly declines to claim unobtained experimental results. Defines nine fundamental types (WorldState W_t != K_t; Observation O; Evidence E, explicitly Observation != Evidence; Assertion A; Assessment Q(A,E,C); KnowledgeState K_t=(A_t,Q_t,E_t,C_t,P_t); Goal G, Goal != Action; Knowledge Requirement R; Epistemic Contract C_G) and a minimal state K_t=(E_t,A_t,Q_t,C_t,P_t,V_t) with G and C_G kept outside it, marked PROVISIONAL. Raises an explicit [UNRESOLVED] question -- whether evidence is actually part of K_t or merely externally referenced -- refusing to resolve it by intuition and instead proposing to test which representation is required for historical reconstruction, retraction, provenance, and conflict resolution. Runs eight attack scenarios including the discovery that more knowledge can increase |K_{t+1}| while decreasing Readiness(K_{t+1}), and that Authorization=False implies Execute=Forbidden as part of state-transition semantics, not merely policy overlay.

rows.statement: Step-025a-5 (file 182235) property-tests the ten invariants I1-I10 (originating in step-025a-4) plus four newly promoted invariants I11-I14 (I11 No hindsight: a decision's basis is the knowledge state at decision time, not the current one; I12 World/knowledge independence; I13 Revision must not imply falsehood -- invalidating the only supporting evidence yields Unknown, not False; I14 Conflict resolution must preserve history) against generated adversarial sequences, all fourteen passing with qualifications; identifies exactly two genuine unresolved threats -- CircularDependencies (a derivation cycle A1 supports A2 and A2 supports A1, with AcyclicDerivationGraph proposed but not established) and EvidenceIdentity (not reducible to a text hash) -- plus four further threats (scale/propagation cost, stale rules requiring RuleVersion, changing ontology entering epistemic lineage, and source authority requiring temporal semantics with Truth != Authority); proposes the emergent structure K=(V,E,R,T,P,D,M) (epistemic objects, evidence/support relations, assessments/rules, temporal semantics, provenance, dependency/derivation, model/ontology/rule versions), characterizing KnowledgeOS as an increasingly revealed 'governed temporal epistemic graph' -- marked a strong emerging architectural result; and includes an explicit integrity disclaimer that no automated property-based software test was actually executed, only a conceptual/adversarial falsification pass.

rows.anchor: D7. step-025b (182411) -- Adversarial End-to-End Simulation ... section13 the demonstrated result: after the restore test, KnowledgeGain>0 but MigrationReadiness down => KnowledgeGain != ProgressTowardGoal ... 025b is the file that generates the entire 025C-025G research agenda
rows.statement: Step-025b (file 182411) runs a full end-to-end adversarial simulation (a Nexus migration scenario) covering the whole epistemic-to-operational loop rather than just the kernel, defining an epistemic contract EC_G with nine named requirements and stating Goal != EpistemicContract and Input != Evidence; demonstrates, inside the simulated loop rather than merely arguing it, that after a restore test KnowledgeGain > 0 while MigrationReadiness simultaneously decreases, establishing KnowledgeGain != ProgressTowardGoal empirically within the scenario; formalizes Delta = Zero(K_t, I, EC_G) decomposed into Epistemic/Operational/Governance gaps; states Lord does not necessarily change the world (it may select an epistemic action first); defines the pipeline Recommendation -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution; runs five injected attacks (LLM hallucination, conflicting sources, stale source, changed requirement, execution failure becoming new evidence); defines six epistemic stopping conditions S1-S6 and an epistemic budget B_epi = {Time, Cost, Risk, HumanAttention, Compute}; distinguishes the epistemic loop from the operational loop; and closes by generating the entire subsequent research agenda (unresolved items U1-U6 feeding directly into steps 025c, 025c-3, 025d, 025f, 025g).

rows.anchor: FIRST GENUINE MATHEMATICAL ERROR IN THE CORPUS -- step-025n section18's likelihood-ratio product LR(E1,E2)=LR(E1)*LR(E2) is gated only on conditional independence given H; the factorisation additionally requires independence given not-H. Counterexample supplied by the verifier.
rows.statement: Identifies and proves, by constructed counterexample, the corpus's first genuine mathematical error (not merely a canonicalization defect): step-025n states that conditional independence of two evidence items given hypothesis H alone licenses the likelihood-ratio product LR(E1,E2)=LR(E1)*LR(E2), but the correct factorization requires independence given H AND given not-H. Counterexample: E1 and E2 independent given H but perfectly correlated given not-H makes the denominator P(E1,E2|not-H)=P(E1|not-H), not the product P(E1|not-H)*P(E2|not-H), so the stated product formula overstates the evidence. Notes the source's own policy language (sections 19, 44) does forbid applying the product without a justified dependency model, so the operational safeguard exists even though the stated mathematics is wrong by one missing conjunct; the same understated condition recurs in step-025u section 45 (though its worked arithmetic there is correct). Recorded as finding TV-F-025.
missing: a corrected statement requiring independence given both H and not-H

lineage_claims.quote: the factorisation additionally requires independence given not-H

experiment.hypothesis: Whether conditional independence of two evidence items given H alone is sufficient to license the likelihood-ratio product rule.
experiment.setup: A hypothetical scenario where E1 and E2 are independent given H but perfectly correlated given not-H.
experiment.inputs: A constructed joint distribution satisfying the stated counterexample conditions.
experiment.method: Direct algebraic factorization of the joint likelihood ratio.
experiment.result: The product formula overstates the evidence because P(E1,E2|not-H) does not equal P(E1|not-H)*P(E2|not-H) under the counterexample.
experiment.interpretation: The stated sufficient condition (independence given H only) is mathematically insufficient; both conditional independences are required.
experiment.limitations: A constructed counterexample, not an exhaustive proof of all failure modes.
experiment.conclusion: TV-F-025: the corpus's first identified genuine mathematical error.

rows.anchor: Verifier counterexample (independently computed, lead verifier) ... LR(E1),LR(E2) 9.0, 9.0 | Corpus formula LR(E1)*LR(E2) 81.0 | True LR(E1,E2)=0.81/0.1 8.1 | Overstatement 10x | Posterior from prior odds 1: claimed vs actual 0.988 vs 0.890 ... the error direction is systematically toward overstating support
rows.statement: The lead verifier (not a subagent) independently re-derives and numerically confirms TV-F-025 with a precise counterexample: setting P(E1|H)=P(E2|H)=0.9 with independence given H, and P(E1|not-H)=P(E2|not-H)=0.1 but with E1 and E2 perfectly correlated given not-H, the corpus's product formula yields LR=81.0 while the true joint likelihood ratio is 8.1 -- a 10x overstatement, translating to a claimed posterior of 0.988 versus an actual 0.890 from prior odds of 1. A control check (replacing the not-H correlation with independence) recovers the product formula exactly (81.0), confirming the missing conjunct is precisely what the formula needs. Classifies the error's direction as systematically toward overstating evidential support -- exactly the 'evidence inflation' failure mode the same source file's own principles (EvidenceCount != InformationCount; Evidence has no intrinsic universal weight) exist to prevent. Severity MAJOR, but confirms the corpus's downstream policy language (forbidding the product without a justified dependency model) is safe even though the stated mathematics is wrong.

lineage_claims.quote: the error direction is systematically toward overstating support

experiment.hypothesis: How large is the numeric overstatement caused by step-025n's under-gated likelihood-ratio product formula.
experiment.setup: P(E1|H)=P(E2|H)=0.9 independent given H; P(E1|not-H)=P(E2|not-H)=0.1 but perfectly correlated given not-H.
experiment.method: Compute the joint likelihood ratio directly versus via the corpus's product formula.
experiment.result: Product formula gives LR=81.0; true joint LR is 8.1, a 10x overstatement; posterior 0.988 (claimed) vs 0.890 (actual).
experiment.interpretation: The error systematically inflates apparent evidential support.
experiment.limitations: One constructed counterexample; magnitude of overstatement varies with the degree of not-H correlation.
experiment.conclusion: TV-F-025 confirmed MATHEMATICALLY INVALID as stated, MAJOR severity.

sources.note: S0917's Step 25Y: the fully worked cryptographic-provenance/chain-of-custody model with the central Integrity/Authenticity/Authority/Truth four-way separation, forward/backward provenance traversal, and an explicit no-blockchain-required conclusion.

rows.anchor:
Integrity
eq Authenticity
eq Authority
eq Truth
rows.statement: States four properties often incorrectly collapsed into one: Integrity ≠ Authenticity ≠ Authority ≠ Truth.

rows.anchor: h=Hash(x) ... h\neq h' ... Hash verifies content integrity. It does not establish truth
rows.statement: Defines Integrity via hash comparison, verifying content has not changed without establishing truth.

rows.anchor: Signature=Verify(PublicKey,Signature,Document) ... AuthenticProducer=KnownKeyOwner ... does not prove that the producer's statement is correct
rows.statement: Defines Authenticity via signature verification establishing producer identity, not statement correctness.

rows.anchor: Authorized(a,q,t) ... an employee might be authenticated successfully but have no authority ... Authentication\neq Authorization ... Authenticity\neq Authority
rows.statement: Defines Authority via Authorized(a,q,t), giving Authentication ≠ Authorization and Authenticity ≠ Authority.

rows.anchor: Signed(Document)=True while Truth(Document)=False ... a signed false statement remains a signed false statement ... Cryptographic proof establishes properties of the artifact, not automatically properties of reality
rows.statement: States cryptography cannot establish Truth: a signed false statement remains signed and false — cryptographic proof establishes artifact properties, not reality properties.

rows.anchor: Artifact -> Integrity, Authenticity, Authority, Truth assessment ... Each is evaluated separately
rows.statement: Presents a four-layer epistemic model where each of Integrity, Authenticity, Authority, Truth is evaluated separately.

rows.anchor: E=(Content,Hash,Origin,Producer,Timestamp,Signature,Context,Provenance)
rows.statement: Defines an eight-field Evidence object carrying enough metadata to establish provenance.

rows.anchor: Fingerprint(E)=H(Content) ... Fingerprint(E_1)=Fingerprint(E_2) ... Content(E_1)=Content(E_2) with extremely high practical confidence
rows.statement: Defines evidence fingerprinting via hash, giving high-confidence content identity when fingerprints match.

rows.anchor: Hash=(Algorithm,Digest) ... SHA-256:abc123 ... otherwise future migrations can create ambiguity
rows.statement: Requires the hash algorithm itself to be versioned/recorded (Hash=(Algorithm,Digest)) to avoid future migration ambiguity.

rows.anchor: {"version":"3.70"} versus whitespace-differing JSON ... Raw hashes differ ... Canonicalize(x) before hashing ... retain the distinction between Hash(raw artifact) and Hash(canonical representation)
rows.statement: Worked canonicalization problem: whitespace-differing but semantically-identical documents hash differently, requiring Canonicalize(x) while keeping raw-hash and canonical-hash conceptually distinct.

rows.anchor: ArtifactIdentity\neq SemanticIdentity ... Two different documents may express the same proposition. Conversely, the same document may contain multiple propositions
rows.statement: States ArtifactIdentity ≠ SemanticIdentity: different documents can share a proposition; one document can hold multiple propositions.

rows.anchor: Production->Collector->Storage->KnowledgeOS->Assessment ... ChainOfCustody ... E_0\xrightarrow{capture}E_1\xrightarrow{transfer}E_2\xrightarrow{assessment}E_3 ... Each transition becomes provenance
rows.statement: Defines chain of custody across a five-stage evidence-transfer pipeline, each transition recorded as provenance.

rows.anchor: ImmutableEvidence ... E_{old} is not silently edited. Instead E_{old}\xrightarrow{Correction}E_{new} ... mirrors our temporal model
rows.statement: Prefers ImmutableEvidence with corrections modeled as new events rather than silent edits, mirroring the temporal revision model.

rows.anchor: Correction=(OriginalEvidence,CorrectedEvidence,Reason,Authority,Time) ... The original remains auditable
rows.statement: Defines a five-field Correction object, worked with a Nexus-version-correction example, keeping the original auditable.

rows.anchor: H_{root}=Merkle(E_1,\ldots,E_n) ... detect modification; deletion; insertion ... MerkleIntegrity\neq Truth
rows.statement: Defines a Merkle-tree commitment over an evidence collection detecting modification/deletion/insertion, with the explicit caveat MerkleIntegrity ≠ Truth.

rows.anchor: H_i=Hash(E_i\Vert H_{i-1}) ... modification of an earlier event propagates through subsequent hashes ... tamper evidence
rows.statement: Defines a hash chain giving tamper evidence: modifying an earlier event propagates detectably through later hashes.

rows.anchor: Do we need blockchain? No ... achieve many requirements with cryptographic hashes; signatures; append-only storage; Merkle structures; trusted timestamps; access controls; immutable object storage ... not merely because immutable knowledge sounds blockchain-like
rows.statement: States the architectural conclusion that a tamper-evident knowledge history does not require blockchain, achievable with conventional cryptographic infrastructure — blockchain should not be introduced merely because 'immutable knowledge' sounds blockchain-like.

rows.anchor: Sign_{privateKey}(Artifact) ... Verify_{publicKey}(Artifact,Signature) ... the artifact corresponds to the holder of the signing key. It does not prove the artifact's claims are true
rows.statement: Defines digital signature/verification proving key-holder correspondence, not claim truth.

rows.anchor: certificate valid 2025-01-01->2026-01-01 ... SignatureValidity(t) must be evaluated against the relevant time
rows.statement: Requires signatures to have temporal context, with SignatureValidity(t) evaluated against the certificate's validity window.

rows.anchor: KeyID and KeyVersion should be tracked ... Historical signatures should not become uninterpretable merely because an organization rotated its keys
rows.statement: Requires KeyID/KeyVersion tracking across key rotation so historical signatures remain interpretable.

rows.anchor: Was the key valid when the artifact was signed? ... different from Is the key valid today? ... KeyStatus(t_{signature}) must be considered
rows.statement: Distinguishes evaluating key validity at signing time (KeyStatus(t_signature)) from evaluating it today, relevant to later key revocation.

rows.anchor: Commitment(E,t) ... this artifact existed in relation to the timestamping mechanism. It does not prove that its contents were true
rows.statement: Defines trusted timestamping as proving temporal existence of an artifact, not the truth of its contents.

rows.anchor: Source->Artifact->{Hash,Signature,Timestamp}->Observation->Evidence Assessment->Assertion->Derivation->Conclusion ... a complete epistemic provenance graph
rows.statement: Presents a complete epistemic provenance graph from source through cryptographic properties to final conclusion.

rows.anchor: C\rightarrow D\rightarrow A\rightarrow E\rightarrow Artifact\rightarrow Source ... EndToEndTraceability
rows.statement: Defines backward provenance traversal from any conclusion to its originating source, giving EndToEndTraceability.

rows.anchor: Descendants(E) ... Which conclusions and decisions depend on this evidence? ... becomes critical when evidence is later invalidated
rows.statement: Defines forward provenance traversal Descendants(E), identifying dependent conclusions/decisions, critical when evidence is later invalidated.

rows.anchor: Impact(E_1)=Descendants(E_1) ... E1 invalidated->Assertion A invalidated->Derivation D invalidated->Decision D2 requires review->Action A3 potentially affected ... an extremely powerful operational capability
rows.statement: Worked impact-analysis chain tracing a discovered-wrong evidence item through invalidated assertion/derivation to a decision requiring review and a potentially-affected action.

rows.anchor: Invalid(E)\neq Deleted(E) ... Invalidate(E,t,reason) ... preserves the historical record
rows.statement: Restates non-destructive invalidation: Invalid(E) ≠ Deleted(E), modeled as an Invalidate(E,t,reason) event preserving history.

rows.anchor: Assessment(E)=f(Integrity,Authenticity,Authority,Reliability,Independence,TemporalValidity,SemanticValidity) ... much more rigorous
rows.statement: Defines a seven-dimension evidence Assessment function, more rigorous than simple trust.

rows.anchor: Integrity: HIGH, Authenticity: HIGH, Authority: LOW, Reliability: UNKNOWN, Truth: UNKNOWN ... more informative than EvidenceScore=0.72
rows.statement: Worked example showing a mixed multi-dimensional profile is more informative than a single scalar EvidenceScore.

rows.anchor: Score(E)=0.95 ... authentic? authoritative? likely true? fresh? relevant? ... A single number hides the epistemic dimensions ... VectorAssessment>SingleConfidenceScore
rows.statement: Warns a bare score like 0.95 is ambiguous across authenticity/authority/likely-truth/freshness/relevance — VectorAssessment > SingleConfidenceScore.

rows.anchor: A(E)=(I,Au,Auth,R,Ind,T,S) ... a multidimensional evidence assessment
rows.statement: Defines a seven-component evidence-assessment vector A(E)=(Integrity,Authority,Authenticity,Reliability,Independence,TemporalValidity,SemanticValidity).

rows.anchor: Rel(E,q) ... A valid document about Nexus development does not necessarily prove the production Nexus version ... Authentic(E)=True does not imply Relevant(E,q)=True
rows.statement: Adds Relevance Rel(E,q) as a distinct dimension: authenticity does not imply relevance to a specific question.

rows.anchor: Sufficient(E_1,\ldots,E_n,q) ... For a low-risk question E_1 may be enough. For a high-risk governance decision E_1,E_2,E_3 may be required
rows.statement: Defines a domain- and decision-specific evidence-sufficiency function requiring different amounts of evidence depending on risk level.

rows.anchor: EvidenceStrength=0.9 ... EvidenceRequirement(q)=High ... 0.9 might be insufficient ... EvidenceSufficiency depends on decision context
rows.statement: States EvidenceSufficiency depends on decision context: a fixed evidence-strength value may be insufficient against a stricter decision threshold.

rows.anchor: Chain of custody ... not become a generic technical concern only ... compliance; legal evidence; security incidents; financial transactions; governance decisions ... the domain may define stronger custody invariants
rows.statement: Places chain-of-custody as domain-owned in certain bounded contexts (compliance, legal, security, finance, governance), not merely a generic technical concern.

rows.anchor: OriginalEvidence must remain retrievable after correction/invalidation ... historical auditability
rows.statement: States the anti-tampering invariant: original evidence must remain retrievable after correction/invalidation, for historical auditability.

rows.anchor: Conclusion\rightarrow Derivation\rightarrow Evidence\rightarrow Origin ... If this chain cannot be established, the conclusion should receive a weaker epistemic status ... Untraceable
rows.statement: States the provenance invariant Conclusion->Derivation->Evidence->Origin, with an Untraceable status when the chain cannot be established.

rows.anchor: Conclusion: Migration is safe. Provenance: missing ... OrphanKnowledge. And Zero_{provenance}
rows.statement: Defines OrphanKnowledge and Zero_provenance for a conclusion with missing provenance, explicitly not treated as equivalent to a fully traceable conclusion.

rows.anchor: A signed document may be perfectly authentic. But we still need Meaning(Document) ... CryptographicProvenance and SemanticProvenance are complementary
rows.statement: States cryptographic provenance and semantic provenance are complementary, not substitutable — authenticity says nothing about meaning.

rows.anchor: The Nexus migration requires an Architecture Board review [LLM] ... we can prove Output_{LLM} has not been altered. But that says nothing about whether the statement is correct ... LLMOutputIntegrity\neq LLMOutputTruth
rows.statement: Worked example: hashing an LLM's output proves it unaltered without proving it correct — LLMOutputIntegrity ≠ LLMOutputTruth; the output still needs evidence and derivation.

rows.anchor: ModelID, ModelVersion, Prompt/InstructionContext, InputReferences, GenerationTime, ToolCalls, OutputHash ... allows reproducibility and audit
rows.statement: Defines a seven-field AI-provenance record for reproducibility and audit of AI-generated assertions.

rows.anchor: privacy; security; access control; data minimization. Not every prompt or raw source should necessarily be globally visible ... Provenance completeness must coexist with information governance
rows.statement: Warns provenance completeness must respect privacy/security/access-control/data-minimization; not every prompt or raw source should be globally visible.

rows.anchor: CanSee(Provenance) and CanSee(Content) can be different permissions ... Conclusion derived from Evidence E17 ... but not necessarily the confidential contents of E17
rows.statement: Distinguishes CanSee(Provenance) from CanSee(Content) as separate access permissions, allowing a user to know a conclusion's evidentiary basis without seeing confidential content.

rows.anchor: Integrity does not imply Availability ... IntegrityStatus separately from AvailabilityStatus
rows.statement: States Integrity does not imply Availability, requiring separately tracked IntegrityStatus and AvailabilityStatus.

rows.anchor: Falsification tests A-I: modified artifact->HashMismatch PASS; signed false statement->Authenticity=True,Truth=Unknown/False PASS; authenticated-unauthorized approval attempt->Authenticated=True,Authorized=False PASS; invalidated evidence->dependency graph identifies affected conclusions PASS; artif
rows.statement: Runs nine falsification tests (A-I, all PASS) against the evidence-integrity model: a modified artifact yields HashMismatch; a signed false statement yields Authenticity=True but Truth=Unknown/False; an authenticated-but-unauthorized approval attempt yields Authenticated=True/Authorized=False; invalidating evidence used by a conclusion causes the dependency graph to identify affected conclusions; replacing an artifact's content while keeping its database ID yields IntegrityViolation; correcting a record keeps the original accessible alongside a new corrected record; three replicas of identical signed evidence yield IndependentSources=1; a highly-convincing but unsupported LLM conclusion yields OutputIntegrity=True possibly but EvidenceSupport=Insufficient so it cannot become authoritative merely by being well-written; and a valid document using an obsolete semantic definition yields CryptographicIntegrity=True but SemanticValidity=RequiresHistoricalContext.

experiment.hypothesis: The evidence-integrity/authenticity/authority/truth-separation model behaves correctly across nine representative scenarios.
experiment.setup: Nine scenarios A-I spanning tampering, signed-false-statements, unauthorized actors, evidence invalidation impact, artifact substitution, correction, replication, unsupported LLM claims, and obsolete semantics.
experiment.method: apply the integrity/authenticity/authority/truth definitions and provenance rules to each scenario
experiment.result: All nine scenarios produce the theoretically expected outcome
experiment.interpretation: Confirms the model never conflates cryptographic verification with factual correctness.
experiment.limitations: illustrative, not executed
experiment.conclusion: All nine tests PASS.

rows.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
rows.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). rows.anchor: Concept relationships — the reviewer's example chain, validated ... KnowledgeOS creates PKS contains Engineering Knowledge organized by Ontology used by Capabilities executed through Runtime produces Evidence improves KnowledgeOS
rows.statement: The proposed chain is validated edge by edge: 'KnowledgeOS creates PKS' is a hypothesis (n=0, every PKS is authored by a person); 'PKS contains Engineering Knowledge' is WRONG, violating I-7 (a PKS contains product knowledge and bindings; reusable method must not live in it — the current breach is the exception that proves the rule); 'knowledge organized by Ontology' holds with the precision that L-A organizes artifacts/carriers, not knowledge itself (I-1); 'used by Capabilities' holds (capabilities may read across space boundaries, never own — H-1); 'Capabilities executed through Runtime' is imprecise (capabilities are advisory scripts invoked on demand; the runtime executes Execution Assets/ASTs; 41 enforced controls live runtime-side while every capability is advisory — the drawn edge hides this finding); 'Runtime produces Evidence' should attribute production to WORK (P-7/P-8), the runtime only hosts the work; 'Evidence improves KnowledgeOS' is only partly true (n≈3 informal, B-1's fact).

Notable entries: KNOWLEDGE SPACE may contain artifacts and other knowledge spaces, generates PROJECTIONS; PKS may contain product artifacts but never reusable Method, references Engineering Knowledge, generates Product Projections; ARTIFACT is a leaf (contains nothing) but depends on the Knowledge it represents; KNOWLEDGE generates nothing, being represented rather than generative.

rows.anchor: Concept-by-concept projection ... 8 invariant · 2 specialize · 1 disappears · 1 relationship fails
rows.statement: Twelve concepts projected into PublicDigit, a hypothetical Hospital Information System, and a hypothetical ERP System: MISSION, STRATEGY, DESIGN POLICY, CAPABILITY, KNOWLEDGE, ARTIFACT, KNOWLEDGE SPACE, PRODUCT are invariant across all three; PRINCIPLE specializes (partly external in Hospital and ERP, owned by a regulator/accounting standard); PKS fails (one per product, or per deployment?); RUNTIME ADAPTER disappears in both new domains; PROJECTION (I-4) fails, since a discharge summary and a financial statement are both generated and legally/formally authoritative.

experiment.hypothesis: The relationship ontology's twelve concepts and eleven invariants hold unchanged when projected into unrelated product domains.
experiment.setup: The ontology was held fixed and conceptually (no implementation) projected into three domains: PublicDigit (actual), a hypothetical Hospital Information System, and a hypothetical ERP System, examining each concept and invariant for survival.
experiment.assumptions: the hypothetical domains are represented faithfully enough by their described contexts, invariants, design policies, bindings and authorities
experiment.inputs: domain sketches for PublicDigit, Hospital, ERP (contexts, core invariant, a design policy, a binding, authority)
experiment.method: concept-by-concept and invariant-by-invariant projection and comparison across the three domains
experiment.result: 8 of 12 concepts and 10 of 11 invariants survived unchanged; PRINCIPLE and PKS required specialization; RUNTIME ADAPTER disappeared in the two new domains; I-4 was falsified.
experiment.interpretation: the ontology is largely domain-independent but has a systemic gap: it can express structure but not transformation (specialization, external constraint, instantiation, attestation).
experiment.limitations: the Hospital and ERP domains are hypothetical, not implemented or independently reviewed
experiment.conclusion: the ontology survives projection but not unchanged; PublicDigit itself masked two of the three failures (multi-tenancy, external legal authority).

rows.anchor: F-2 · "One PKS per product" fails for configurable products ... the same ERP is deployed to fifty customers ... What the ontology cannot express | the difference between a PRODUCT and a DEPLOYMENT of it
rows.statement: 'One PKS per product' fails: the same ERP deployed to fifty customers with different charts of accounts, fiscal calendars, and jurisdictions raises the unanswered question of whether that is one PKS with fifty bindings or fifty PKSs. PublicDigit masks this: it has multi-tenancy (organisation_id) in the code, and the model treats it as one product — the concept is present in the product and absent from the ontology. PRODUCT is atomic in the model and cannot express PRODUCT vs DEPLOYMENT.

rows.anchor: Product Definition ... The generative relation is creates, not contains. KnowledgeOS → creates → PKS → guides → Product
rows.statement: Product definitions: KnowledgeOS (the reusable engineering platform, output is rules and methods, never product knowledge; canon status: potential product, Supporting Subdomain, gate unopened); PKS (one product's knowledge, one per product, never reusable, generated is n=0, every PKS hand-built to date); Business Product (the software delivering business value); Running Software (deployed system + evidence); AI Runtime (an adapter, not a product, replaceable); Product Binding (the product-specific input contract a reusable method requires, SD-1 the archetype — 'the concept this baseline contributes'). The generative relation is 'creates', not 'contains': KnowledgeOS creates PKS, which guides Product — a compiler is not the program it produces.

rows.anchor: Product Architecture — Five tiers ... T2 is the tier the recent work uncovered, and it is NOT PKS ... subsystems are INTERNAL
rows.statement: A five-tier product architecture: T1 KnowledgeOS (the reusable engineering product); T2 KnowledgeOS Services (governance, capabilities, validation, runtime integration, operational learning, PKS generation — the platform's internal service layer, not PKS); T3 Product PKS (one generated PKS per product); T4 Business Product; T5 Running Software. Six subsystems marked with honest per-subsystem evidence status: Governance and Capabilities and Validation evidenced-operating; Runtime Integration evidenced at n=1 runtime only; Operational Learning evidenced but non-functioning (0 traversals); PKS Generation is responsibility-only, no implementation. Subsystems are declared internal, never repository roots — promoting one to a root would encode an internal design decision as a repository-wide boundary; ES-005.2 independently forbids proposing an empty directory.
invariants: subsystems are internal, not repository roots

rows.anchor: Extraction Boundary ... The boundary is not a file list. It is a decomposition ... METHOD | BINDING | EVIDENCE / CASE LAW
rows.statement: The extraction boundary is corrected from a file list (Product Boundary Discovery's section 6, refuted at n=1) to a decomposition: METHOD belongs to KnowledgeOS (domain-free and binding-free and evidence-free); BINDING belongs to the Product PKS (the product-specific input contract the method requires); EVIDENCE/CASE LAW belongs to the Product PKS (what happened in one project). Applied to Round47-OP: the nine boundary criteria and the candidate rejection protocol are METHOD (KnowledgeOS); SD-1 is BINDING (the PKS, replaced by a generic input contract); the worked election seams are EVIDENCE (PublicDigit's PKS). The real extraction work is decomposing artifacts into method/binding/evidence, not moving files — a knowledge-engineering question, not a DDD one.

rows.anchor: P3 · Responsibility vs Component — the genesis gap ... Accepted refinement: "PKS Generator doesn't exist" was imprecise ... a Human-in-the-Loop Adapter
rows.statement: A responsibility becomes a component only when exercised at least once, by someone other than the originator, with a repeatable pattern extracted from >=2 instances. A prior claim 'PKS Generator doesn't exist' is refined as imprecise: the RESPONSIBILITY exists (an architect reads KnowledgeOS and creates a PKS); the COMPONENT does not exist (no automation, no repeatable pattern, n=0); today's implementation is a Human-in-the-Loop Adapter — the port exists, the adapter is a person. Bootstrapping decomposes into three responsibilities: bootstrap PKS (n=0), bootstrap engineering (n=1), bootstrap software (n=0).

This decomposes bootstrapping into three distinct responsibilities, only one exercised: R-A bootstrap a PKS (n=0, every PKS to date hand-built); R-B bootstrap engineering (n=1, the experiment, boundary insufficient); R-C bootstrap software (n=0, no code written in the experiment). rows.anchor: Objective 2 — Products vs subsystems ... Promoting a subsystem responsibility to a repository root would encode an INTERNAL DESIGN DECISION as a REPOSITORY-WIDE OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY
rows.statement: Two orthogonal classifications must not be collapsed: product ownership (who owns this knowledge, a stable ownership boundary) vs architectural responsibility (what responsibility does this artifact describe, internal and changes as design evolves). KnowledgeOS is classified PRODUCT (canon: potential product, gate unopened); PKS a generated product artifact instance; PublicDigit a business product; runtime adapters not products, replaceable; Bootstrap/Capabilities/Governance/Validation/Learning are internal subsystems of KnowledgeOS, analogous to Spring Core/Beans/MVC. Promoting a subsystem to a repository root would encode an internal design decision as a repository-wide ownership boundary.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Platform Lifecycle (Idea→Knowledge→PKS→Implementation→Evidence→Evolution) ... B-1 correction: software→evidence OBSERVED · back-edge n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal · KnowledgeOS→PKS n=0 · Genesis has NO route
rationale_evidence.statement: The platform lifecycle is graded link-by-link: software-to-evidence is observed; the back-edge is n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal; KnowledgeOS-to-PKS generation is n=0; and the Genesis stage has no route at all. Individual grades are confirmed; the loop as a whole remains a hypothesis.

rationale_evidence.anchor: R-6 | KnowledgeOS —creates→ PKS | UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven inside and outside
rationale_evidence.statement: Relationship R-6: KnowledgeOS creates PKS. External support: scaffolding/generators (Spring Initializr-class) are implementation guidance only; context-engineering platforms that auto-assemble context are adjacent. Challenge: no external instance of generating a governed knowledge space is found; internally n=0. Confidence: UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven both inside and outside the corpus.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The relationship pass sharpens the concept pass's conclusion: the platform's EDGES are almost all standard engineering — what is uniquely unproven is ONE edge (creates → PKS) and ONE layer name (DP-n)
rationale_evidence.statement: Aggregate result: externally supported (>=HIGH) relationships are R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8, R-10, and R-2's separation; medium relationships are R-1, R-7, R-9; the unique, operationally-unproven items are R-6 (creates->PKS) and DP-n as a named layer. The distinctive bet of KnowledgeOS is now precisely locatable as R-6; everything else is either validated or a naming choice, and R-6 is exactly what the charter's gated stages and the docket's doors already refuse to assume.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Concept relationships — the reviewer's example chain, validated ... KnowledgeOS creates PKS contains Engineering Knowledge organized by Ontology used by Capabilities executed through Runtime produces Evidence improves KnowledgeOS
rationale_evidence.statement: The proposed chain is validated edge by edge: 'KnowledgeOS creates PKS' is a hypothesis (n=0, every PKS is authored by a person); 'PKS contains Engineering Knowledge' is WRONG, violating I-7 (a PKS contains product knowledge and bindings; reusable method must not live in it — the current breach is the exception that proves the rule); 'knowledge organized by Ontology' holds with the precision that L-A organizes artifacts/carriers, not knowledge itself (I-1); 'used by Capabilities' holds (capabilities may read across space boundaries, never own — H-1); 'Capabilities executed through Runtime' is imprecise (capabilities are advisory scripts invoked on demand; the runtime executes Execution Assets/ASTs; 41 enforced controls live runtime-side while every capability is advisory — the drawn edge hides this finding); 'Runtime produces Evidence' should attribute production to WORK (P-7/P-8), the runtime only hosts the work; 'Evidence improves KnowledgeOS' is only partly true (n≈3 informal, B-1's fact).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Confidence — R16 Workbook scale, scored independently ... falsified ≠ unevidenced
rationale_evidence.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

rationale_evidence.anchor: The Lifecycle (L-1..L-6) ... the genesis correction P3/§0 forces into the lifecycle: the platform governs change; it does not govern genesis
rationale_evidence.statement: Six lifecycle transitions graded: L-1 discover a product (HYPOTHESIS, charter Stage 1 unapproved); L-2 discovery->generate a PKS (HYPOTHESIS, n=0, adapter is human); L-3 PKS->guide engineering (PARTIAL, protocol used, effect unmeasured); L-4 engineering->produce software (EVIDENCED, 1,532 files); L-5 software->collect evidence (PARTIAL, 106 reports); L-6 evidence->improve KnowledgeOS (EMPTY, never traversed). The genesis correction forces an additional insertion: Idea -> GENESIS -> KnowledgeOS -> Engineering -> Software, where the GENESIS box has no governing rule.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Migration Map — Nine of sixteen rows need NO MOVE ... Seven are blocked, and every blocker is a recorded governance gate, not a design gap
rationale_evidence.statement: A 16-row migration map (M-1..M-16) traces every artifact's current home, future home, and extraction trigger, all quoted from canon. Nine rows need no move (already in permanent home), including M-10 CAP-001 Domain/Application/Shared as extractable now with zero repository knowledge verified. Seven rows are blocked, each by a recorded governance gate (R-37, BRM-1, Phase II freeze, OQ-K1), not a design gap: M-5 Layer_Verification_Rule (OQ-K1), M-6 Integrity Model/Review Method/ARB Discipline (Phase II freeze + R-37 + OQ-K1), M-7 Methodology Baseline (BRM-1), M-9 PKS_Phase_III (R-37), M-11 CAP-001 Infrastructure (must never be extracted), M-12 .claude/settings.json (never moves), M-13 Capability Mapping (waits on a second runtime adapter), M-16 Cross-product research (OQ-K2).

rationale_evidence.anchor: C-3 · What the experiment actually tested — ACCEPTED, and it is the most consequential correction ... three distinct responsibilities, only one of which has ever been exercised
rationale_evidence.statement: The MVK experiment tested Knowledge -> ARCHITECT (reading rules) -> Software (n=1, FAIL on boundary), not KnowledgeOS -> PKS GENERATOR -> Software (n=0, not tested). This decomposes bootstrapping into three distinct responsibilities, only one exercised: R-A bootstrap a PKS (n=0, every PKS to date hand-built); R-B bootstrap engineering (n=1, the experiment, boundary insufficient); R-C bootstrap software (n=0, no code written in the experiment). The 'PKS Generator' slot in the target architecture is currently occupied by a person reading documents; whether a generator can occupy it is untested.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Strategic Context Map (conceptual) ... One of five arrows is evidenced. The loop-closing arrow is empty, and the loop contains a component that has never existed
rationale_evidence.statement: A conceptual context map (no folders, no files moved) traces five arrows: KnowledgeOS->PKS Generator (component does not exist); PKS Generator->Product PKS (hypothesis, n=0); Product PKS->Business Product (partially evidenced); Business Product->Operational Evidence (evidenced, 106 reports); Operational Evidence->KnowledgeOS (empty, zero-independent, never traversed). One of five arrows is evidenced; the loop-closing arrow is empty and the loop contains a component (PKS Generator) that has never existed. No additional context is justified by the experiment.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Bootstrap Readiness ... 4 of 8 steps are ready. The blocked ones are steps 1, 2, 3 and 8 — the beginning and the end ... The orchestration is a Process Manager whose middle exists and whose ends do not
rationale_evidence.statement: An 8-step bootstrap orchestration of existing capabilities (no design of knowledgeos init) shows 4 of 8 steps ready (tactical modelling, capability instantiation, runtime binding, verification) while steps 1 (establish execution lifecycle, blocked by Genesis/role scaling), 2 (discover the domain, blocked by SD-1), 3 (produce the PKS, blocked at n=0), and 8 (harvest and improve, blocked by 0 traversals) are blocked — the beginning and the end. init remains premature since P3 requires n>=2.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Landscape integration -- which EKS/PKS/AIP responsibilities already exist, and where their boundaries lie
rationale_evidence.statement: Nine landscape findings (C-1..C-10 evidence) mapped onto the register, with F2/F3/F4 carry-forwards honored (implemented mechanism != domain ownership; evidence is current-state-scoped not universal; consumption != ownership != KnowledgeOS): state-as-fold/append-only log (C-2, SAME as Revisability-001's enforcement, mechanism layer); forward-only supersession (C-5, SAME as Revisability-001, asymmetric ownership PKS-governance/EKS-mechanism/AIP-declared-only); closed-verdict vocabulary (C-3, SAME as the Validation Layer, a published-language boundary); assessment-conferring-no-authority (C-4, SAME as INV-003 Established); epistemic-class discipline (C-8, SAME as Pramana-001's source-role separation, PKS-owned, asymmetric F3); regenerable non-authoritative projection (C-7, SAME as INV-004 Established); honest-UNKNOWN (C-10, SAME as H-ZERO-001, 'discipline, not mechanism'); authority-as-recorded-reference (C-1, SAME as the Authority family's core, X-02 SAME-vs-RELATED across systems UNKNOWN/U-02); the F4 relationship question (AIP is DISTINCT -- a consumer/runtime, not the owner, not the KnowledgeOS layer itself).

rows.anchor: R-1 resolved — the "missing AI-execution layer" ALREADY EXISTS ... VERDICT: the concept exists and is GOVERNED — it is the Platform Registry's asset model
rows.statement: The reviewer's proposed new concept, 'AI Execution Assets' (prompts, system instructions, workflow templates, checklists, questionnaires), is checked before admitting: AST-011 is a registered prompt template (IDD_Prompt_Template_Push_Implementation_Design.md); AST-012/013 are instruction documents; AST-002..010/014 are hooks/guards; a closed runtime_moment_enum exists (SESSION_START, PRE_ACTION, POST_ARTIFACT, SESSION_END, ON_DEMAND); CMP components are technology-agnostic abstractions; R-42 scopes the registry to platform assets only. Verdict: the concept already exists and is governed as the Platform Registry's AST asset model — a prompt is an AST with a runtime moment and five-question lineage. What is actually missing is one LINK, not one layer: the capability model never states that a capability's runtime-facing artifacts are ASTs. R-1 downgrades from 'missing semantic layer' to 'unlinked existing layer', recorded as SC-6, an ARB linkage question, not a new concept — occurrence #12 of model amnesia avoided by checking.

rows.anchor: The six concepts ... MISSION · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE · ENGINEERING CAPABILITY · ENGINEERING ARTIFACT · PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE · PRODUCT
rows.statement: Six concepts defined by responsibility/lifecycle/owner/dependencies, none defined by a folder: MISSION (why the platform exists; enacted->candidate->ratified, currently enacted-unratified; owner: sponsor; depends on nothing, the root); ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (rules/methods/decisions that transfer between products; ES-006.1 ladder; owner DA for policy, sponsor+ARB for method; depends on MISSION); ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (protect exactly one invariant; observed->...->promoted; shape frozen under PGP-01..05; depends on MISSION+KNOWLEDGE); ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (carry knowledge in a representation, never the knowledge itself; statuses.yaml 8 states lint-enforced; owner field; depends on KNOWLEDGE); PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE (hold one product's concepts/language/contexts/bindings; authored today, generated as hypothesis n=0; owner product team; depends on KNOWLEDGE method + PRODUCT subject); PRODUCT (deliver business value; own delivery lifecycle; owner product team; depends on PKS + CAPABILITY).

Chain: MISSION -> STRATEGY -> PRINCIPLE -> DESIGN POLICY -> CAPABILITY -> KNOWLEDGE -> ARTIFACT.

rows.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
rows.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

rows.anchor: The relationship model — the commission's seven questions ... contains = a container relation · references = a pointer · generates = produces a new instance · depends on = cannot be understood without
rows.statement: A full relationship table across all thirteen concepts, using four typed relations (contains = container relation, references = a pointer, generates = produces a new instance, depends on = cannot be understood without). Notable entries: KNOWLEDGE SPACE may contain artifacts and other knowledge spaces, generates PROJECTIONS; PKS may contain product artifacts but never reusable Method, references Engineering Knowledge, generates Product Projections; ARTIFACT is a leaf (contains nothing) but depends on the Knowledge it represents; KNOWLEDGE generates nothing, being represented rather than generative.
invariants: I-7: a PKS never contains reusable Method

rows.statement: Eleven real artifacts (identifier-check.php, governed-registers.yaml, portal/graph/knowledge-graph.md, .claude/settings.json, Round39-MC, Round40-00 charter, 106 verification reports, docs/knowledge/, PKS_..._M4, CAP-001 §9 evidence record, this document) were each placed under the model with no additional top-level concept required. The test surfaced a new candidate relation: governed-registers.yaml sits in the product space while the capability reading it is platform — a Capability may read across a space boundary but never own what it reads — recorded as I-12 candidate (H-1).

rows.anchor: The responsibility matrix (11 responsibilities × METHOD/BINDING/EVIDENCE/IMPLEMENTATION, plus ENFORCEMENT)
rows.statement: Eleven responsibilities scored across five dimensions (Product Discovery, Strategic Discovery, Tactical Discovery, PKS Generation, Engineering Governance, Capability Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Verification, Evidence Collection, Operational Learning, Capability Evolution). Dimension totals: METHOD 8/11 complete (strongest dimension); BINDING 4/11 carry a coupling (SD-1 fatal, ES-005.1 leak, config paths, 2 product-specific by nature); EVIDENCE 4/11 at n=0, only 3 have more than a single instance; IMPLEMENTATION 6/11 fully manual, 0 generative; ENFORCEMENT 0/11 (before correction below).

rows.anchor: CORRECTED 2026-08-02 — "0 OF 11 ENFORCING" IS TOO STRONG ... .claude/settings.json holds deny ×19 and ask ×22 — 41 controls the runtime genuinely ENFORCES. What I actually established is that no CAPABILITY enforces, not that nothing does
rows.statement: A prior claim that 0 of 11 responsibilities are enforcing is corrected: applying the Boundaries!=Triggers vocabulary immediately falsifies it, since .claude/settings.json holds permissions.deny x19 (BOUNDARY, enforced) and permissions.ask x22 (TRIGGER, enforced) — 41 controls the runtime genuinely enforces; 10 hooks + 6 scripts are ADVISORY (16, not enforced). The sharper finding: enforcement lives in the RUNTIME ADAPTER, capabilities live in the PLATFORM — enforcement exists exactly where governance does not, and is absent exactly where it does.

lineage_claims.quote: "0 OF 11 ENFORCING" IS TOO STRONG ... What I actually established is that no CAPABILITY enforces, not that nothing does.

rows.anchor: THE FINDING THIS ASSESSMENT CONTRIBUTES: MATURITY ≠ ENFORCEMENT ... the platform is adoptable by habit, never by mechanism ... knowledgeos init is an ENFORCING mechanism — a command that makes something happen. The platform has never had one, at any maturity level
rows.statement: Not one capability-level responsibility is enforcing; every automation is advisory (all ten .claude/scripts/ hooks are *-reminder/*-guard; identifier-check.php, knowledge-lint, link-check, doc-placement --verify all run only if invoked). This confirms CAP-001's OE-1 at platform scale: the platform is adoptable by habit, never by mechanism. Since knowledgeos init is by definition an enforcing mechanism (a command that makes something happen), the platform has never had one at any maturity level.

rows.anchor: Bootstrap Record — what the MVK did produce ... The most telling single result: the tactical principles demoted "two staff may adjust the same item at once" from invariant to mechanism
rows.statement: The executing session produced substantial output despite the FAIL verdict: a Stock Accuracy capability; one bounded context (Inventory, with Selling/Receiving/Catalog deliberately rejected as role separations not boundaries); a 7-term ubiquitous language with two homonyms guarded before being written (Stock, Count); three invariants; a decision record satisfying all eight Decision-Model-Integrity properties with no template available; a RED test boundary; a capability on the CAP-001 template; and five candidate abstractions (2 value objects, 1 event, 1 command, 1 repository method) rejected by MVK rules. The tactical principles' demotion of a modelling temptation from invariant to mechanism is highlighted as a governance kit doing discriminating work in a domain it was never written for.

rows.anchor: The nature questions — temporal · persistent · executable · conceptual ... Exactly one archetype has execution as its ESSENCE: CAPABILITY
rows.statement: Exactly one archetype has execution as its essence: CAPABILITY (I-11 verbatim: 'Knowledge does not execute. Capabilities execute.'); RUNTIME ASSETS execute at the boundary (AST-nnn); an executable ARTIFACT (e.g. identifier-check.php) is executable only as a representation-dimension property, not an archetype property — executability does not change its kind. Conceptual (never executable, never runtime-resident): PURPOSE, DOMAIN, KNOWLEDGE. Temporal: PROCESS (has a clock, two lifecycles never conflated, work-execution progression) and PROJECTION (temporal by rebuildability, authoritative only via attestation). Persistent: KNOWLEDGE outlives its artifacts; ARTIFACTS persist as representations; PURPOSE persists by enactment.

rows.anchor: The hierarchy hypothesis — TESTED AND REFUTED AS A SINGLE STACK ... one supported edge, one refuted edge, four unevidenced. The single stack does not exist
rows.statement: The proposed single stack Purpose->Knowledge->Domain->Capability->Process->Runtime->Artifact is tested edge by edge: Purpose-above-all is supported; Knowledge->Domain has no evidence in either direction; Domain->Capability is already refuted (DP-n owns capabilities, not domains); Capability->Process has no evidence (if anything the arrow points the other way); Process->Runtime is inverted-ish (the runtime hosts the work); Runtime->Artifact holds only as containment of configuration artifacts. Verdict: one supported, one refuted, four unevidenced — the single stack does not exist. Collapsing four distinct orders into one stack is level mixing, a fourth instance of that error class in the corpus.

lineage_claims.quote: one supported edge, one refuted edge, four unevidenced. The single stack does not exist.

rows.anchor: What exists instead ... FOUR DISTINCT PARTIAL ORDERS, one per relationship type: AUTHORITY · PRODUCTION · REALIZATION · CONTAINMENT
rows.statement: Four evidenced partial orders replace the refuted single stack: AUTHORITY (who justifies whom) PURPOSE->STRATEGY->PRINCIPLE->DP-n->CAPABILITY; PRODUCTION (who produces whom) PROCESS->Knowledge/Artifacts/Evidence, CAPABILITY->Evidence, CONTAINER->Projection (n=1); REALIZATION (concept -> executable/persistent form) KNOWLEDGE->ARTIFACT (I-1), CAPABILITY->RUNTIME ASSET (R-7, SC-6 gap); CONTAINMENT (what moves together) CONTAINER contains Artifacts (contains other spaces? H-3 open). The intuition underneath the stack survives: relations are directional, with DOMAIN/KNOWLEDGE conceptual and RUNTIME/ARTIFACT realized; but 'which is above' is only answerable per relation, not for the stack as a whole.

Persistent: KNOWLEDGE outlives its artifacts; ARTIFACTS persist as representations; PURPOSE persists by enactment.

rows.anchor: Williamson rejects the assumption that knowledge can be completely separated into an internal mental part and an external-world part... he explicitly describes knowledge as broad
rows.statement: Knowledge is broad: K_A(P) depends not only on A's internal representation but on the external world, context, object of knowledge, and relevant environment. This revises the earlier Agent->projection->Knowledge Space model: the agent does not invent the space, the agent's knowledge is constitutively connected to the space (KNOWLEDGE SPACE Ω -> external world/social reality/semantic structures -> participant/agent -> capacity+access -> epistemic state).

rows.anchor: The Knowledge Space is an unbounded space of reality, meaning, institutional structures, events, relations and propositions.
rows.statement: Final synthesis: 'The Knowledge Space is an unbounded space of reality, meaning, institutional structures, events, relations and propositions. Persons, machines and organizations have limited capacities and therefore form bounded, contextual, time-dependent projections of that space. Knowledge is a factive relation/state within such a projection—not merely information, representation, belief, evidence or truth alone. KnowledgeOS preserves the identities, contexts, provenance, temporal histories, epistemic transitions and knowledge attributions necessary for those projections to be reconstructed and evaluated under different regimes.' Capstone principle: KnowledgeOS must not confuse the projection with the space, the representation with the knowledge, or the epistemic assessment with reality — supported by McGinn, Floridi, Dretske, Fagin, Gärdenfors, Searle, and Williamson jointly.
invariants: never confuse projection with space, representation with knowledge, or assessment with reality

rows.anchor: Sₜᴬ = commitments + entitlements + inferred consequences + challenges + dependencies + provenance + context + participant perspective
rows.statement: The 'state of knowledge at time t' (S_t^A) is enriched from 'facts known by A' to commitments + entitlements + inferred consequences + challenges + dependencies + provenance + context + participant perspective — the state is not merely what is stored but what the participant is committed to, entitled to claim, and what inferential consequences follow from that position.

lineage_claims.quote: Now we can make it richer.

rows.anchor: the same sentence can have different inferential significance for different speakers because their background commitments differ.
rows.statement: Brandom explains how different-participant projections (S_t^A != S_t^B != S_t^G, all oriented toward the same infinite Knowledge Space) can differ: different participants have different collateral commitments, so the same proposition P has different inferential significance for Alice/Bob/AI while sharing the concept — this is described as almost exactly the Knowledge Projection idea.

rows.anchor: "Knowledge is a position in a dynamically changing, socially and objectively constrained space of commitments, contents, evidence, inferences and actions."
rows.statement: Final Zero-Lens result of this document: the model moves from 'Knowledge is a thing we store' toward 'Knowledge is a position in a dynamically changing, socially and objectively constrained space of commitments, contents, evidence, inferences and actions', with KnowledgeOS as 'the substrate that preserves and makes explicit the structure and history of those positions and their relationships to the wider Knowledge Space.' Next proposed test: whether Commitment + Content + Inferential Relations + Entitlement + Context + Time + Participant survives the same Merricks non-redundancy and Zero-Lens tests against real KnowledgeOS episodes, to potentially yield a minimal Kernel rather than another large philosophical ontology.

rows.anchor: Knowledge, as modeled by KnowledgeOS, is a bounded, time-dependent epistemic state of a participant or collective...
rows.statement: Refined working definitions: Knowledge is a bounded, time-dependent epistemic state of a participant or collective, oriented toward a part of the unbounded Knowledge Space, represented by commitments, observations, assumptions, rules, available alternatives, evidential support, inferential consequences, and applicable uncertainties under an explicitly declared epistemic regime — the representation is not identical to knowledge itself. Knowledge Space is the unbounded space of entities, states, events, concepts, relations, institutional structures, propositions, explanations and possible connections toward which finite participants orient observation/reasoning. The KnowledgeOS Kernel is the domain-independent preservation substrate making bounded knowledge projections reconstructible (identity, context, boundary, participant, time, inputs/observations, content references, commitments/assessments, provenance, relations, conflicts, transitions, history), leaving semantics/reasoning to explicit external epistemic regimes.

rows.anchor: Knowledge is always knowledge-at-a-time within an evolving Knowledge Space.
rows.statement: C-15 (a formal Kernel candidate about retraction) is reframed: rather than 'Knowledge can be retracted', the deeper model is 'Knowledge is always knowledge-at-a-time within an evolving Knowledge Space.' A projection is a view/selection of the evolving space at a point in time per perspective/purpose/agent/context; 'Knowledge X was true/justified at T1' does not necessarily imply 'X must remain true/usable at T2' — historical knowledge doesn't disappear, a later projection simply doesn't contain it as currently applicable.

rows.anchor: ### KnowledgeCore ... ### Projection ... ### Knowledge Space ... ### Kernel
rows.statement: Proposed four-part separation: KnowledgeCore protects identity, justification, admissibility, epistemic history, continuity; Projection answers 'what knowledge is relevant/visible/applicable from this perspective at this time?'; Knowledge Space represents the broader evolving space in which knowledge exists and changes; Kernel protects the fundamental epistemic guarantees without becoming the entire cognitive system. Illustrated with an AI system example: 09:00 projection 'customer is eligible' vs 14:00 projection 'customer is not currently eligible' after new evidence, without erasing the 09:00 knowledge — described as closer to a 'persistent epistemic brain' than a simple CRUD knowledge base.

rows.anchor: We cannot quantify "how much of the infinite Knowledge Space we know." We can quantify: **coverage of a declared finite inquiry boundary.**
rows.statement: Coverage(K,C)=|relevant elements represented/assessed|/|Ω_C| is only meaningful relative to a declared finite scope Ω_C; since the full Knowledge Space Ω is infinite, |K|/|Ω| is explicitly stated to be useless — coverage of a declared finite inquiry boundary is the defensible quantity, not coverage of the infinite space itself.

type_signature.domain: knowledge state K, declared scope C

invariants: coverage can only be measured against a declared finite boundary, never against the infinite Knowledge Space itself

rows.anchor: ### External adequacy ... ### Predictive adequacy ... ### Refinement stability
rows.statement: Since d(K,Ω) cannot be computed directly (Ω is not a finite reference set), proposes three orientation-toward-the-infinite-Knowledge-Space proxies: External adequacy (independent verification success), Predictive adequacy (Pr[prediction correct]), and Refinement stability (as scope C1⊂C2⊂C3 expands, does d(Projection(C1), Restriction(Projection(C2),C1))→0?) — called a candidate formalization of 'serve the nature of the Knowledge Space'.

rows.anchor: A knowledge element is a context- and time-bounded epistemic unit consisting of a proposition or meaningful content attributed to a participant...
rows.statement: Final working (not philosophically final) definitions: a knowledge element is a context/time-bounded epistemic unit (proposition/content attributed to a participant, with provenance, evidential basis, inferential/deontic relationships, assumptions, current epistemic assessment under a declared regime); a knowledge state is the evolving collection/relational configuration of such elements available at a point in time; the Knowledge Space is the unbounded space toward which finite states are oriented, which KnowledgeOS does not contain but preserves structures to reconstruct/compare finite projections of; the Kernel is the minimal preservation substrate for those projections and histories, with mathematical/statistical quantification belonging to external epistemic/analytical regimes. Recommends stopping the search for a single 'knowledge quantity' in favor of designing a Knowledge Measurement Vector + Knowledge State Distance + Projection Refinement test.

rows.anchor: There may be an **infinite number of propositions believed, while only a finite number are ever represented**; reasoning bridges the gap between what is represented and what is believed.
rows.statement: Treated as a major direct support for the infinite Knowledge Space hypothesis: R_t^A ⊂ K_t^A ⊂ Ω where Ω=unbounded Knowledge Space, K_t^A=what participant A believes/knows at time t, R_t^A=what is explicitly represented, with |R_t^A|<|K_t^A|<|Ω| as conceptual (not literal measurable) cardinality comparisons; reasoning bridges the gap between what is represented and what is believed, adding a REPRESENTATION and REASONING layer between the infinite space and the epistemic state.

rows.anchor: d(\mu_{B_1},Restriction(\mu_{B_2},B_1)) should be small if the model is structurally stable.
rows.statement: Since distance(μ_A,Ω) cannot be measured directly (Ω unbounded, not fully known), proposes measuring 'convergence under refinement': for increasingly detailed regions B1⊂B2⊂B3 with projections μ_B1,μ_B2,μ_B3, examine d(μ_B1, Restriction(μ_B2,B1)) — should be small if the model is structurally stable, giving 'projection coherence under expansion', proposed as one of the best mathematical interpretations of 'serving the nature of the Knowledge Space.' Final knowledge-quality vector Q_K=(Coverage,Evidence,Consistency,Stability,Alignment,Relevance,ExplanatoryGain,PredictiveAccuracy) replacing a single KnowledgeQuality=0.8 scalar, plus a Utility(B)=∫_B r(x)dμ(x) making importance question-relative and context-relative rather than a fixed topic score.

rows.anchor: Knowledge is a participant- and context-relative epistemic relation/state directed toward an unbounded Knowledge Space. A finite participant forms a capacity-bounded projection from its available information, interpretations, inferences and context.
rows.statement: Final recommended formulation of this document: Knowledge is a participant- and context-relative epistemic relation/state directed toward an unbounded Knowledge Space; a finite participant forms a capacity-bounded projection from available information/interpretations/inferences/context; the projection evolves over time (expand/revise/contract/transform); measured properties under explicit regimes do not constitute knowledge itself. Knowledge Space is the structured domain of entities/events/states/concepts/propositions/relations/institutional structures toward which knowledge can be directed, not identified with any single epistemic or probabilistic model. KnowledgeOS is the preservation and projection infrastructure recording identities/contexts/boundaries/observations/provenance/relations/information-histories/transitions required to reconstruct participants' engagements with the Knowledge Space, while external regimes derive projections/measurements/decisions. The filtering regime E[X_t|ℱ_t^A] is then 'one fully rigorous specialized KnowledgeOS regime', not the whole framework.

rows.anchor: Knowledge is a factive epistemic relation between a participant and domain content, represented within an evolving epistemic state and situated in a context and time. The relation is not reducible to any single representation, probability, measurement, inference rule, or mathematical model.
rows.statement: Final capstone definitions: Knowledge is a factive epistemic relation between a participant and domain content, represented within an evolving epistemic state, situated in a context and time, not reducible to any single representation/probability/measurement/inference-rule/mathematical-model. Knowledge Space is a structured, potentially unbounded semantic domain toward which knowledge can be directed. A Knowledge Projection is a bounded representation of a participant's epistemic state over a selected region of Knowledge Space under a specified context and regime. KnowledgeOS is infrastructure preserving relational/temporal/provenance structure from which epistemic states and knowledge attributions can be reconstructed, while external regimes equip that structure with appropriate mathematics. The Kernel is the smallest domain-independent bounded context that owns identity/lifecycle/provenance of knowledge-bearing participants, content references, information histories, contexts, epistemic states, knowledge attributions, and transitions — not everything needed to calculate knowledge, not a universal ontology, not a measure space, not an AI reasoning engine.

lexical.anchor: the real ownership map is the space map

formal.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in

rationale_evidence.anchor: Kinds the candidates missed but the passes repeatedly found: PURPOSE · CONTAINER · PROJECTION
rationale_evidence.statement: Three additional kinds were repeatedly found by the passes but missing from the A-G candidate list: PURPOSE (mission/vision, found twice in the Relationship Ontology), CONTAINER (Knowledge Space — declared boundary, nesting), and PROJECTION (derived, operating in production).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Classification — every gap from the projection ... G-1..G-5
rationale_evidence.statement: Five gaps classified by category (Structural/Behavioral/Evolutionary) and cause: G-1 (I-4/ATTESTS/PROJECTION inert-vs-attested) is EVOLUTIONARY, caused by a missing lifecycle, belongs to LIFECYCLE. G-2 (SPECIALIZES, Engineering Knowledge -> product knowledge) is EVOLUTIONARY, a missing relationship, belongs to ONTOLOGY. G-3 (external authority/CONSTRAINS) is BEHAVIORAL, a missing relationship (obligation != ownership), belongs to GOVERNANCE. G-4 (PRODUCT vs DEPLOYMENT/INSTANTIATES) is STRUCTURAL but dissolves: a deployment is a nested Knowledge Space, so it belongs to ONTOLOGY as resolved, no new concept. G-5 (Runtime Adapter disappeared in both new domains) is STRUCTURAL but is a confirmation of Hexagonal behaving correctly, not a failure.

rationale_evidence.anchor: G-4 answers H-3 — the nesting question — using evidence rather than preference: Knowledge Spaces NEST, and a deployment is the nested case
rationale_evidence.statement: H-3 (the nesting question) is answered by G-4: Knowledge Spaces nest, and a deployment is the nested case. No new concept was introduced; the ontology already explained the evidence, which is the test the commission set.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge-concern vs platform-concern -- candidate split (evidence/finding, NOT decided)
rationale_evidence.statement: Candidate split (not decided): Knowledge concern (BC-1 NOT BUILT; Knowledge Engineer adopted-role-only); Assurance concern (BC-3/BC-4, partial/missing); Platform/mechanical concern (BC-7, workflow engine, registry -- fully implemented, A); Communication concern (C-10 NOT ESTABLISHED, C-19 stewardship, Communication Engineer nervous-system framing in unadopted history -- F/G). OQ-D (the EKP/PKS boundary) is explicitly OPEN -- deliberately not decided.
