rationale_evidence.statement: Brandom explains how different-participant projections (S_t^A != S_t^B != S_t^G, all oriented toward the same infinite Knowledge Space) can differ: different participants have different collateral commitments, so the same proposition P has different inferential significance for Alice/Bob/AI while sharing the concept — this is described as almost exactly the Knowledge Projection idea.

sources.note: Step 132's Design-Mode-to-Evidence-Mode reconstruction methodology: five current-state categories, per-capability current/target/evidence/status matrix, evidence-strength hierarchy, four-way FACT/DERIVED/HYPOTHESIS/TARGET claim discipline, seven delta categories (including INVESTIGATE to prevent premature INTRODUCE), and the never-introduce-without-searching rule.

rows.anchor: Evidence before Architecture Claims
rows.statement: States the governing rule for this phase, 'Evidence before Architecture Claims,' and defines five current-state categories (Existing/Partial/Missing/Misaligned/Unknown) plus a five-question reconstruction model per capability (what should exist=target, what actually exists=current, what proves it=evidence, does it conform=assessment, what must happen next=delta), emphasizing an architecture statement without evidence is only a hypothesis.

rows.anchor: | Capability | Target | Current | Evidence | Status |
rows.statement: Presents a deliberately conservative Current->Target matrix across thirteen capabilities (Knowledge model, Provenance, Governance, Evidence, Assurance, Agent integration, Agent memory, Registry, Hooks, Context construction, Authorization, Runtime evidence, Assurance graph), most marked Unknown/Partial pending reconstruction, and lists known existing mechanisms (AI Engineering Platform, KnowledgeOS/EKS, governance mechanisms, registry, hooks, .claude/, .codex/, .claude/memory/, AGENTS.md, deterministic assurance, session/change logging) — the current system is 'not a blank-slate knowledge platform.'

rows.anchor: Registry ≠ AssuranceGraph. Memory ≠ AuthoritativeKnowledge. Hook ≠ Governance. Check ≠ CompleteAssuranceModel.
rows.statement: Warns that the presence of mechanisms does not mean the target architecture is fully implemented — a registry is not automatically an assurance graph, memory is not automatically authoritative knowledge, a hook is not automatically governance, a check is not automatically a complete assurance model — the actual semantics must be established.

rows.anchor: Does .claude/ own knowledge, or does it point to knowledge?
rows.statement: Defines per-component reconstruction targets and their critical tests: repository topology (do application/domain/infrastructure/governance/knowledge/evidence/assurance/agents directories exist — must not be assumed); package boundary tests (Domain->Infrastructure=FAIL if direct/inappropriate; Agent->Domain potentially valid through application contracts; Agent->Database needs scrutiny; Governance->Agent implementation generally suspicious; Assurance->External systems expected through ports/adapters); .claude/ and .codex/ each tested by 'does it own knowledge, or point to knowledge?' with the desired symmetry (.claude/ and .codex/ hold agent behavior/integration, KnowledgeOS holds governed engineering knowledge); AGENTS.md tested against AGENTS.md=Pointer+OperatingContract (not =EnterpriseKnowledgeBase); .claude/memory/ tested by 'what epistemic status does memory have?' (potentially valid: session hints/workflow state/preferences/temporary context/pointers; potentially problematic: authoritative architecture/binding governance decisions/enterprise policies/unverified claims).

rows.anchor: TechnicalRegistry or KnowledgeRegistry or something broader.
rows.statement: Defines the registry reconstruction target (what exactly is registered — repositories/agents/knowledge objects/architecture artifacts/services/policies/tools/checks — determining whether it is a TechnicalRegistry, KnowledgeRegistry, or broader) and the hook reconstruction target (each hook classified by Trigger->Action->Evidence, e.g. Git event->Hook->Validation->Evidence vs. Agent event->Hook->Session logging; a blocking hook is not automatically governance — Hook->Policy traceability is required to know which policy authorizes the block).

rows.anchor: What is checked? Where are the rules defined? Who owns the rules? ... Are failures connected to governance?
rows.statement: Defines the deterministic-assurance reconstruction target via eight questions (what is checked, where rules are defined, who owns them, how results are recorded, whether versioned, whether evidence preserved, reproducibility, connection to governance), distinguishing CollectionOfChecks from AssuranceSystem; provisionally classifies current assurance maturity as AssuranceCapability=Existing/Partial rather than CompleteAssuranceContext, with semantic integration as the missing question; requires the full chain Rule->Checker->Execution->Result->Evidence->Finding as strong evidence of an assurance architecture (a bare 'a checker exists' is weak evidence).

rows.anchor: Existence, SemanticMaturity, Enforcement, Traceability
rows.statement: Defines a four-dimension capability assessment framework (Existence, SemanticMaturity, Enforcement, Traceability) with a worked example table (Agent hooks, Registry, Memory, Assurance checks, Governance decisions, Evidence model, Assurance graph rows), most cells marked '?' pending reconstruction.

rows.anchor: Runtime/Code > Executable Configuration > Tests/Checks > Structured Data > Architecture Documents > Narrative Statements.
rows.statement: Defines an evidence-strength hierarchy for current-state claims (documents remain important, but the stronger the claim, the stronger the required evidence should be).

rows.anchor: FACT / DERIVED / HYPOTHESIS / TARGET
rows.statement: Defines a four-way architecture-claim classification (FACT: directly observed; DERIVED: logically derived from observed facts; HYPOTHESIS: architectural interpretation requiring validation; TARGET: desired future architecture), worked example — FACT '.claude/ contains a memory directory,' DERIVED 'Claude has persistent local memory mechanisms,' HYPOTHESIS 'the memory mechanism is intended as non-authoritative context,' TARGET 'all authoritative engineering knowledge should resolve through KnowledgeOS' — preventing accidental blending of current and target architecture.

rows.anchor: KEEP, STRENGTHEN, REFACTOR, INTRODUCE, REMOVE, REPLACE, INVESTIGATE
rows.statement: Defines seven current-to-target delta categories; specifically warns that uncertainty (e.g. 'the registry might already provide evidence lineage') should be marked INVESTIGATE, not prematurely INTRODUCE EvidenceSystem — we should not turn uncertainty into architecture work prematurely.

rows.anchor: Repository → Modules/Packages → Data Model → APIs → Agent Harnesses → Hooks → Registry → Assurance → Governance → Integrations → Runtime → Current Architecture → Target Delta
rows.statement: Defines the safest architecture-reconstruction sequence (repository first, target delta last) to prevent designing features that already exist, reframing the central question from 'what should KnowledgeOS be' to 'how much of the target is already present, under what names, with what guarantees' — the actual archaeology problem; gives an expected-output reconstruction-matrix template (target capability / existing implementation / evidence / architectural assessment / delta).

rows.anchor: Never introduce a target component merely because its conceptual counterpart has not yet been found.
rows.statement: States the architecture-reconstruction rule: first determine whether a component exists under another name before introducing it as new, particularly important because the platform evolved incrementally.

rows.anchor: Design Mode → Evidence Mode
rows.statement: Step 132 verdict: the reconstruction formally switches from Design Mode to Evidence Mode (Current->Evidence->Assessment->Delta->Target), since the target architecture is now sufficiently developed to serve as a reference model.

rows.anchor: WHAT EXISTS TODAY vs WHAT THE TARGET ARCHITECTURE REQUIRES.
rows.statement: Reopens Step 132 (Current-State Reconstruction) here, listing a fifteen-item inspection scope (repository/package structure, .claude/, .codex/, AGENTS.md, registry, governance artifacts, hooks, deterministic assurance, memory, persistence, APIs, integration boundaries, existing context/knowledge model, evidence model, current deployment) producing a Current->Target Architecture Delta Matrix classified Already Exists/Partially Exists/Missing/Architecturally Wrong/Unknown — this preview is elaborated in full detail in the separately-processed Step 132 file (S1031).

rows.anchor: CURRENT ≠ TARGET. FACT/DERIVED/HYPOTHESIS/TARGET/UNKNOWN.
rows.statement: Restates the CURRENT/TARGET/DELTA/CONFIDENCE reconstruction format and the five-way claim classification, requiring FACT->DERIVED chains while HYPOTHESIS cannot become CURRENT without evidence.

rows.anchor: AgentRuntimeContext ⊃ RepositoryArtifacts — desirable for reproducible agent behavior, not inherently wrong.
rows.statement: Current-state observation 1: the agent integration layer is already repository-local, which is desirable for reproducibility; the architectural question is what those artifacts are allowed to own, not whether they exist.

rows.anchor: Same semantic contract ≠ same technical implementation.
rows.statement: Current-state observation 2: Claude (.claude/) and Codex (.codex/) are evolving toward symmetry, technically different but consuming the same KnowledgeOS authority.

rows.anchor: AGENTS.md → KnowledgeOS → Authoritative Knowledge (not AGENTS.md → KnowledgeOS replacement).
rows.statement: Current-state observation 3: AGENTS.md functions as an important agent entry/pointer mechanism with high architectural value, provided it points to rather than replaces KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: Agent Contextual Memory unless a governed promotion mechanism explicitly elevates a memory item.
rows.statement: Current-state observation 4: .claude/memory/ gives agents cross-session persistence, but its semantic status must remain Agent Contextual Memory absent explicit governed promotion.

rows.anchor: Rule → Checker → Result already exists; the architecture has not evolved around LLM → judgment.
rows.statement: Current-state observation 5, called 'one of the most significant findings': the platform already contains deterministic assurance mechanisms, a strong foundation for the target Assurance Context.

rows.anchor: Session/change logging is an existing bridge between AgentExecution and EngineeringChange — we do not need to invent agent-action traceability from zero.
rows.statement: Current-state observation 6: the remaining question is whether existing records have sufficient semantic identity and provenance.

rows.anchor: RegistryExists — its semantic maturity remains to be measured; must not yet classify it as the Assurance Graph.
rows.statement: Current-state observation 7: the registry provides structured identification/discovery but should not be prematurely equated with the Assurance Graph.

rows.anchor: Which semantics are encoded only in documents, and which are machine-addressable?
rows.statement: Current-state observation 8: KnowledgeOS already contains governance-oriented artifacts (constitution, conventions, standards, landscape, decisions, review/verdict artifacts), significantly document-oriented — not inherently a weakness, but raising the machine-addressability question.

rows.anchor: Governance documents, Architecture artifacts, Agent memory, Repository instructions, Registry, Verification results, Session logs, Engineering source → Knowledge fragmentation.
rows.statement: Current-state observation 9: eight distinct knowledge-bearing surfaces exist, creating a central architectural risk of knowledge fragmentation.

rows.anchor: AGENTS.md = How to interact; Architecture Constitution = What is governed. Fragmentation ≠ Duplication.
rows.statement: Clarifies fragmentation does not automatically mean duplication — two artifacts mentioning the same rules can have distinct responsibilities; the problem occurs only when both become competing authorities, posing the current authority question 'which source wins when two knowledge-bearing artifacts disagree?' — absent a machine-enforceable answer, this is AuthorityAmbiguity, a current-state finding unless governance evidence proves otherwise.

rows.anchor: Governed Authority → Authoritative Knowledge → Verified Evidence → Derived Knowledge → Agent Context → Agent Local Memory. Lower-level context cannot silently override higher-level authority.
rows.statement: Proposes a target six-level authority hierarchy with the key principle that lower-level context cannot silently override higher-level authority, to be formalized precisely later.

rows.anchor: | Capability | CURRENT | TARGET | DELTA |
rows.statement: Presents the first Current->Target delta matrix across 14 capabilities (agent local instructions, Claude/Codex integration, agent memory, registry, governance artifacts, deterministic checks, session/change logging, evidence, verification, cross-context graph, authority model, context generation, action authorization), each marked Exists/Partial with a specific delta action (constrain, normalize, formalize, connect, introduce, centralize, verify).

rows.anchor: Formalize semantic authority and relationships — not 'build a graph database.'
rows.statement: States the most important delta item is formalizing semantic authority/relationships, not building a graph database (the graph is merely an implementation mechanism for navigability).

rows.anchor: Semantic fragmentation + Insufficient explicit relationships + Inconsistent authority boundaries — not Missing platform.
rows.statement: Concludes the existing ecosystem already has Knowledge+Governance+Assurance+AgentIntegration+EvidenceLikeRecords — the problem is better framed as semantic fragmentation, insufficient explicit relationships, and inconsistent authority boundaries, not a missing platform.

rows.anchor: Current-state capability map: Governance/Agent Platform/Assurance → Registry/Logging → Engineering. What is less explicit is the semantic graph connecting them.
rows.statement: Presents a current-state capability map diagram, concluding the explicit semantic graph connecting the pieces is what is missing, with current relationships implicitly represented via filenames/directory structure/references/conventions/Git history/scripts/human knowledge rather than as explicit, machine-addressable relationships (e.g. current: 'ADR-42.md references Rule-17.md' vs target: 'D42 -governs-> R17').

rows.anchor: Use the graph for authority/relationship facts; use the LLM for reasoning.
rows.statement: States LLM inference over documents is probabilistic while a governed graph relationship is explicit, giving the principle 'use the graph for authority/relationship facts; use the LLM for reasoning'; formalizes target context construction C=Filter(G,Task,Actor,Scope,Time,Authority), the agent receiving C, not everything.

rows.anchor: Current: Rule/check/script → PASS/FAIL. Target: Governed Rule → Checker → Verification → Evidence → Finding → Governance disposition. Delta is primarily semantic integration.
rows.statement: Presents current->target comparison diagrams for assurance (delta = semantic integration, not replacement), evidence (currently distributed across logs/Git/CI/scripts/sessions/documents; target is an Evidence Context with source/provenance/timestamp/actor/subject/integrity, achieved via evidence federation — ExternalEvidence->EvidenceReference rather than copying everything, e.g. Evidence E91 referencing an external Git commit), governance (current: decision document; target: Decision with identity/authority/lifecycle/validity/relationships/document projection, the document becoming a representation rather than the only machine-readable form), registry (evolving into an identity foundation with capability/ownership/lifecycle/graph references rather than being replaced), memory (Memory->Candidate knowledge->Evidence->Verification->Governed knowledge, a controlled promotion path), and logging (Session->Action->Evidence->Verification->Graph, the log becoming part of the semantic evidence chain).

rows.anchor: Centralize authority, not necessarily execution.
rows.statement: States what should centralize is Authority/Identity/Governance/Evidence/Cross-context relationships/High-risk authorization, not all execution — preserving the edge architecture's fast-feedback strength (local: fast feedback, agent integration, working memory, source code, tests, developer tooling; central: authority, governance, knowledge, evidence, assurance, authorization, graph); identifies the major current weakness as 'agent context can be assembled from heterogeneous sources without a universal authority model' — exactly what the Context Service should solve, requiring every high-value context item to carry Source/Authority/Validity/Evidence and a six-value status (AUTHORITATIVE/VERIFIED/OBSERVED/DERIVED/LOCAL/UNKNOWN).

rows.anchor: One semantic authority per concept. Every material relationship must be explicit and addressable. Every material engineering action must be traceable to context, authorization, and evidence. Agent memory is contextual unless explicitly promoted. Deterministic verification outranks probabilistic inference where mechanically verifiable. Derived projections must not become competing sources of truth.
rows.statement: States six first target-architecture principles derived from the archaeology, consolidating prior invariants (source-of-truth, explicit relationships, action traceability, memory-promotion, deterministic-precedence, projection-non-authority) into a single archaeology-derived list.

rows.anchor: Existing KnowledgeOS/EKS + Semantic Formalization + Authority Model + Evidence Integration + Assurance Graph.
rows.statement: Step 142 verdict: rejects 'current platform -> completely new architecture' in favor of an evolutionary model (existing platform plus semantic formalization, authority model, evidence integration, and assurance graph).

rationale_evidence.statement: Current-state observation 8: KnowledgeOS already contains governance-oriented artifacts (constitution, conventions, standards, landscape, decisions, review/verdict artifacts), significantly document-oriented — not inherently a weakness, but raising the machine-addressability question.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Governance documents, Architecture artifacts, Agent memory, Repository instructions, Registry, Verification results, Session logs, Engineering source → Knowledge fragmentation.
rationale_evidence.statement: Current-state observation 9: eight distinct knowledge-bearing surfaces exist, creating a central architectural risk of knowledge fragmentation.

rationale_evidence.anchor: AGENTS.md = How to interact; Architecture Constitution = What is governed. Fragmentation ≠ Duplication.
rationale_evidence.statement: Clarifies fragmentation does not automatically mean duplication — two artifacts mentioning the same rules can have distinct responsibilities; the problem occurs only when both become competing authorities, posing the current authority question 'which source wins when two knowledge-bearing artifacts disagree?' — absent a machine-enforceable answer, this is AuthorityAmbiguity, a current-state finding unless governance evidence proves otherwise.

aliases: Dynamic Epistemic Logic of Questions and Inquiry (thesis) as a KnowledgeOS research lens

sources.note: An external formal-logic thesis on questions/issues (model M=<W,approx,sim,V> with a separate issue relation approx and epistemic indistinguishability sim) read as a structural (not adopted) source proposing KnowledgeState != InquiryState, ZoomIn as issue refinement, ZoomIn != FactFinding as independently motivated by 'questioning actions do not themselves give information', order-sensitive/non-commutative composition of questioning actions, and a behavioral-equivalence-first strategy relevant to the unresolved KnowledgeOS equiv_sem problem. Proposes KR-DELQ-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 with six research questions. NOTE (batch B0068, verified against later S2856): the source volume is subsequently identified as misattributed at some point in this thread (a 'source-misattribution-correction-the-volume-is-minica-not-sher' file appears later in this same batch, S2856) -- flagged here for cross-reference; this file's own attribution to 'Minica' is stated directly in-file and not contradicted within S2846 itself.

rows.anchor: M = <W,approx,sim,V> ... approx: issue/question relation, sim: epistemic indistinguishability, V: valuation ... KnowledgeState != InquiryState, or more precisely K_t != QState_t.
rows.statement: Reads the thesis's core model M=<W,approx,sim,V> (a possible-worlds model with a distinct issue/question relation approx and an epistemic-indistinguishability relation sim) as structural support for KnowledgeState != InquiryState (K_t != QState_t), where K_t is what the system currently represents/attributes and QState_t is what is currently being investigated and which alternatives/questions are active; proposes a richer Inquiry = Question + IssueStructure + EpistemicState + Purpose/Contract in place of a bare tuple Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma,Sigma).

lineage_claims.target: an external DEL-of-questions thesis, attributed in-file to 'Minica'
lineage_claims.quote: I read the attached ... book is much more important for KnowledgeOS than merely as inspiration for Zoom-In.

rows.anchor: ZoomIn approx Issue Refinement -- not as an identity, but as a research hypothesis. ... questioning actions ... do not themselves give information immediately; they raise/manage issues ... almost exactly our ZF5: ZoomIn != FactFinding
rows.statement: Proposes ZoomIn approx Issue Refinement as a research hypothesis (not identity), and reports that the thesis's characterization of questioning actions as knowledge-seeking actions that do not themselves supply information gives an external theoretical analogue for the already-adopted ZF5 (ZoomIn != FactFinding) and DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination.

rows.anchor: There is no question composition principle ... sequential questioning can produce structures that cannot be represented by one equivalent question. ... Dynamic questioning systems exhibit order-sensitive composition ... KnowledgeOS inquiry operations may require order-sensitive semantics.
rows.statement: Reports the thesis's finding that many apparent composition laws fail for questioning actions (sequence order matters; no general question-composition principle exists) as an external research precedent for taking non-commutativity of KnowledgeOS inquiry operations seriously, connecting to the corpus's own empirical Zero(C1oC2)!=Zero(C2oC1) findings, while explicitly refusing to claim the source 'proves' KnowledgeOS non-commutativity ([EXT] dynamic questioning systems exhibit order-sensitive composition -> [PROP] KnowledgeOS inquiry operations may require order-sensitive semantics).

rows.anchor: Define observable/question-relevant behavior first -> define equivalence -> minimize structure. ... That does not solve KnowledgeOS semantic equivalence. But it gives us a very strong research direction.
rows.statement: Extracts a three-step methodological pattern from the thesis's behavioral-equivalence-then-minimization work (define observable/question-relevant behavior first, then define equivalence, then minimize structure) as a candidate strategy relevant to the corpus's unresolved semantic equivalence (equiv_sem) and capability-preorder (<=_cap) problem, explicitly not itself a solution.

rows.anchor: KR-DELQ-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 ... Issue/Knowledge Separation ... Question as State-Changing Object ... Issue Refinement ... Resolution ... Inquiry Composition ... Behavioral Equivalence ... Inquiry Strategy -> Epistemic Agency
rows.statement: Proposes KR-DELQ-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 with six research questions (issue/knowledge separation; question as state-changing object; issue refinement for Zoom-In; determination as contract-relative issue resolution; inquiry-operation commutativity; question-relative behavioral equivalence contributing to equiv_sem) plus a seventh bridge Inquiry Strategy -> Epistemic Agency via the thesis's local-property querying-strategy chapter, all tagged [EXT]/[PROP], Theory v1.2 frozen, kernel untouched, no new primitive.

rows.anchor: Epistemic Information != Current Issue/Question Structure ... M = <W,approx,sim,V> ... approx: issue/question relation, representing the alternatives currently relevant to investigation.
rows.statement: States the thesis's central distinction Epistemic Information != Current Issue/Question Structure via the model M=<W,approx,sim,V> (possible worlds W, epistemic indistinguishability sim, issue/question relation approx representing alternatives currently relevant to investigation, valuation V), extremely close to the corpus's own emerging Zoom-In problem.

rows.anchor: soft announcements that cut epistemic links while keeping the whole model available for further reference ... contrasted with eliminative announcements. ... Focus != Delete ... Inquiry transformation != Knowledge destruction.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's 'soft announcement' operator (cuts epistemic links while keeping the whole model available, contrasted with eliminative announcements) as an established formal precedent closely resembling the corpus's own ZF1 (Focus != Delete, Inquiry transformation != Knowledge destruction), explicitly not treated as proof of ZF1 within KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: Question and resolution are different operations ... Question changes the issue structure. Resolution changes the epistemic relation in response to the issue. ... Yes: K_b phi, No: K_b neg phi, Don'tKnow: neg K_b phi and neg K_b neg phi. ... Question Raised not-implies Knowledge Acquired.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's Question != Resolution separation (question changes issue structure, resolution changes the epistemic relation) and its tripartite answer structure (Yes: K_b(phi); No: K_b(not-phi); Don'tKnow: not-K_b(phi) and not-K_b(not-phi), a legitimate epistemic outcome, not an error) as external formal support for the corpus's own ZoomIn!=FactFinding->Determination pipeline and for Question Raised does not imply Knowledge Acquired / Discovery of an Issue does not imply Determination -- described as almost exactly the Case B witness already designed for KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01, while warning not to copy the three-valued structure directly into KnowledgeOS.
invariants: Question Raised does not imply Knowledge Acquired

rows.anchor: a candidate may be excluded only when the local property provides a justified reason that it cannot be a solution. ... SearchSpaceReduction != ArbitraryCandidateDeletion. ... Excludes(h | E,Q,C,S,R) with a warrant for exclusion. ... Zero != SearchPruning.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's query-strategy safety condition (a candidate may be excluded from the search space only when a local property provides a justified reason it cannot be a solution) to propose Excludes(h|E,Q,C,S,R) with an explicit exclusion warrant, giving SearchSpaceReduction != ArbitraryCandidateDeletion; separates this Query Strategy/SearchPruning question ('which parts of the search space can safely be ignored while preserving the possibility of finding the solution') from the Zero Lens question ('can this structure be eliminated while preserving the contract'), Zero != SearchPruning, with only a possible (not assumed) relation Zero -> Safe Reduction -> Query Strategy under a suitable contract.

type_signature.domain: hypothesis h, evidence E, inquiry Q, context C, standard S, regime R

missing: formal relation between Zero and Query Strategy

rows.anchor: ordinary bisimulation was insufficient ... developed a richer behavioral equivalence -- intersection bisimulation/intersimulation -- to preserve exactly the distinctions relevant to the language. ... Define observable language -> define behavioral equivalence -> minimize while preserving it. ... Truth preservation != Full semantic preservation.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's discovery that ordinary bisimulation was insufficient (it could erase strategically relevant information while preserving modal truth) and its development of a richer intersimulation/intersection-bisimulation equivalence, as a concrete formal precedent for the corpus's unresolved equiv_sem problem and kernel-minimality programme (Define observable language -> define behavioral equivalence -> minimize while preserving it), giving Truth preservation != Full semantic preservation and Observable equivalence depends on what the observer/contract can observe, reinforcing 'minimality is semantic, not syntactic.'

rows.anchor: Which source should be queried? ... different information sources, including agents and objective sources/oracles ... SourceSelection != FactFinding. It is an agency/query-planning decision. ... query-available information can be limited by subjective knowledge, measurement instruments, experimental design, computing power, missing resources ... Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's source-selection and resource-limitation discussion to propose S_t^available={Human,Log,Instrument,Database,Network,Agent,Oracle,...} and SelectSource(Q,K,C,S,R), giving SourceSelection != FactFinding (an agency/query-planning decision) and connecting resource limitations (subjective knowledge, instruments, computing power) to the already-established Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient chain from the Epistemic Agency resource-state work.

rows.anchor: 'Why' questions concern reasons for behavior ... What? -> How? -> Why? -> Why act? ... The last question is already Action Warrant. So this thesis gives additional support for our F_t != W_t != Decision_t.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's identification of 'why' questions (concerning reasons for behavior) as external support connecting to the corpus's Action Fact-Finding work: a What?->How?->Why?->Why-act? hierarchy where the last question is already Action Warrant, reinforcing F_t != W_t != Decision_t.

rows.anchor: a realistic inquiry does not merely contain an unordered set of questions. It maintains a structured agenda whose issues can be raised, resolved, reprioritized, inserted, deleted. ... Inquiry_t = structured, evolving agenda of epistemic issues.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's structured-inquiry-agenda concept (issues can be raised, resolved, reprioritized, inserted, deleted; being good at research includes asking good questions, not only answering them) to propose Inquiry_t as a structured, evolving agenda of epistemic issues rather than a single question Q_t, and recursive sub-question generation Q_0->Q_1,...,Q_n with Q_i->E_i->Q_{i+1}.

rows.anchor: I_t = <Q_t, approx_t, D_t^cand, S_t^source, A_t> ... Factivity Separation: I_t carries no truth assertions ... Non-Destructive Focus: Focus(I_t,w) not-implies w not-in K_t ... State Evolution Autonomy: Delta I_t != empty not-implies Delta K_t != empty (Question Raised not-implies Knowledge Acquired).
rows.statement: Formalizes the candidate Inquiry State schema I_t=(Q_t,approx_t,D_t^cand,S_t^source,A_t) (active question DAG with per-question id/target/status/priority; issue-partitioning relation approx_t over states; candidate dimension set; source-dependency map; inquiry agenda/history) with three explicit separation rules: Factivity Separation (I_t carries no truth assertions), Non-Destructive Focus (focusing does not remove states from K_t), and State Evolution Autonomy (Delta I_t!=empty does not imply Delta K_t!=empty), giving ZF5 a clean formal witness Delta I_t!=empty AND Delta K_t=empty.
invariants: Focus does not imply removal from K_t
Delta I_t != empty does not imply Delta K_t != empty

rows.anchor: ZoomIn: (K_t,I_t,O_t) -> (I_{t+1}, D^cand_{t+1}) ... K_t: Current frozen Epistemic State (Unmutated). ... KR-DYNAMIC-QUESTION-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 ... DQ1 ... DQ5 ... Does KnowledgeOS require a distinct evolving Inquiry State in order to model fact-finding correctly?
rows.statement: Finalizes the ZoomIn operational interface as ZoomIn:(K_t,I_t,O_t)->(I_{t+1},D^cand_{t+1}) leaving K_t unmutated, with a five-step execution sequence (trigger binding, issue-structure restructuring via soft update, candidate dimension discovery, agenda/sub-question generation, source-dependency assignment feeding downstream FactFinding); registers KR-DYNAMIC-QUESTION-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 with DQ1-DQ5 (is a dedicated I_t strictly required; how do soft issue updates re-partition alternatives without destroying context; can safe candidate pruning be bounded by exclusion warrants; how does intersimulation bound equiv_sem minimality; how should hierarchical agendas manage recursive sub-questions); poses the deeper research question of whether KnowledgeOS requires a distinct evolving Inquiry State to model fact-finding correctly, while explicitly keeping KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 as the sole active experiment and using this thesis only as an interpretive lens for its results.

rows.anchor: The attached book is not Gila Sher's Epistemic Friction. It is Stefan A. Minica's 2011 PhD thesis, Dynamic-Epistemic Logic of Questions and Inquiry. The file itself identifies that title and author... The previous Sher attribution should therefore not be carried forward for this file.
rows.statement: Self-declared source-attribution correction (extracted here as a claim, per the corpus's standing rule that self-declared statuses require independent verification rather than acceptance on citation): the volume most recently analyzed in the preceding thread, previously attributed to Gila Sher's Epistemic Friction, is stated to actually be Stefan A. Minica's 2011 PhD thesis Dynamic-Epistemic Logic of Questions and Inquiry, identified from the file's own title page and Chapter 2 heading; the prior Sher attribution is explicitly withdrawn for this file going forward.
missing: independent verification of the correction beyond the source's own self-report

lineage_claims.quote: The previous Sher attribution should therefore not be carried forward for this file.

rows.anchor: R = sim intersect approx ... What remains possible when we consider both what the agent cannot distinguish and what the current issue considers relevant. ... this intersection is not reducible to either relation alone. ... A_t^rel = A_t^epi intersect A_t^issue.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's intersection relation R=sim∩approx (what remains possible given both epistemic indistinguishability and current issue relevance, not reducible to either relation alone) as inspiration for a candidate A_t^rel=A_t^epi ∩ A_t^issue representing currently relevant epistemic alternatives that must actually be investigated, tagged [PROP].
missing: formal definition of A_t^epi and A_t^issue

rows.anchor: Known != Issue != Candidate != Determined ... A gap is not necessarily simply 'something missing.' It can be an unresolved issue over a structured set of alternatives. ... Issue(Q,K_t) = partition/distinction structure over admissible alternatives.
rows.statement: Extracts a four-way separation Known != Issue != Candidate != Determined from the thesis's formulas distinguishing facts neither known nor settled that would become known upon resolution, warning that the corpus's existing Gap concept risks carrying too much responsibility (a gap can be an unresolved issue over a structured alternative set, not merely 'something missing'), proposing Issue(Q,K_t) as a candidate partition/distinction structure, [PROP] only.

rows.anchor: Questioning != Answering != Resolution which translates very naturally into: ZoomIn != FactFinding != Determination. This is one of the strongest external correspondences we have found so far. But it remains [EXT] -> [PROP], not [PROVED].
rows.statement: States that Minica's Questioning != Answering != Resolution translates naturally into ZoomIn != FactFinding != Determination, describing it as the strongest external correspondence found so far for ZF5, explicitly kept at [EXT]->[PROP], not [PROVED]; separately notes Issue Refinement != Information Elimination reinforces the triad ZoomIn != Zero != FactFinding.

rows.anchor: Minica explicitly demonstrates that many apparently intuitive composition laws for question/announcement actions do not hold... there is no general question-composition principle for the richer system. ... phi?;phi? != phi? in general. ... we explicitly decided not to assume projection properties for Zoom-In. So the book independently reinforces that decision.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's demonstration that composition and iteration are not automatically well-behaved for questioning/announcement actions (sequential compositions are not generally equivalent under swap; asking the same question twice need not equal asking it once, phi?;phi? != phi? in general) as independent external reinforcement of the corpus's own methodological rule (do not infer algebraic laws from intuitive operator meaning; test composition explicitly) and of the earlier decision not to assume idempotence/projection properties for Zoom-In, connecting to the corpus's own Zero(S1) and Zero(S2) not implying Zero(S1 union S2) finding.

rows.anchor: uncertainty about a future answer is predictive uncertainty, not simply lack of observational access to the present/past. ... Predictive Uncertainty != Observational Uncertainty ... We do not yet know whether the next Runner job will produce the traffic spike ... is not the same epistemic state as ... We cannot observe the Runner logs.
rows.statement: Extracts a Predictive Uncertainty != Observational Uncertainty distinction from the thesis's product-update model, extending the corpus's existing Unknown != Unobserved != Unobservable != Underdetermined taxonomy, illustrated by 'we don't know whether the next Runner job will spike traffic' (predictive) versus 'we cannot observe the Runner logs' (observational) being fundamentally different reasons for uncertainty, flagged as potentially important for Action Fact-Finding.

rows.anchor: I_t^a != I_t^b even when K_t^a != K_t^b ... an agent can solve a question by raising it ... An epistemic action can change the information state without directly changing the external system.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's multi-agent extension (each agent has its own epistemic and issue relations; one agent may regard p as an issue while another does not) to propose I_t^a != I_t^b as relevant to distributed fact-finding, testimony, expert agents, privacy, and KnowledgeOS federation; and extracts the 'solving a question by raising it' example (asking a question changes the epistemic situation and can itself provide the answer) to argue an epistemic action can change the information state without changing the external system, motivating the split A_Q^epi (Ask, Measure, Query, Inspect, Request evidence, Challenge, Wait, Investigate further) vs A_Q^domain (Restart, Reconfigure, Deploy, Block, Mitigate, Delete).

rows.anchor: not every question can be asked because of instrument limitations, information-source availability, social conventions, financial resources, procedural constraints. ... Possible Question != Available Question != Executable Investigation. This connects directly to: Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's procedural-information limitations (instrument, source-availability, social, financial, procedural constraints) into Possible Question != Available Question != Executable Investigation, explicitly connected to the already-established Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient chain from the Epistemic Agency resource-state work; uses the classic nine-pearls weighing problem (only certain questions available at each stage, next question depends on previous answer, forming a conditional event tree) as a candidate benchmark for Inquiry Strategy = conditional sequence of epistemic actions, pi:(K_t,I_t)->a_t with a_{t+1}=pi(K_{t+1},I_{t+1}), richer than static NextAction=argmax Utility(a).
invariants: Possible Question != Available Question != Executable Investigation

experiment.hypothesis: Inquiry strategy is better modeled as a conditional sequence of epistemic actions than as static utility-maximizing action selection
experiment.setup: Nine-pearls weighing-problem-style conditional decision tree, adapted as a candidate KnowledgeOS benchmark
experiment.assumptions: Available questions depend on prior answers (procedural constraints)
experiment.method: Not yet executed
experiment.limitations: Purely a proposed future benchmark, not run
experiment.conclusion: Proposed as a possible future KnowledgeOS experiment for Epistemic Agency

rows.anchor: M_{t+1} = M_t (x) gamma_t ... This is an external formal analogue for our K_{t+1} = Theta(K_t,e_{t+1},Q,C,S,M,H,EC). But do not replace Theta with product update. The semantic objects are different.
rows.statement: Draws an explicit (non-identifying) analogy between the thesis's product-update construction M_{t+1}=M_t (x) gamma_t (combining an action structure of possible events, relations, and preconditions with the prior model) and the corpus's existing state-transition function K_{t+1}=Theta(K_t,e_{t+1},Q,C,S,M,H,EC), explicitly warning not to replace Theta with product update since the semantic objects differ, posing instead the research question whether some KnowledgeOS state transitions can be represented as structured epistemic event updates.

rows.anchor: KR-DYNAMIC-QUESTION-INQUIRY-2026-09 ... DQ1 -- Issue/Knowledge Separation ... DQ7 -- Agent-Relative Inquiry ... Knowledge State and Inquiry State are orthogonal dimensions of epistemic organization.
rows.statement: Finalizes KR-DYNAMIC-QUESTION-INQUIRY-2026-09 with seven research questions DQ1-DQ7 (issue/knowledge separation; focus without deletion; questioning dynamics; sequential non-equivalence a;b!=b;a; procedural/conditional inquiry protocols; predictive vs observational uncertainty; agent-relative inquiry I_t^a!=I_t^b), states the candidate principle 'Knowledge State and Inquiry State are orthogonal dimensions of epistemic organization' (K_t=K_t' can hold while I_t!=I_t', and conversely I_t can change while K_t=K_{t+1}), and recommends registering this lens and testing its distinctions rather than altering the active ZF2/ZF3/ZF5 experiment.
invariants: Knowledge State and Inquiry State are orthogonal dimensions of epistemic organization

rows.anchor: the author explicitly distinguishes source relevance from goal/inquiry relevance. A question can be very useful for exploiting an available source but poorly aligned with the overall goal ... SourceRelevance != InquiryRelevance ... ActionFeasibility != EpistemicValue ... GitLab logs: highly source-relevant. But if the question is 'Is Nexus compliant with backup policy?' then GitLab may have low inquiry relevance.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's Chapter 6 warning that source relevance and goal/inquiry relevance are distinct (a question can exploit an available source well while being poorly aligned with the actual goal), giving SourceRelevance != InquiryRelevance and ActionFeasibility != EpistemicValue, illustrated by GitLab logs being highly source-relevant but low-inquiry-relevance for a 'Is Nexus compliant with backup policy?' question, preventing an agent from choosing the easiest evidence source instead of the most relevant one.

rows.anchor: protocols as sets of legal sequences of inquiry actions. A protocol can constrain which questioning actions are available at each stage. ... InquiryProtocol_t with AvailableActions_t = Protocol(K_t,Q_t,C_t).
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's protocol semantics (legal sequences of inquiry actions, constraining availability at each stage) into a candidate InquiryProtocol_t with AvailableActions_t=Protocol(K_t,Q_t,C_t), giving the lifecycle Q_t -> AvailableInquiryActions_t -> Select -> Execute -> Observation -> Update as a stronger foundation for Epistemic Agency than unconstrained 'the AI chooses the next action.'

rows.anchor: the protocol semantics explicitly constructs histories: h = w.sigma where the history contains the initial world and sequence of actions. ... History != Current State ... K_t = K_{t+1} not-implies History_t = History_{t+1}.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's first-class history object h=w.sigma (initial world plus action sequence) as external mathematical support for the corpus's independently-discovered History != Current State distinction and K_t=K_{t+1} does not imply History_t=History_{t+1}, flagged as potentially important for epistemic audit reconstruction.
invariants: K_t = K_{t+1} does not imply History_t = History_{t+1}

rows.anchor: behavioral equivalence is the appropriate invariance notion for its questioning language. ... Define Observable Behavior -> Define Equivalence -> Refine/Minimize. That is precisely the sequence our kernel research is currently missing.
rows.statement: Restates the thesis's behavioral-equivalence-then-minimization methodology (Define Observable Behavior -> Define Equivalence -> Refine/Minimize) as precisely the sequence the corpus's own kernel-minimality research is currently missing for equiv_sem, while explicitly refusing to claim the thesis solves the KnowledgeOS semantic-equivalence problem.

rows.anchor: A property cannot be understood independently of the structure under which it is evaluated. ... Different relations capture different notions of relevance/knowledge/issue structure, and their intersection produces information that neither relation alone captures.
rows.statement: Draws a structural parallel between the thesis's relation-intersection result (different relations capture different notions of relevance/knowledge/issue structure; their intersection captures information neither alone does) and the corpus's own experimentally-discovered context/transformation/preservation-relativity of Zero, generalizing to the methodological principle 'a property cannot be understood independently of the structure under which it is evaluated', explicitly not claiming Zero=R.
invariants: A property cannot be understood independently of the structure under which it is evaluated

rows.anchor: A. Inquiry expansion J_t -> J_{t+1} 'What should we investigate?' B. Candidate expansion H_t -> H_{t+1} 'What explanations become candidates?' C. Knowledge expansion K_t -> K_{t+1} 'What has actually become epistemically established?' These are not the same.
rows.statement: Refines the ZF2/ZF3 'dimension discovery' test into three distinct expansion events: A. Inquiry expansion (J_t->J_{t+1}, what should we investigate), B. Candidate expansion (H_t->H_{t+1}, what explanations become candidates), C. Knowledge expansion (K_t->K_{t+1}, what is actually epistemically established), explicitly stated as not the same and described as the most important architectural insight the book gives for the current Zoom-In work.

rows.anchor: K_t Knowledge/Epistemic State, J_t Issue/Inquiry State, H_Q Hypothesis Space, E_t Evidence State, F_t Determination, AR_t Action Rationale, with J_t != H_Q != E_t != F_t != K_t. ... Can KnowledgeOS formally separate Issue-State dynamics from Epistemic-State dynamics? ... a candidate research object would be I_t = (K_t,J_t,H_Q,E_t,F_t) with transitions.
rows.statement: Proposes six distinct epistemic objects (K_t Knowledge/Epistemic State, J_t Issue/Inquiry State, H_Q Hypothesis Space, E_t Evidence State, F_t Determination, AR_t Action Rationale) with J_t != H_Q != E_t != F_t != K_t, and poses the research question 'Can KnowledgeOS formally separate Issue-State dynamics from Epistemic-State dynamics?' with a candidate composite object mathfrak-I_t=(K_t,J_t,H_Q,E_t,F_t) and transitions J_t-Question->J_{t+1}, J_t-ZoomIn->D^cand_{t+1}, (D^cand,H_Q,E)-FactFind->F_t, F_t-Attribution->K_{t+1}; recommends a formal Issue-State/Epistemic-State separation study as the next research artifact instead of another broad Zoom experiment.
missing: executed experiment testing whether the six objects are actually empirically distinguishable

sources.note: Step 245's fully concrete, worked-example Knowledge State K0=(C0,sigma0,theta0,lambda0,pi0) with C0=(V0,E0) a typed graph instance; independently re-derives the Content/Qualification/Governance decomposition of K5 first proposed in Step 243, proves a restricted closure theorem for T_addObservation under a precondition Pre(K,o), and leaves temporal-validity attachment and lineage direction as explicit open design questions.

rows.anchor: We therefore construct a minimal candidate: K_0=(C_0,Q_0,Gamma_0) where C_0 = content, Q_0 = epistemic qualification, Gamma_0 = governing/contextual qualification. This is a construction hypothesis, not yet the final kernel.
rows.statement: Proposes a minimal candidate Knowledge State as a three-part construction hypothesis K0=(C0,Q0,Gamma0) (content, epistemic qualification, governing/contextual qualification), with the requirement that each component itself receive a mathematical type before further construction.

lineage_claims.quote: We now follow directly from Step 244.

rows.anchor: C_0=(V_0,E_0) ... C_0 in Graph with V_0 subseteq Node and E_0 subseteq Node x RelationType x Node. This gives us a concrete structural representation without yet claiming that all KnowledgeOS knowledge must be a graph.
rows.statement: Defines Content C0=(V0,E0) as a typed graph (V0 subseteq Node, E0 subseteq Node x RelationType x Node), explicitly scoping the claim to 'a concrete structural representation' without asserting that all KnowledgeOS knowledge must be graph-shaped.

rows.anchor: We must not collapse o=p. Instead o in Observation while p in Proposition. And the semantic relation is Supports(o,p). ... Otherwise the theory cannot distinguish 'The proposition is true' from 'We observed evidence supporting the proposition.'
rows.statement: Establishes, via the worked example, that Observation and Proposition must be distinct typed objects related by Supports(o,p) rather than identified (o=p); without this distinction the theory cannot separate 'the proposition is true' from 'evidence was observed supporting the proposition' -- flagged as critical for the later epistemic theory.

rows.anchor: A candidate status space is: Sigma = {Observed, Supported, Inferred, Validated, Rejected, Unknown}. This is not yet accepted as the canonical vocabulary. It is merely a candidate domain derived from the concepts already under reconstruction.
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate 6-value epistemic status space Sigma={Observed, Supported, Inferred, Validated, Rejected, Unknown}, explicitly disclaiming canonical status -- a candidate domain only.

rows.anchor: theta(p) in Interval ... the possibility remains that temporal validity belongs to an assertion instance, rather than to the proposition itself. That distinction must remain open.
rows.statement: Defines temporal validity as theta:Proposition -> Interval (not a scalar), but leaves open whether temporal validity actually belongs to the proposition itself or to a separate 'assertion instance' concept.

rows.anchor: lambda subseteq Artifact x Artifact ... The direction must eventually be frozen because a->b and b->a have completely different semantics. So: Lineage direction = OPEN DESIGN QUESTION at this stage.
rows.statement: Defines lineage as a directed relation over artifacts (lambda subseteq Artifact x Artifact, e.g. e->o->p from the worked example) but flags the direction convention itself (e.g. o->p vs p<-o<-e) as an open design question since the two directions carry different semantics.

rows.anchor: we should resist immediately embedding context into every proposition. An alternative is: Interpret: Proposition x Context -> Meaning. This preserves separation. ... this is a design hypothesis requiring later testing.
rows.statement: Considers two alternatives for context: embedding it directly into each proposition (p_c=(p,c)) versus keeping propositions context-free and defining a separate Interpret:Proposition x Context -> Meaning function; prefers the latter to preserve separation of concerns, flagged as a design hypothesis needing later testing.

rows.anchor: Validate: Proposition x Evidence x Policy -> Assessment. This is much better than making policy itself part of the proposition.
rows.statement: Defines governance/policy application as Validate:Proposition x Evidence x Policy -> Assessment, arguing this is preferable to embedding policy directly into the proposition object.

rows.anchor: K_0=(C_0,sigma_0,theta_0,lambda_0,pi_0) where C_0=(V_0,E_0) [concrete worked values] ... This is now an actual mathematical object, rather than merely a symbolic kernel.
rows.statement: Assembles a fully concrete K0=(C0,sigma0,theta0,lambda0,pi0) with actual worked values: V0={s,v1,p,o,e}, E0={(s,hasVersion,v1),(o,supports,p),(e,produces,o)}, sigma0(p)=Observed, theta0(p)=[t0,infinity), lambda0={e->o->p}, pi0 in Policy -- explicitly characterized as an actual mathematical object rather than a merely symbolic kernel notation, directly instantiating the K5=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) shape with concrete content.

rows.anchor: we need a validity predicate Valid(K). Thus: K = {K | Valid(K)}. And we must define Valid(K_0). ... Type validity ... Referential validity ... Relation validity ... Status validity ... Temporal validity ... Lineage validity. These are genuine candidate invariants.
rows.statement: Defines the Knowledge-State space as K={K | Valid(K)} and proposes six candidate validity conditions for K0: type validity of V0/E0, referential validity (every edge references existing nodes), relation validity (relation types are well-typed), status validity (sigma0(p) in Sigma), temporal validity (theta0(p) in Interval), and lineage validity (every lineage reference points to an existing artifact).
invariants: referential validity: (a,r,b) in E0 => a,b in V0

rows.anchor: T_addObservation(K_0,o_2)=K_1. If o_2 is correctly typed and all references remain valid, then Valid(K_1). Thus: K_0 in K and Valid(o_2) => T_addObservation(K_0,o_2) in K. This gives us the first concrete candidate closure theorem. But it is only proved for this restricted transformation. It does no
rows.statement: States and proves a first, restricted closure theorem: K0 in K and Valid(o2) implies T_addObservation(K0,o2) in K, for the single add-observation transformation only -- explicitly not a proof of global transformation closure over K.

rows.anchor: T_addObservation is naturally a partial function: T_addObservation: D -> K where D subseteq K x Observation. The domain condition could be Pre(K,o)=true. Then T(K,o) is defined iff Pre(K,o). This is a major result for the eventual transition algebra.
rows.statement: Establishes that state transformations are naturally partial functions (T_addObservation: D -> K, D subseteq K x Observation) defined only where a precondition Pre(K,o) holds -- e.g. an observation referencing an absent entity makes the transformation undefined -- flagged as a major result for the eventual transition algebra (transformations are not assumed total).

rows.anchor: PASS -- Candidate Knowledge State successfully constructed but FORMAL CLOSURE -- NOT YET PROVEN and FINAL KERNEL -- NOT YET SELECTED. ... Can K_0 survive identity, equality, contradiction, uncertainty, and competing evidence without introducing ad-hoc rules? That is the next serious mathematical tes
rows.statement: Records the Step-245 verdict (PASS on constructing a candidate K0; FORMAL CLOSURE not yet proven; FINAL KERNEL not yet selected) and sets the next mandatory test: whether K0 can survive identity, equality, contradiction, uncertainty, and competing evidence without ad-hoc rules, rather than being extended blindly.

rows.anchor: Identity: PASS at representation level. Equality: FAIL/OPEN. Contradiction: PARTIAL PASS. Uncertainty: PARTIAL/OPEN.
rows.statement: Scores the Step-245 candidate K0 on the four stress tests: object identity PASS at the representation level; Knowledge-State equality FAIL/OPEN (no canonical K1=K2 established); contradiction PARTIAL PASS (representable but requires context+time+domain constraints, not intrinsic); uncertainty PARTIAL/OPEN (representable via an external regime, numeric semantics unresolved).

rows.anchor: whether K1=K2 depends partly on whether provenance is semantically constitutive. We therefore cannot yet decide whether lambda is merely metadata or part of identity. Provenance minimality = OPEN.
rows.statement: Names an explicit open question sharper than 'lineage is important': whether lineage/provenance (lambda) is merely descriptive metadata or is constitutive of Knowledge-State identity/equality -- 'provenance minimality' remains unresolved.

rows.anchor: Do not proceed directly to 'Step 246: test K0' as if K0 were already the canonical Knowledge State. First audit whether K0 is even the correct category of object. [9 unresolved hypotheses listed]
rows.statement: Lists 9 specific unresolved hypotheses embedded in Step 245's K0 (policy pi may belong to governance/transformation not state; lineage lambda may be history not a state component; epistemic status sigma may be a derived assessment not a primitive; temporal validity theta may belong to an assertion/observation instance not the proposition; content C=(V,E) being a graph is a modelling hypothesis; K0 in K has not been demonstrated since Valid(K) is only partial; the closure theorem covers only one restricted transformation; the status vocabulary remains normative/unresolved; the K/L/T/E/C/A/P distinction must not be silently re-collapsed) and forbids treating K0 as canonical before auditing whether it is even the right category of object.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 245 constructed K0 = (C0, sigma0, theta0, lambda0, pi0) and concluded Candidate Knowledge State successfully constructed. This is useful, but it is not yet a valid theory.

rows.anchor: construct a reconciliation table covering the following previous results: K is undefined (Step 230); K5 is a candidate; K8 is a candidate; I*={Provenance}; lineage is implemented; KnowledgeState absent from production code; Validation is an Assessment (Step 232); Policy/Governance external to transf
rows.statement: Requires an explicit reconciliation table across 10 named prior findings spanning Step 230, K5/K8, the verifier's I*={Provenance} invariant, the implementation audit (lineage implemented, KnowledgeState absent), Step 232 (Validation is an Assessment), and Step 245's K0 and Content/Qualification/Governance decomposition, classifying each apparent conflict as genuine contradiction, different abstraction level, different object type, historical evolution, or prior error -- with an explicit ban on silent reconciliation.

rows.anchor: Test both alternatives. Model A: K=(C,sigma,theta,lambda,pi). Model B: K=(C,sigma,theta,lambda) with Validate: K x Evidence x Policy -> Assessment and/or T: K x Input x Policy x Authority -> K'. Determine which model has the better type discipline.
rows.statement: Mandates a direct test of whether policy pi belongs inside the Knowledge State (Model A: K=(C,sigma,theta,lambda,pi)) or is external, expressed only through Validate:K x Evidence x Policy->Assessment and/or T:K x Input x Policy x Authority->K' (Model B: K=(C,sigma,theta,lambda)), to be decided on type-discipline grounds rather than intuition.

rows.anchor: Can two knowledge states be identical while having different histories? If yes, then History(K) != K may be fundamental. Construct an example K1 and K2 with identical current semantic content but different histories. Then test K1=K2 under: structural, semantic, provenance-sensitive, historical ident
rows.statement: Mandates testing whether lambda (lineage) belongs inside K, outside K, or as a derived function History:K->Histories, via a required counterexample construction: two states with identical current semantic content but different histories, tested against 4 equality notions (structural, semantic, provenance-sensitive, historical identity) to determine whether History(K) != K is fundamental.

rows.anchor: Model 1: sigma: Proposition -> Status. Model 2: sigma: Proposition x Evidence x Context -> Status. Model 3: Assessment: Proposition x Evidence x Context x Policy -> Assessment where Status(Assessment) is derived. ... This may reveal that EpistemicStatus is not a primitive of Knowledge State at all.
rows.statement: Formalizes three explicit candidate models for epistemic status (a pure function of the proposition; a function of proposition+evidence+context; or a derived projection of a full Assessment function including policy), to be tested with 3 concrete counterexample patterns (same proposition/different evidence; same proposition+evidence/different context; same evidence/different policy), anticipating that EpistemicStatus may not be a Knowledge-State primitive at all.

rows.anchor: Construct a counterexample where same proposition, different assertion instances, different validity intervals [is possible]. ... Also preserve the distinction between valid time, known time, record time, decision time ... Do not collapse bitemporal concepts into one timestamp.
rows.statement: Requires testing whether temporal validity (theta) attaches to Proposition, Assertion, Observation, or Assessment via a counterexample (same proposition, distinct assertion instances, distinct validity intervals), and mandates preserving up to four distinct temporal dimensions (valid time, known time, record time, decision time) rather than collapsing them into one timestamp, where the corpus supports the distinction.

rows.anchor: Can the required KnowledgeOS semantics be represented by a graph without making the graph itself the ontology? Compare: Graph as representation, against Graph as mathematical object, against Graph as implementation structure. Do not confuse them.
rows.statement: Requires testing whether C=(V,E)'s graph structure is an ontological fact, a representation choice, or an implementation choice, distinguishing 'graph as representation' from 'graph as mathematical object' from 'graph as implementation structure' as three non-identical claims.

rows.anchor: Four of the five components of Step 245's K_0 are REFUTED AS STATE COMPONENTS by executed counterexample: pi, lambda, sigma and theta all belong outside K. Only C survives, and only as a representation choice. This CONFIRMS Step 245's own boxed hedge that K_5 may be a projection/packaging of a riche
rows.statement: Headline result: executed counterexamples refute pi, lambda, sigma and theta as components of the Knowledge State K0 (only C survives, as a representation choice); this outcome confirms rather than contradicts Step 245's own internal hedge that K5=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) may be a projection of a richer typed structure.

lineage_claims.quote: This CONFIRMS Step 245's own boxed hedge [07] that K_5 may be a projection/packaging of a richer typed structure rather than a set of five primitives.

rows.anchor: Only one genuine conflict: policy placement. ... Classification: GENUINE CONTRADICTION between the prior audits and Step 245 on pi. ... Feedback-loop check: Step 245 fingerprinted against all verifier artifacts -- (q,s,e,c,t,u) 0 hits ... Classification: SOURCE-INDEPENDENT.
rows.statement: Executes the mandated 10-row reconciliation table, finding only one genuine contradiction (policy pi's placement, Step 245 inside K vs prior audits outside) with everything else being unaddressed-but-not-contradictory; runs a feedback-loop fingerprint check (searching Step 245 for verifier-specific terminology, 0 hits) and classifies Step 245 as SOURCE-INDEPENDENT evidence, continuing Step 232's own inner tuple rather than responding to this verification programme.

rows.anchor: K_0's own content has edges = empty set. A set suffices for the constructed example. The graph is required only when relations between propositions must be expressed. VERDICT: C=(V,E) is a REPRESENTATION CHOICE ... not an ontological fact and not an implementation necessity. ... PROPOSED, not CORPUS
rows.statement: Notes that Step 245's own concrete K0 instance uses zero edges, so a plain set would have sufficed; concludes C=(V,E)'s graph structure is a representation choice justified only when inter-proposition relations must be expressed, not an ontological fact or implementation necessity -- downgrading Step 245's unstated graph assumption to PROPOSED rather than CORPUS ESTABLISHES; this is the one component of K0 that survives the attack (in reduced form).

rows.anchor: Valid(K) -- still not computable. Its predicates would need a designated status vocabulary (underdetermined) and a decidable context-membership test (undefined). K remains incompletely defined, and K_0 in K is therefore still not demonstrated.
rows.statement: Even after the typed-family reconstruction, Valid(K) remains uncomputable because it needs a designated status vocabulary (still underdetermined by the corpus) and an undefined context-membership test; K0 in K, the question Step 245 itself posed and left open (245.12), still has no answer.

rows.anchor: FORMALLY INCOMPLETE. Not inconsistent: no contradiction survives once the typed family replaces the tuple. Not closed: Valid(K) is not computable and Proposition != Assertion is undefined. [completeness table across 8 dimensions] What survives: C, the transition rule with external policy/authority,
rows.statement: Delivers the final mandated verdict: FORMALLY INCOMPLETE (neither inconsistent -- no contradiction survives the typed-family reconstruction -- nor closed -- Valid(K) uncomputable and Proposition!=Assertion undefined), with a per-dimension completeness table (Conceptual HIGH; Mathematical/Statistical-epistemic/DDD-semantic INCOMPLETE; Computational/Engineering-specification/Implementation-conformance/Empirical-validation PARTIAL); summarizes that content-as-representation, the externally-parameterized transition rule, Validation->Assessment, History-as-external-function, and assertion-level bitemporality all survive the attack, while pi, lambda, sigma and theta do not survive as K-components (four of the original five); stops per the mandate's Section 18 on three conditions without patching silently or assigning a kernel label.

rows.anchor: Non-step files (the Q-series, day 2): 12. Numbered steps: 5 -- steps 8, 11, 16, 185. Numbered steps >=200: 0. Files stating the type chain P != A != K_t: 1 -- question-7, a NON-STEP file. Step 245 rebuilds K0 ... with no assertion layer at all -- collapsing the exact distinction Q7 called the bigges
rows.statement: Reports a measured corpus search (executed grep-style count) for the assertion layer A=(P,Sigma,E,tau,Pi): 12 occurrences in non-step Q-series (day-2) files, only 5 in numbered steps (8, 11, 16, 185), zero in steps 200 and above, and exactly one file (Q7, a non-step file) stating the full type chain P!=A!=K_t -- concluding Step 245's K0 construction, 219 steps later, silently re-collapses exactly the distinction Q7 identified as the corpus's biggest mathematical problem.

rows.anchor: The evolution is real but non-monotonic. The strongest formal content is at the beginning (Q-series, day 2), not the end. Three contradictions stand [pi/lambda inside K vs Q7 outside; sigma stored vs Q7/232.4 derived; Step 245 has no assertion layer vs Q7's central object]. All three resolve against
rows.statement: States the corpus's evolution is non-monotonic (strongest formal content at the beginning, not the end) and resolves all 3 remaining Step-245 contradictions (pi/lambda placement, sigma being stored vs derived, absence of an assertion layer) against Step 245 and in favor of the corpus's own day-2 (Q7) work -- the clearest single statement in this batch that later is not always more developed.

rows.anchor: Content-only: Falsified as universal candidate. Structured state (Content,Qualification,Governance,...): remains viable. History-inclusive state (State,Lineage,Provenance,...): also remains viable. No candidate has yet passed all requirements.
rows.statement: Consolidates candidate state representations into 3 groups: content-only is falsified as a universal candidate; a structured (Content,Qualification,Governance) model and a history-inclusive (State,Lineage,Provenance) model both remain viable, with neither yet passing all requirements -- narrowing but not resolving the architecture question.
