sources.note: ADR-AIP-04, the deferred future decision on role-model/capability ownership for the AI Engineering Platform.

rows.anchor: Why ADR-AIP-04 stays frozen during this work ... BC-7 discovery may itself produce role-ownership evidence ... Starting ADR-AIP-04 before this landscape lands would mean designing roles before understanding their ownership.
rows.statement: A principled reason is given for freezing ADR-AIP-04 (role-model ownership) during BC-7's strategic discovery: the discovery itself may surface evidence about whether Role/Assignment/Actor/Authority belong partly to BC-7, so deciding roles first would risk designing them before their ownership is understood.

rows.anchor: Implementation · code changes · component movement · workflow_engine changes · ADR-AIP-04 decision · role-model ownership decision.
rows.statement: The commission's forbidden-classes list mechanically excludes implementation, the workflow_engine itself, and any ADR-AIP-04/role-model decision from this tactical discovery work.

rows.anchor: Python Stage-2 verification → portfolio quiet → ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery → role/capability consequences → Implementation Architecture → Implementation.
rows.statement: The ARB's registered sequencing determination orders remaining platform work: finish Python Stage-2 verification, quiet the portfolio, then run ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery before any implementation architecture, with the architectural reason recorded that beginning implementation first risks encoding an incomplete role model.

rows.anchor: ADR-AIP-04 must NOT be framed as 'let's add a Knowledge Engineer and a Communication Engineer.' ... What capabilities does a sustainable AI Engineering Platform require?
rows.statement: A capability-first guard is registered before ADR-AIP-04 discovery is even commissioned: the governing question must stay 'what capabilities does a sustainable AI engineering platform require', evaluated strictly in the order capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> shared platform service, never role-first.

rows.anchor: the governing question is "what capabilities does a sustainable AI Engineering Platform require?", evaluated capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> shared platform service, with people and agents last.
rows.statement: A capability-first discovery guard is registered before the ADR-AIP-04 commission exists: the discovery must proceed strictly in order capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> shared platform service, placing people and agents last.
invariants: capability-first ordering must not be violated

rows.anchor: Recommendation: commission ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery first -- it is the first-named purpose, its guard is already registered, and the BC-7 role-model question has been formally deferred to it since 2026-08-17.
rows.statement: ADR-AIP-04 capability discovery is recommended as Track 2's first commissioned work item, because BC-7's role-model ownership question (Stage-2 OQ-5) was already formally deferred to it on 2026-08-17.

lineage_claims.quote: the BC-7 role-model question has been formally deferred to it since 2026-08-17

rows.anchor: Determine the capabilities required for a sustainable session-based AI Engineering Operating System *before* formalizing or extending the role model.
rows.statement: The purpose of the ADR-AIP-04 commission is to determine required capabilities before formalizing or extending any role model; it is a discovery/architecture item and does not authorize implementation.

rows.anchor: Every important statement classified OBSERVED - INFERRED - PROPOSED - DECIDED - OPEN. Do not turn a proposal into a decision.
rows.statement: A five-value classification discipline (OBSERVED, INFERRED, PROPOSED, DECIDED, OPEN) is mandated for every important statement in the ADR-AIP-04 deliverable, with an explicit prohibition against silently promoting a proposal to a decision.

rows.anchor: ADR-AIP-04 -- Capability Discovery Proposal, seventeen sections: Context ... Capability Inventory ... Ownership Analysis ... Invariants ... Role/Stewardship Analysis ... Candidate Contexts or Stewardships ... Open Questions ... PO/ARB Decisions Required.
rows.statement: A fixed seventeen-section deliverable structure is mandated for the ADR-AIP-04 discovery proposal, spanning context through to PO/ARB decisions required.

rows.anchor: RETURNED FOR MATERIAL CORRECTION ... The verification question was: is this sufficiently justified to be placed before PO/ARB for decision? On E and I -- not yet.
rows.statement: Overall verdict: the discovery proposal is returned for material correction on two evidence claims (six-role hypothesis, C-14 status) while its DDD discipline, mechanism evidence, and refusal to promote C-19 to a bounded context are found to survive independent falsification.

rows.anchor: Whether the discovery independently converged or reconstructed an unread source CANNOT BE ESTABLISHED. ... Classification: OPEN.
rows.statement: Because the discovery's Section 13 stewardship reading materially matches the untracked document's 'Option B', but I-did-not-read-it is a self-declared and unattestable claim, the question of independent convergence vs reconstruction from an unread source is classified OPEN, and the convergence must not be counted as corroboration.

rows.anchor: Amendment 1 declares NO producing process. ... Its authorship is recoverable only by inference
rows.statement: Finding W-4: Amendment 1 violates its own lane's requirement to disclose a producing process; its authorship is only inferable, and no correction assignment was ever registered for its production -- a governance/provenance defect distinct from the content defects.

rows.anchor: THE CORRECTION SUCCEEDED. THE DECISION SURFACE IS NOT YET CLEAN.
rows.statement: Overall verdict on Amendment 1: the corrective discipline succeeded in substance (no finding strengthened, no capability invented, nothing outside the proposal touched) but two defects (W-1's own recurrence of the truncated-search error; W-2's misplaced pointer) must land before the decision surface is clean for PO/ARB.

rows.anchor: capability -> ownership -> bounded context / stewardship -> human role -> agent -> platform service -> technology
rows.statement: The capability-first ordering is restated as the binding method for the entire discovery: capability -> ownership -> bounded context/stewardship -> human role -> agent -> platform service -> technology, with the explicit prohibition on beginning from role creation.

rows.anchor: every invariant BC-7 owns is MECHANICALLY enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is DECLARED ONLY. INFERRED: the platform's assurance is strong exactly where it is executable and weak exactly where it is prose -- and a role model is prose.
rows.statement: The discovery's core structural result: BC-7's invariants (I-1 single mutation owner, I-2 HANDOFF+human START, I-3 sticky STOPPED, G-1 closure is a governance act, G-2 single writer for the Authority State) are all mechanically enforced, while almost every invariant outside BC-7 (R-34 producer!=acceptor, INV-ATTR-2 separation, AIP-11 frozen-artifact supersession, AIP-14 Product Primacy) is declared only, with no enforcement mechanism.
invariants: I-2 HANDOFF and human START jointly required
G-1 closure is a governance act
G-2 Authority State has exactly one writer
INV-ATTR-2 separation is declared not attestable

rows.anchor: One process occupied verification -> architecture-review -> architecture-drafting -> domain roles in sequence, and in each lane recorded its own START -- a governance act -- because no separate governance process was present
rows.statement: Finding F-9/F-9a: the drafting process itself, first-hand, occupied verification, architecture-review, architecture-drafting and domain roles in sequence within one process, self-recording its own STARTs each time -- evidence that 'Governance' as practised is a cross-cutting capability set with only ONE strictly-separated duty (acceptance/closure via COMPLETE, mechanically refused to non-governance/human writers), not a distinct actor.

assumptions.statement: no separate governance process was present for the cited lanes
assumptions.anchor: because no separate governance process was present

rows.anchor: an absence claim requires an exhaustive, untruncated search AND an explicit statement of what was searched. ... a search that can be truncated is not a survey.
rows.statement: Amendment 1's root-cause finding (A1.0): both verified defects (V-1, V-2) share one mechanism -- an absence claim resting on a truncated search or an ungeneralised narrow claim -- proposing a durable discipline that an absence claim requires an exhaustive, untruncated search plus an explicit statement of what was searched.

rows.anchor: the evidence package has now been materially wrong three times about the same thing, and the honest summary is that this discovery has been better at DDD reasoning than at surveying its own estate.
rows.statement: Correction #2's self-assessment: across the discovery, Amendment 1 and Correction #2, the same evidence-survey error class recurred three times, while the DDD reasoning method itself (capability-before-agent, parsimony, refusing role-inferred-capability) held; no finding is strengthened by Correction #2 and two (C-14, SB-3) end weaker than before.

rows.anchor: READY FOR PO/ARB DECISION ... Three material evidence errors in one work item is a real record. But the correction that matters most -- F-3'' -- replaced its basis rather than defending it
rows.statement: Overall verdict: the discovery/Amendment 1/Correction 2 package is READY FOR PO/ARB DECISION -- ungoverned material is properly routed to OQ-I, inferred ownership is refused at every convenient point, and eleven actual architectural decisions remain, none pre-empted; two low-severity residuals (missing supersession markers) do not block.

rows.anchor: W-1 ... As of this decision that thesis is FALSE -- the model IS governed. What remains live in W-1 is the evidence-quality question
rows.statement: The adoption decision retroactively supersedes the narrow thesis Verification #2's finding W-1 was testing ('the six-role model is not currently established as governed architecture'), because that thesis is now false by decision; the verdict-G re-scoping requires the still-pending Verification #3 lane to be redirected to the evidence-quality question rather than the adoption question itself.

lineage_claims.quote: the thesis is SUPERSEDED, not disproven

rows.anchor: Determine whether the amended analysis correctly implements the registered AMD1 + AMD2 epistemic and DDD corrections, AND whether it REMAINS A DECISION-PREPARATION ARTIFACT rather than silently becoming an architectural decision.
rows.statement: Verification identifies insufficiency; it does not provide the replacement architecture -- written verbatim into the execution context as a binding boundary for this and future verification assignments in the work item.

rows.anchor: The act bars "the author of any review that materially caused AMD2, if identifiable." That review is not in the estate -- Governance searched and found no artifact ... its author is not identifiable, the bar cannot be applied to it
rows.statement: A cited 'Independent review of the capability architecture analysis' that materially triggered AMD2 does not exist as an artifact anywhere in the estate; the independence bar cannot be applied against an unidentifiable author, and the act's own qualifier ('if identifiable') is what permits registration to proceed rather than stall.

rows.anchor: What is still missing from the lifecycle ... 4. ADR-AIP-04: What capabilities should the AI Engineering Platform formally provide? ... These are future work, not defects in the current lifecycle.
rows.statement: Five remaining lifecycle gaps are listed as future work: role identity/provenance, knowledge evidence provenance, communication capability ownership, ADR-AIP-04's capability question, and how the accepted BC-7 model becomes software implementation.

rows.anchor: the amendment asserts no original wording was rewritten ... section 13 decision 3 applies strikethrough to the original question text ... the words remain, but rendered struck out, i.e. visually negated rather than annotated
rows.statement: Finding F-6: an amendment's categorical claim that 'no original wording was rewritten' has one counter-instance -- a strikethrough visually negates rather than merely annotates the struck text -- distinguishing four distinct kinds of edit operation (historical preservation, additive amendment, actual replacement, workflow transcription).

sources.note: S0528's extraction from Peter Gärdenfors' Knowledge in Flux: epistemic states (not knowledge) as the primary modeling unit; expansion/revision/contraction as the three fundamental change types; epistemic entrenchment as a contextual, regime-dependent resistance-to-revision dimension distinct from probability; propositions modeled as state transformations P:K->K'; explanation as surprise-reduction relative to the recipient's epistemic state; causal belief modeled via contraction; a three-level preserved-history/epistemic-state/presented-knowledge architecture. Ranked by the author as one of the most useful sources read in the whole McGinn-Floridi-Dretske-Fagin-Gärdenfors research arc.

rows.anchor: the central entities are epistemic states, representing a person's cognitive/epistemic situation at a point in time, while treating them as rational idealizations rather than literal psychological objects. ... 1. Model of epistemic states 2. Epistemic attitudes 3. Epistemic inputs 4. Epistemic commitment function ... I would not put the commitment function in the Kernel. It is a regime-specific rule for transforming states.
rows.statement: Reframes the guiding question from 'what is Knowledge?' to 'what is the minimal representation of an epistemic state, and how does that state change?', adopting Gärdenfors' four-component belief system (model of epistemic states, epistemic attitudes, epistemic inputs, epistemic commitment function), explicitly excluding the commitment function from the Kernel as a regime-specific transformation rule -- the Kernel preserves the state and the input/history needed to reconstruct the transformation.

rows.anchor: belief sets, possible worlds, ordinal plausibility, Bayesian probabilities, truth-maintenance systems, mental models ... KnowledgeOS should not store an epistemic state as "possible worlds." Possible worlds are one epistemic representation regime. ... Epistemic status is regime-relative. That should probably become an explicit KnowledgeOS principle.
rows.statement: Surveys six alternative epistemic-state representation regimes Gärdenfors considers (belief sets, possible worlds, ordinal plausibility, Bayesian probabilities, truth-maintenance systems, mental models), concluding possible worlds are only one such regime among several, reinforcing the Kernel-preserves/regimes-reason architecture; derives the principle 'epistemic status is regime-relative' -- the same proposition can be accepted/rejected/indeterminate under one attitude model or assigned probability/plausibility under another.

rows.anchor: some models can contain hidden variables that have no direct expression in the available language ... Language does not contain the whole knowledge state. ... Pāṇinian/Vāṇī: language is expression. Floridi: representation ≠ information. Dretske: information ≠ encoding. Gärdenfors: epistemic state ≠ language. This is now a very strong cross-lens invariant.
rows.statement: Reports Gärdenfors' hidden/latent epistemic-state variables (aspects of a second-order probabilistic epistemic state with no direct linguistic expression), formalizing 'language does not contain the whole knowledge state' and recording independent four-lens convergence (Vāṇī: language is expression; Floridi: representation≠information; Dretske: information≠encoding; Gärdenfors: epistemic state≠language) into the principle 'language is an external expression/communication layer over the epistemic substrate.'
invariants: language is an external expression/communication layer over the epistemic substrate

rows.anchor: EXPANSION REVISION CONTRACTION ... An expansion adds information consistent with the current state. A revision incorporates information that conflicts with the current state. A contraction removes a commitment. ... we should preserve: previous_state, input, change_type, change_policy, resulting_state, rationale.
rows.statement: Formalizes three fundamental epistemic change types (expansion: adds compatible information; revision: incorporates conflicting information; contraction: removes a commitment) as a state-transition graph, requiring KnowledgeOS preserve previous_state/input/change_type/change_policy/resulting_state/rationale rather than merely overwriting a current_state field -- much stronger than an undifferentiated knowledge(t1)->knowledge(t2) chain.
dependencies: non-monotonic knowledge over time (S0523, S0526, S0527)

rows.anchor: Supersession is not necessarily: "A is false now." It may mean: Under the current epistemic regime and new input, retaining A is no longer rational/acceptable.
rows.statement: Reframes supersession using the revision policy: rather than 'A is false now', supersession means retaining A is no longer rational/acceptable under the current epistemic regime and new input, with some commitments retained and others retracted -- a better model for living knowledge.

rows.anchor: beliefs have different degrees of epistemic entrenchment. Some are more difficult to give up because they are more important for inquiry, explanation and decision making. And this is not the same thing as probability. ... "2 + 2 = 4" probability = 1, entrenchment = extremely high. "The UI button is blue" probability = 1, entrenchment = low.
rows.statement: Introduces epistemic entrenchment -- degree of resistance to giving up a belief, driven by importance for inquiry/explanation/decision-making -- as distinct from probability, illustrated by two claims with identical probability=1 but radically different entrenchment ('2+2=4' extremely high vs 'the UI button is blue' low), called probably the most valuable new idea from the book.

rows.anchor: entrenchment depends on the epistemic state. The same proposition can have a different entrenchment ordering in different belief systems ... scientific paradigm shifts ... Importance is not an intrinsic property of a proposition. ... importance(P) = 0.9 would be misleading unless it specifies for whom? for what inquiry? in which context? under which epistemic regime? at what time?
rows.statement: Uses Gärdenfors' claim that entrenchment orderings differ across belief systems (illustrated by scientific paradigm shifts, where a once-central claim becomes peripheral) to correct any naive 'importance(P)=0.9' score: importance is not intrinsic to a proposition but must specify for whom, for what inquiry, in which context, under which regime, at what time; extends the Knowledge Space boundary model (previously Level-of-Abstraction-based) by adding an entrenchment-structure dimension alongside scope/LoA/inquiry/context/regime/participants, with Topic as a projection of this fuller state.
invariants: importance is not an intrinsic property of a proposition

lineage_claims.target: Level of Abstraction based Knowledge Space boundary (S0521)
lineage_claims.quote: This gives us a much better definition of a "Knowledge Space boundary" ... Gärdenfors adds another dimension: epistemic relevance/entrenchment.

rows.anchor: Minimal Epistemic Disturbance ... make the smallest rational change necessary to accommodate the new input. ... give up as little information as possible and avoid unnecessary loss. ... Not a Kernel primitive, but a very strong regime.
rows.statement: Names the 'Minimal Epistemic Disturbance' principle from Gärdenfors' minimal-change revision criterion and informational-economy contraction: when revising, change no more commitments than necessary to accommodate new input, avoiding unnecessary information loss; proposed as a strong candidate revision regime rather than a Kernel primitive.

rows.anchor: EVIDENCE HISTORY: immutable. EPISTEMIC STATE: revisable. KNOWLEDGE PROJECTION: recomputable. ... Observation O1 remains true as historical observation. But Interpretation I1 can be withdrawn. And Epistemic state S1 can become S2 without rewriting O1.
rows.statement: Resolves the apparent conflict between 'evidence is immutable' and 'knowledge is revised' by distinguishing three tiers: Evidence History (immutable), Epistemic State (revisable), Knowledge Projection (recomputable) -- an observation O1 remains true as a historical record even as an interpretation I1 built on it is withdrawn and the epistemic state moves from S1 to S2 without rewriting O1.

rows.anchor: LEVEL A — PRESERVED HISTORY: observations, inputs, assertions, sources, events, evidence, provenance; immutable. LEVEL B — EPISTEMIC STATE: acceptance, rejection, suspension, probability, plausibility, entrenchment, belief; mutable/derived. LEVEL C — PRESENTED KNOWLEDGE: answers, summaries, topics, reports, recommendations, current understanding; derived projections. This is one of the strongest architectural conclusions we've reached.
rows.statement: Proposes a three-level architecture explicitly called one of the strongest architectural conclusions reached: Level A Preserved History (observations, inputs, assertions, sources, events, evidence, provenance -- immutable), Level B Epistemic State (acceptance, rejection, suspension, probability, plausibility, entrenchment, belief -- mutable/derived), Level C Presented Knowledge (answers, summaries, topics, reports, recommendations, current understanding -- derived projections).
dependencies: preserved history vs epistemic state distinction (same file)

rows.anchor: an epistemic input can be represented simply as a function from epistemic states to epistemic states. He explicitly calls this ontologically simpler. ... Input Event + Transformation Policy -> State Transition. ... EpistemicTransition: before, input, rule/regime, conflict, retained commitments, retracted commitments, after.
rows.statement: Uses Gärdenfors' ontological-simplification move (an epistemic input need not be a giant separate entity; it can be represented as a function K->K' on epistemic states) -- compatible with the Merricks/Zero-Lens eliminativism method -- to propose Input Event + Transformation Policy -> State Transition rather than an EpistemicInput entity, and a candidate (not-yet-Kernel) EpistemicTransition record (before, input, rule/regime, conflict, retained commitments, retracted commitments, after).

rows.anchor: an explanation should provide relevant information that makes the phenomenon less surprising relative to the recipient's epistemic state. ... explanations depend on the epistemic circumstances of both the requester and the explainer. ... Explanation Quality = f(new information, recipient epistemic state, question/context).
rows.statement: Defines explanation quality relative to the recipient's epistemic state (not as an intrinsic explanans/explanandum relation): a good explanation makes the phenomenon less surprising given the recipient's prior knowledge, context, and available evidence, formalized as Explanation Quality = f(new information, recipient epistemic state, question/context) -- a better starting point than an LLM-style intrinsic answer-quality score.

rows.anchor: P(failure | current knowledge) = 0.05 ... After: The certificate expired. ... P(failure | expanded/revised knowledge) = 0.70. The explanation reduced surprise. ... surprise_before - surprise_after ... cognitive relief from reduced surprise.
rows.statement: Defines an Explanation Gain metric = surprise_before - surprise_after (Gärdenfors' 'cognitive relief'), illustrated by a service-failure example where a candidate explanation ('the certificate expired') raises P(failure|knowledge) from 0.05 to 0.70, called a promising statistical bridge for KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: current knowledge includes C and E -> temporarily remove C -> ask whether E becomes less expected -> C has causal relevance. His probabilistic criterion is that, in the contracted epistemic state, occurrence of C raises the probability of E. ... probabilistic influence alone does not automatically establish causation ... P(E|C) > P(E) is not automatically C causes E. ... preserve causal_hypothesis separately from statistical_association.
rows.statement: Formalizes causal belief via contraction: temporarily remove candidate cause C from the epistemic state and test whether effect E becomes less expected (probabilistic criterion: in the contracted state, C's occurrence raises P(E)); connects this to the project's Persons+Causes research, proposing KnowledgeOS distinguish observed sequence/correlation/causal belief/causal evidence/causal hypothesis/causal explanation; explicitly warns P(E|C)>P(E) does not automatically establish C causes E (spurious/direct/indirect causes need additional treatment), requiring causal_hypothesis be preserved separately from statistical_association.
invariants: P(E|C) > P(E) does not automatically establish causation

rows.anchor: belief revision techniques to logical databases and legal codes. A logical database can be treated as a model of an epistemic state, and updates correspond to expansion, revision and contraction. ... deleting a tuple is not enough: removing one fact can have implications for several derived facts. ... Never equate storage mutation with epistemic change. Deleting a record is not the same thing as retracting a proposition.
rows.statement: Reports Gärdenfors' direct application of belief revision to logical databases and legal codes (database updates correspond to expansion/revision/contraction; deleting one tuple is insufficient since it has implications for derived facts), deriving the principle 'never equate storage mutation with epistemic change' -- deleting a record is not the same as retracting a proposition, which can have dependent consequences.

rows.anchor: the epistemic layer needs: OBSERVE, ACCEPT, EXPAND, REVISE, CONTRACT, SUPERSEDE, QUESTION, REASSESS, DERIVE. And importantly: DELETE is not a semantic operation equivalent to: CONTRACT.
rows.statement: Argues the Kernel should not be CRUD-centric (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE), proposing instead a nine-operation epistemic vocabulary (OBSERVE, ACCEPT, EXPAND, REVISE, CONTRACT, SUPERSEDE, QUESTION, REASSESS, DERIVE), explicitly distinguishing DELETE from CONTRACT as different operations.

rows.anchor: a proposition can be characterized by the change it would induce if added to an epistemic state. ... P : K → K' ... Meaning can be understood through the effect of an expression/proposition on a belief system.
rows.statement: Reports Gärdenfors' definition of a proposition as the change it would induce if added to an epistemic state (P: K -> K'), viewing a proposition as a potential transformation rather than only semantic content; correspondingly reframes meaning as understood through the effect of an expression on a belief system, connecting language/semantics/questions/belief-revision without making language foundational, independently supporting the Vāṇī/Paninian insight.

rows.anchor: his epistemological theory can formulate epistemic states and rationality criteria without using truth as the basic ingredient; truth is secondary within this conceptualistic framework. That does not refute McGinn. They are answering different questions. ... Ontology / truth theory ≠ Epistemic dynamics. So our Kernel should probably not attempt to derive epistemic dynamics from a single metaphysical truth theory.
rows.statement: Reconciles Gärdenfors (epistemic dynamics formulated without truth as a basic ingredient) with McGinn (truth as a primitive, reality-implying logical property): the two are not in conflict since they answer different questions, giving the principle Ontology/truth theory != Epistemic dynamics; the Kernel should not attempt to derive epistemic dynamics from a single metaphysical truth theory, instead supporting a relation to truth/verification while keeping epistemic-state transitions their own concern.

rows.anchor: 1. A state exists at a time. ... 14. State dynamics can support database/legal-code updates. This is much closer to a Kernel boundary than the ontology we had been building before.
rows.statement: Applies the Zero Lens by removing all Gärdenfors-specific machinery (AGM, possible worlds, Bayesian probabilities, Spohn, Ramsey test, belief set, logical language), leaving a fourteen-statement residual (a state exists at a time; contains commitments/attitudes; inputs can enter and change the state; different kinds of change exist; change follows a rationality/commitment policy; some commitments are more entrenched than others; the policy avoids unnecessary information loss; the same input can have different effects in different states; meaning can be studied through state-changing effects; explanation depends on the recipient's existing state; causal belief can depend on hypothetical state changes; state dynamics can support logic and database/legal-code updates), judged much closer to a Kernel boundary than the prior ontology-building work.

rows.anchor: PRESERVATION SUBSTRATE: Identity, Agent/epistemic participant, Context, Time, Epistemic input, Input provenance, Assertion/proposition reference, Epistemic attitude/assessment, State-transition event, Previous state reference, Resulting-state reference, Change type, Rationale/commitment reference, Conflict/incompatibility, Evidence/source, Entrenchment assessment. Notice what is not here: possible worlds, Bayesian probabilities, logic engine, truth engine, LLM, topic hierarchy, embedding.
rows.statement: Revises the candidate Preservation Substrate to sixteen items (Identity, Agent/epistemic participant, Context, Time, Epistemic input, Input provenance, Assertion/proposition reference, Epistemic attitude/assessment, State-transition event, Previous state reference, Resulting-state reference, Change type, Rationale/commitment reference, Conflict/incompatibility, Evidence/source, Entrenchment assessment), explicitly excluding possible worlds, Bayesian probabilities, logic engine, truth engine, LLM, topic hierarchy, and embedding as belonging to external regimes.

lineage_claims.quote: This book makes me revise our previous candidate.

rows.anchor: Epistemic Change Preservation Principle: KnowledgeOS must preserve not only what an agent/system currently accepts, but also the inputs, context, change type, and transformation history through which that epistemic state was reached. ... matters for: audit, replay, explanation, trust, revision, governance, AI-agent learning.
rows.statement: Names the 'Epistemic Change Preservation Principle': KnowledgeOS must preserve not only the currently accepted content but also the inputs, context, change type, and transformation history through which the epistemic state was reached, since the same final state can arise via different histories and the dynamics themselves are meaningful for audit, replay, explanation, trust, revision, governance, and AI-agent learning, fitting the project's existing deterministic-replay work.

rows.anchor: Knowledge Space is a dynamic space of epistemic states and state transitions, grounded in preserved inputs, propositions/contents, attitudes, contexts and histories, where different epistemic regimes can model the same underlying knowledge-bearing history in different ways. ... Knowledge Space ≠ possible worlds ≠ belief set ≠ Bayesian probability model. Those are models of regions/aspects of Knowledge Space.
rows.statement: Revises the Knowledge Space definition again (superseding 'a space of states, propositions, agents and possible worlds'): Knowledge Space is a dynamic space of epistemic states and state transitions, grounded in preserved inputs/propositions/attitudes/contexts/histories, over which different epistemic regimes model the same underlying knowledge-bearing history differently; possible worlds, belief sets, and Bayesian probability models are all merely models of regions/aspects of Knowledge Space, not Knowledge Space itself.
dependencies: Knowledge Space = possible-world state space, rejected (S0527)
invariants: Knowledge Space ≠ possible worlds ≠ belief set ≠ Bayesian probability model

lineage_claims.target: Knowledge Space as space of states/propositions/agents/possible worlds (S0523, S0527)
lineage_claims.quote: I would now revise our definition again.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Knowledge Space Model v0.1 — State, Input, Transition, Attitude, Provenance and Regime ... test it against real KnowledgeOS episodes, rather than continuing to expand the philosophical ontology.
rows.statement: Declines to add another epistemology book immediately, proposing the next serious step as 'KnowledgeOS Knowledge Space Model v0.1 -- State, Input, Transition, Attitude, Provenance and Regime', tested against real episodes via a concrete experiment (Initial State -> epistemic input -> Transformation {expansion?/revision?/contraction?/unresolved?} -> New Epistemic State {what changed/retained/retracted/why/under which regime/what remains unknown}) rather than continuing to expand the philosophical ontology.

rows.anchor: Knowledge is moving in an infinite Knowledge Space. ... Knowledge should serve the nature of the Knowledge Space itself. ... Knowledge is not merely accumulated inside the Knowledge Space; its structure, relations, boundaries, changes, and representations should remain coherent with the nature of the space being modelled.
rows.statement: Consolidates sixteen prior project intuitions about Knowledge Space (infinite, boundary-crossing, facts+arguments, dynamic, representation≠knowledge, LoA-dependent, tolerates uncertainty/contradiction/suspension, changes via expansion/revision/contraction, entrenchment-dependent importance, exceeds language, questions open paths, explanations reduce surprise) into one closing principle: knowledge's structure/relations/boundaries/changes/representations must remain coherent with the nature of the space being modeled, not merely accumulate inside it.

rows.anchor: Floridi gives us the idea that a representation is made at a selected **Level of Abstraction**, with a selected set of observables.
rows.statement: Ties the Knowledge Capacity construct back to all four prior book-lenses: Floridi's Level-of-Abstraction/observables defines what portion of a system can be represented; Gärdenfors' epistemic state contains commitments and changes through inputs/expansion/revision/contraction; Dretske separates information from its physical/linguistic encoding, so the capacity to 'write' information is not identical to the information itself; Searle adds that some information participates in institutional structures where context determines what something counts as.

rows.anchor: Peter Gärdenfors — Knowledge in Flux ... This may tell us whether our proposed: EXPAND REVISE CONTRACT CHALLENGE SUPERSEDE REINSTATE are actually fundamental—or merely convenient engineering names.
rows.statement: Proposes Gardenfors' Knowledge in Flux as high priority to attack E_t -> E_{t+1} via belief revision (expansion/contraction/revision/consistency/information change/epistemic dynamics), to determine whether the proposed lifecycle operations EXPAND/REVISE/CONTRACT/CHALLENGE/SUPERSEDE/REINSTATE are fundamental or merely convenient engineering names.

lexical.anchor: the central entities are epistemic states, representing a person's cognitive/epistemic situation at a point in time, while treating them as rational idealizations rather than literal psychological objects. ... 1. Model of epistemic states 2. Epistemic attitudes 3. Epistemic inputs 4. Epistemic commitment function ... I would not put the commitment function in the Kernel. It is a regime-specific rule for transforming states.

formal.anchor: EXPANSION REVISION CONTRACTION ... An expansion adds information consistent with the current state. A revision incorporates information that conflicts with the current state. A contraction removes a commitment. ... we should preserve: previous_state, input, change_type, change_policy, resulting_state, rationale.

governance.anchor: KnowledgeOS Knowledge Space Model v0.1 — State, Input, Transition, Attitude, Provenance and Regime ... test it against real KnowledgeOS episodes, rather than continuing to expand the philosophical ontology.

sources.note: S0859's Step 4: a full axiom set for admissible evidence-aggregation operators (determinism, permutation/duplicate invariance, non-inflation, monotonicity refinements, contradiction/conflict preservation, dependency/unknown-dependency sensitivity, temporal/context sensitivity, provenance preservation, no-evidence-creation, no-certainty-creation), split into kernel invariants vs policy properties, crystallized into a ten-item E-K1..E-K10 candidate 'KnowledgeOS epistemic constitution', and a nine-framework comparison concluding no single universal calculus suffices (Kernel + Pluggable Calculi); hands off to Step 5 (semantic domain of evidence contribution).

rows.anchor: First axiom: determinism ... EA_\rho(E,P,C)=EA_\rho(E,P,C) ... The same evidence, context and policy must produce the same assessment. If an LLM happens to produce different results each time, that variability cannot be hidden inside the mathematical definition. It must be represented as InferenceUn
rows.statement: States the determinism axiom: fixed (evidence, proposition, context, policy) must produce the same EA_ρ; LLM output variability must be represented explicitly as InferenceUncertainty rather than hidden inside the aggregation function — LLM variability ≠ epistemic randomness.

rows.anchor: Permutation invariance ... EA_\rho(\{e_1,e_2,e_3\},P,C) = EA_\rho(\{e_3,e_1,e_2\},P,C) ... The final assessment cannot depend merely on ingestion order.
rows.statement: States the permutation-invariance axiom: the final EA must not depend on the order evidence was ingested (document today, database tomorrow, LLM result later, human review afterward).

rows.anchor: Duplicate invariance ... e_1\equiv e_2 ... EA(E\cup\{e_1,e_2\}) = EA(E\cup\{e_1\}) ... prevents document duplication → artificial certainty. This should be a kernel invariant.
rows.statement: States duplicate invariance — identical/equivalent evidence items must not increase the assessment beyond a single instance — flagged explicitly as a candidate kernel invariant preventing 'document duplication → artificial certainty'.

rows.anchor: Derived-evidence non-inflation ... e_2=Transform(e_1) ... e_1\prec e_2 should imply IncrementalIndependentSupport(e_2\mid e_1)=0 unless the policy explicitly identifies an additional independent observation contained in e_2. This is particularly important for Document\rightarrow LLM\rightarrow Summa
rows.statement: States the derived-evidence non-inflation axiom: if e2 is a transform of e1, its incremental independent support is 0 by default, unless policy identifies an additional independent observation within it — critical for Document→LLM→Summary→Report chains.

rows.anchor: Irrelevance invariance ... Rel(e,P,C)=0 then EA(E\cup\{e\},P,C)=EA(E,P,C) ... The evidence is not deleted. It simply has no contribution ... NonRelevant\neq Nonexistent
rows.statement: States irrelevance invariance: zero-relevance evidence leaves EA unchanged but is not deleted from the record — NonRelevant ≠ Nonexistent.

rows.anchor: Supporting monotonicity ... e\Rightarrow P then S^+(E\cup\{e\})\ge S^+(E) ... e\Rightarrow\neg P implies S^-(E\cup\{e\})\ge S^-(E). This does not mean that the final conclusion must become more certain. Because new opposing evidence can simultaneously appear.
rows.statement: States a refined monotonicity axiom applying separately to S+ and S- components (each only increases with admissible independent supporting/opposing evidence respectively), explicitly not implying the overall conclusion becomes more certain, since opposing evidence can appear simultaneously.

rows.anchor: Contradiction preservation ... E^+\neq\emptyset and E^-\neq\emptyset then the assessment must retain both. EA(P)=(S^+,S^-,Conflict,\ldots) rather than EA(P)=singleScore ... S^+=0.91, S^-=0.88 must not become 0.03 because 0.03 conceals the existence of a serious conflict.
rows.statement: States the contradiction-preservation axiom, called 'one of the most important axioms': when both supporting and opposing evidence exist, EA must retain both as structured fields rather than collapsing to a single net score, since e.g. S+=0.91,S-=0.88 collapsing to 0.03 would conceal a serious conflict.

rows.anchor: Conflict sensitivity ... S^+>0 and S^->0 then Conflict(P)=Active subject to the conflict rule. ... Conflict_\rho(E^+,E^-,C) \rightarrow \{NoConflict,Potential,Active,Unresolved\} ... conflict detection is not simply arithmetic subtraction.
rows.statement: Defines Conflict_ρ(E+,E-,C)→{NoConflict,Potential,Active,Unresolved} as a four-valued policy-governed function, stating conflict detection is not simple arithmetic subtraction.

rows.anchor: Dependency sensitivity ... e_1\prec e_2 ... e_2 must not be treated as equivalent to an independent observation. Agg(E\cup\{e_2\}) \neq Agg(E\cup\{e_2^{independent}\}) ... This is a very strong test for candidate aggregation models.
rows.statement: States dependency sensitivity as a strong test axiom: aggregating a dependent evidence item must differ from aggregating an otherwise-identical independent one (Agg(E∪{e2}) ≠ Agg(E∪{e2^independent})).

rows.anchor: Unknown dependency must remain unknown ... Dependency(e_1,e_2)=Unknown ... cannot validly transform that into Independent(e_1,e_2)=True. UnknownDependency \Rightarrow No\ automatic\ independence\ credit. This does not mean UnknownDependency\Rightarrow Dependent. We retain Unknown. This is a three-va
rows.statement: States that unknown dependency must remain Unknown throughout aggregation — no automatic independence credit, but also not automatically treated as Dependent — reaffirming the three-valued epistemic property from earlier files.

rows.anchor: Corroboration ... e_1\perp_\rho e_2 and both support P, then the assessment should be capable of representing corroboration Corroboration_\rho(e_1,e_2)>0. But we deliberately do not specify Corroboration=0.4 yet. That is policy territory.
rows.statement: States corroboration must be representable (Corroboration_ρ(e1,e2)>0 for independent, mutually supporting evidence) without fixing its numeric value, which remains policy territory.

rows.anchor: Temporal sensitivity ... e_1 is current and e_2 is stale. We cannot treat them as identical. But Stale(e_2)\neq Delete(e_2). TemporalValidity affects contribution, not historical existence. ... A 2024 architecture document can still be valuable evidence about what existed in 2024, even if it is not
rows.statement: States temporal sensitivity: stale evidence has reduced contribution but is never deleted (Stale ≠ Delete); temporal validity affects contribution, not historical existence — a 2024 document remains valid evidence about 2024 even if not about today.

rows.anchor: Context sensitivity ... Contribution(e,P,C) ... Contribution(e,P,C_1) \neq Contribution(e,P,C_2) is perfectly legitimate. ... relevant to historical architecture reconstruction; irrelevant to a production migration decision; highly relevant to an audit of the 2024 environment. Evidence has no univer
rows.statement: States context sensitivity: the same evidence can legitimately have different contributions in different contexts (illustrated by 'Nexus 3.69' being relevant/irrelevant/highly-relevant depending on the question asked) — 'Evidence has no universal relevance.'

rows.anchor: Provenance preservation ... Basis(EA)\subseteq E ... EA\rightarrow EvidenceLineage must be recoverable. This gives us auditability. A KnowledgeOS conclusion should be able to answer "Why do you believe this?" with an actual evidence graph.
rows.statement: States provenance preservation: EA must retain a recoverable evidence basis/lineage so a conclusion can answer 'Why do you believe this?' with an actual evidence graph.

rows.anchor: No evidence creation ... E=\emptyset then Agg(E)=NoEvidence not Agg(E)=0.5 and certainly not Agg(E)=Confirmed. This is a critical distinction between absence of evidence and neutral evidence.
rows.statement: States a no-evidence-creation axiom: aggregating the empty set must yield NoEvidence, never a neutral scalar (0.5) or Confirmed — distinguishing absence-of-evidence from neutral-evidence.

rows.anchor: No certainty creation from aggregation alone ... StrongEvidence\not\Rightarrow Truth. Instead StrongEvidence \Rightarrow StrongSupport under the policy. Then another rule determines whether StrongSupport \Rightarrow AcceptedAssertion. That is a conclusion policy, not an evidence law.
rows.statement: States StrongEvidence ⇏ Truth; strong evidence only yields StrongSupport under policy, and whether StrongSupport becomes an AcceptedAssertion is a separate conclusion-policy decision, not an evidence law.

rows.anchor: This gives us three mathematical layers ... Layer A — Evidence aggregation E\rightarrow EA ... Layer B — Epistemic conclusion EA\rightarrow A ... Layer C — Decision A,I,P\rightarrow Decision ... Evidence\neq Conclusion\neq Decision
rows.statement: Formalizes three mathematical layers — Layer A Evidence aggregation (E→EA), Layer B Epistemic conclusion (EA→A), Layer C Decision (A,Ideal,Purpose→Decision) — reaffirming Evidence ≠ Conclusion ≠ Decision.

rows.anchor: Now we can define admissible aggregation ... Agg_\rho is admissible if it satisfies the applicable KnowledgeOS axioms \mathcal A=\{A_1,\ldots,A_n\} ... Agg_\rho\models\mathcal A ... This is the correct mathematical way to compare Bayesian, Dempster–Shafer, weighted, saturating, etc.
rows.statement: Defines admissibility formally: Agg_ρ ⊨ A (satisfies the axiom set A) as the correct way to compare candidate frameworks (Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, weighted, saturating).

rows.anchor: But not every axiom must be universal ... kernel invariants: A_1 Identity preservation, A_2 Provenance preservation, A_3 Contradiction preservation, A_4 No automatic independence ... policy properties: A_5 Corroboration rule, A_6 Saturation, A_7 Decision threshold, A_8 Probability interpretation. Th
rows.statement: Splits the axiom set into four kernel invariants (Identity preservation, Provenance preservation, Contradiction preservation, No automatic independence) versus four policy properties (Corroboration rule, Saturation, Decision threshold, Probability interpretation), called essential for DDD.

rows.anchor: The emerging KnowledgeOS Evidence Constitution ... E-K1 — Evidence identity ... E-K2 — No duplicate inflation ... E-K3 — Provenance preservation ... E-K4 — Dependency awareness ... E-K5 — Unknown is not independent ... E-K6 — Contradiction preservation ... E-K7 — Context dependence ... E-K8 — Tempor
rows.statement: Provisionally formulates a ten-item candidate 'KnowledgeOS epistemic constitution': E-K1 Evidence identity (e=e, explicitly represented), E-K2 No duplicate inflation, E-K3 Provenance preservation (Assessment⇒Basis), E-K4 Dependency awareness, E-K5 Unknown is not independent, E-K6 Contradiction preservation, E-K7 Context dependence, E-K8 Temporal preservation (Stale≠Deleted), E-K9 No truth by aggregation (EvidenceAssessment≠Truth), E-K10 No decision by aggregation (EvidenceAssessment≠Decision).

rows.anchor: Now test candidate mathematics ... Maximum ... Avoids duplicate inflation ... Cannot represent cumulative corroboration well ... Mean ... Simple ... Duplicate-sensitive; dilution problems ... Weighted sum ... Flexible ... Weights become policy assumptions ... Bayesian ... Requires priors, likelihood
rows.statement: Compares nine candidate aggregation frameworks (Maximum, Mean, Weighted sum, Saturating aggregation, Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, Possibility theory, Argumentation frameworks, Graph-based evidence models) against strengths/problems, concluding there is probably no single universal KnowledgeOS evidence algebra — a Kernel + Pluggable Assessment Calculi architecture is mathematically stronger.

rows.anchor: The architecture now looks like this ... RAW INPUTS → Evidence → Identity/Lineage/Dependency/Context/Validity → Evidence Graph → Assessment Calculus ρ → Evidence Assessment → Conclusion / Conflict → Knowledge State → Zero/Lord/Sarathi ... the calculus is a replaceable policy component.
rows.statement: Diagrams the full pipeline from raw inputs through Evidence, identity/lineage/dependency/context/validity processing, an Evidence Graph, a replaceable Assessment Calculus ρ, Evidence Assessment, Conclusion/Conflict, Knowledge State, to Zero/Lord/Sārathi.

rows.anchor: Step 4 conclusion ... We are no longer asking "Which formula gives the best confidence score?" We are asking "Which mathematical assessment calculi satisfy the epistemic and domain invariants of KnowledgeOS?" ... \mathcal C_{admissible} = \{\rho\mid Agg_\rho\models\mathcal A_{kernel}\} ... \mathcal
rows.statement: Reframes Step 4's achievement as reformulating the question from 'best confidence formula' to 'which calculi satisfy KnowledgeOS's epistemic/domain invariants', formalized as the admissible-calculus set C_admissible={ρ | Agg_ρ⊨A_kernel}, with domain policies allowed to add axioms (A_ρ⊇A_kernel).

rows.anchor: Step 5 — The next problem ... What exactly is the mathematical object being aggregated? Is it Evidence strength? Belief? Likelihood? Support? Arguments? Information gain? These are not interchangeable mathematical objects. ... Step 5 — Define the semantic domain of evidence contribution
rows.statement: Poses Step 5's question — what mathematical object is actually being aggregated (evidence strength, belief, likelihood, support, arguments, or information gain — explicitly not interchangeable) — as a prerequisite before choosing between Bayesian, belief-function, possibility, or argumentation formalisms.

sources.note: The originating proposal (and its two nested self-reviews) for a class-indexed, three-valued satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r) in {top,bot,U}, defined separately per eight requirement classes (content, evidence, provenance, epistemic-status, consistency, governance, temporal, operational) with Kleene-conjunctive composition for composite requirements, explicitly kept at candidate/[PROP] status pending a Factivity Repair Experiment, and later downgraded further to treat Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal as the primary object with Sat_c only a tested projection.

rows.anchor: Two of the three proposed repairs work, and they are the same intervention: stop calling it knowledge. ... it removes the blocker the review named ... Sat should therefore stay [PROP]
rows.statement: Verdict: R1 and R2 are the genuine repairs and share one intervention (stop calling attribution knowledge); the experiment removes the factivity-based objection to defining Sat but Sat should remain [PROP] for other, independent reasons (Zero's three-way ambiguity, undefined status order, unproven class exhaustiveness).

rows.anchor: Sat(K_t,r) in {top,bot,U} where top=established satisfied; bot=established violated; U=cannot currently be determined. That third value is important. Unknown must not silently become false.
rows.statement: Defines the core three-valued satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r) and states the guiding principle that Unknown must never silently collapse into False.

rows.anchor: R = R_content U R_evidence U R_provenance U R_epistemic U R_consistency U R_governance U R_temporal U R_operational ... Sat(K_t,r) = Sat_c(K_t,r) if r in R_c
rows.statement: Partitions the requirement universe into eight classes (content, evidence, provenance, epistemic-status, consistency, governance, temporal, operational) and makes Sat class-indexed rather than one universal predicate.

rows.anchor: p notin Content(K_t) does not necessarily mean not-p in Content(K_t). Absence is not negation. ... Evidence existence != evidence sufficiency ... Evidence != Truth.
rows.statement: States two foundational non-collapse distinctions for the content and evidence classes: absence is not negation, and evidence existence is not evidence sufficiency, evidence is not truth.

rows.anchor: the review says: Strong candidate [DEF] Sat: K x R -> {top,bot,U}. I would change that to: [PROP] Candidate common satisfaction interface ... because our latest simulation has already exposed a fundamental issue: factivity vs Gamma-determinacy.
rows.statement: First self-review downgrades Sat from a proposed [DEF] to [PROP], citing the v1.1 factivity/Gamma-determinacy impossibility as the reason it cannot yet be mathematically closed.

rows.anchor: We have not yet derived Sat; we have derived the need for a satisfaction mechanism. ... K_t, r, Gamma_t -[evaluation semantics]-> epistemic evaluation -> Delta_t ... investigating whether that evaluation can legitimately be represented by {top,bot,U}.
rows.statement: Second self-review (a meta-review of the first) sharpens the distinction further: only the need for a satisfaction mechanism has been derived, not Sat itself; recommends investigating an evaluation-semantics object before assuming the three-valued codomain.

rows.anchor: The eight definitions I gave previously are therefore still useful. But I would now label them: Sat_c Formal Candidate Specification v0.1 -- not implementation. ... we absolutely can define all eight Sat_c functions now without implementing them.
rows.statement: Establishes the 'define != implement' discipline that governs the rest of the Sat_c research thread: specify the eight class functions as a v0.1 candidate without writing executable code for them.

rows.anchor: I would change that to: [PROP] Candidate common satisfaction interface Sat: K x R -> {top,bot,U} ... So we cannot yet say that Sat has been mathematically closed.
rows.statement: Downgrades the proposed Sat definition from a strong candidate [DEF] to [PROP] because the factivity-vs-Gamma-determinacy obstruction has not yet been repaired.

rows.anchor: 3-valued semantics: candidate and 4-valued semantics: hypothesis/question rather than choosing either now.
rows.statement: Declines to choose between three-valued and four-valued (contradiction-inclusive) satisfaction semantics, keeping both explicitly open pending further research.

rows.anchor: M-3. value ∘ Eval_c is lossy, concentrated at U. T, F, C, UNDEFINED each receive one distinct evaluation situation; U receives nine, spanning [OPEN], [PROP] and [NEG] statuses.
rows.statement: M-3: the value-composed-with-Eval_c projection is lossy and concentrated at U -- T/F/C/UNDEFINED each receive exactly one distinct evaluation situation while U receives nine, spanning [OPEN]/[PROP]/[NEG] statuses, destroying exactly the distinction the theory most needs (epistemic insufficiency vs theory incompleteness vs context absence vs world unobservability).

rows.anchor: M-5. Blocked-class contagion. Under Kleene conjunction with five of eight evaluator classes undefined, every composite requirement of arity ≥ 4 is permanently U. ... The residual blockage is attributable to exactly two classes: status (⪰ undefined) and consistency (Contr undefined).
rows.statement: M-5: under Kleene conjunction with five of eight Sat_c evaluator classes undefined, every composite requirement of arity>=4 is permanently U; supplying three candidate evaluators halved low-arity contagion but changed nothing at arity>=7; the residual blockage is attributable to exactly two classes, status (>= undefined) and consistency (Contr undefined).

rows.anchor: ⪰ (the epistemic-status ordering) and Contr (the contradiction predicate) are the entire residual blockage of Sat. They are not independent ... Four open items are one decision.
rows.statement: The status ordering (>=) and the contradiction predicate (Contr) are the entire residual blockage of Sat and are not independent: the only total, three-valued contradiction repair preserving absence!=negation routes Sat_content through Sat_consistency, with Contr carrying the fourth-value question -- so four apparently separate open items reduce to one decision.

rows.anchor: N-2 -- define Contr, and the fourth value with it. ... any codomain extension must extend the Zero readings in the same step, or closure silently swallows the new value. Four open items, one decision.
rows.statement: N-2: define the contradiction predicate Contr and the fourth truth value together -- this unblocks consistency and content, carries the codomain question, and per D-0 any codomain extension must extend the Zero readings in the same step or closure silently swallows the new value.

rows.anchor: N-3 -- define ⪰. With Contr, it is the entire residual contagion. Both are currently used by the specification and defined nowhere.
rows.statement: N-3: define the epistemic-status ordering (>=), which together with Contr is the entire residual contagion; both are currently used by the specification but defined nowhere.

rows.anchor: any claim that an epistemic cycle is generative, healthy, progressive, spiral-like or improving must specify the ordering or criterion under which successive states are considered better. ... raw hits 2254, excluded as false positives 461, genuine epistemic-progress claims 1793, with an ordering nearby 302 (16.8%), without any ordering 1491 (83.2%).
rows.statement: Runs a corpus-wide progress-claim audit under the rule that any generative/healthy/progressive/spiral/improving claim must specify its ordering criterion: of 2254 raw hits, 461 are excluded as false positives, leaving 1793 genuine epistemic-progress claims, of which only 302 (16.8%) have a nearby ordering and 1491 (83.2%) specify none.

experiment.hypothesis: Progress/improvement claims about epistemic cycles in the corpus generally fail to specify an ordering criterion
experiment.setup: text search for progress/improvement-related terms across the corpus
experiment.assumptions: terms like convergence/improvement genuinely refer to K_t claims unless excluded as false positives
experiment.method: search, classify hits as genuine epistemic-progress claims vs false positives (e.g. an unrelated research-lane folder name), then check for a nearby explicit ordering/criterion
experiment.result: 1793 genuine claims, 302 (16.8%) with an ordering, 1491 (83.2%) without
experiment.interpretation: the vast majority of progress claims are currently unfalsifiable since the epistemic-status ordering is undefined
experiment.limitations: 'nearby ordering' detection may itself have false negatives/positives
experiment.conclusion: [EXP]

rows.anchor: Self-correction: my first run reported '84% of 2254'. 461 of those hits were the word 'convergence' in the name of the other research lane (three_model_convergence/), plus process improvement and source convergence -- none of them claims about K_t improving. Corrected before reporting. The headline figure barely moves (84% → 83%); the denominator was wrong by 20%.
rows.statement: Explicit self-correction: the first audit run miscounted the denominator by including 461 false-positive hits (a folder name 'three_model_convergence/', process-improvement mentions, source-convergence mentions unrelated to K_t claims), a 20% denominator error corrected before reporting, though the headline percentage barely moved (84%->83%).

rows.anchor: 83% of genuine progress claims in the corpus specify no ordering. Since ⪰ is undefined, all 1491 are unfalsifiable as stated -- not wrong, but not checkable either.
rows.statement: [EXP]: because the epistemic-status ordering (>=) remains undefined, all 1491 unordered progress claims in the corpus are unfalsifiable as stated -- not wrong, but not checkable.

rows.anchor: category check needs a declared lens register [OPEN]. progress audit needs ⪰ [OPEN] -- 83% of claims rest on it. stagnation predicate needs ⪰ (a count will not do) [OPEN]. ⪰ is not one open item among several. It is load-bearing for 1491 existing claims, for the stagnation predicate, and for any future statement that a cycle improves.
rows.statement: [INF]: all three checks converge on the same blocker, the undefined epistemic-status ordering (>=): the category check needs a declared lens register, the progress audit needs >= for 83% of its claims, and the stagnation predicate needs >= (a count is insufficient) -- making >= not merely one open item among several but load-bearing for 1491 existing corpus claims plus the stagnation predicate plus any future progress claim.

rows.anchor: value ∘ Eval_c maps nine situations to one value, while π_V(B) similarly destroys the distinctions carried by the richer boundary. ... The projection intentionally identifies states that the theory may need to distinguish. That is a much better diagnosis [than 'U is too vague'].
rows.statement: Reframes the M-3 finding (value-composed-Eval_c collapsing nine situations to U) as an instance of the general induced-equivalence phenomenon: the projection intentionally identifies states the theory may need to keep distinct, a stronger diagnosis than merely 'U is too vague.'

rows.anchor: Sat_c = π_value ∘ Eval_c is perfectly legitimate provided we explicitly accept what it loses. ... lossy projection ≠ bad projection but: lossy projection used beyond its semantic scope = defective model.
rows.statement: Reframes Sat_c=pi_value o Eval_c as legitimate provided its information loss is explicit: lossy projection != bad projection, but a lossy projection used beyond its declared semantic scope = a defective model.

rows.statement: Consequence for the theory: an admissibility criterion that does not read the candidate count n is unsound at scale, and neither v1.2's Sat nor its standard satisfaction criterion S^epi currently has a candidate-count parameter -- left [OPEN], since adding one presupposes the still-undefined epistemic-status ordering.

sources.note: S0675/S0676's session-transfer synthesis document: converges the phase_measure_theory research thread into a candidate Core (P,T,B,I,E,K,R,H,Theta), a DDD bounded-context map, a Zero Lens admission test, Roberts measurement governance, Shani invariants, a Core Admission Matrix, and explicit corrections/prohibitions; declares itself a synthesis artifact, not primary authority. Its Core tuple closely parallels but is not identical to relational-structure-core-regime-model's Kfrak=(P,C,T,X,I,E,R,Lambda) (B0014) -- flagged as possibly the same evolving object, not confirmed.

rows.anchor: Knowledge is currently treated as a factive epistemic relation between a participant and domain content, situated in a context and time ... Information != Epistemic State != Knowledge != Measurement != Decision
rows.statement: Working definition of Knowledge: a factive epistemic relation between a participant and domain content, situated in a context and time, arising from an epistemic state formed through available information, evidence, inference, testimony, memory, perception, practice, or other admissible means; not reducible to any single representation, probability, measurement, or reasoning regime. Chain: Information != Epistemic State != Knowledge != Measurement != Decision.
invariants: Information, Epistemic State, Knowledge, Measurement and Decision are five distinct things, never collapsed

rows.anchor: Knowledge Space is a structured, potentially unbounded semantic/domain space ... It is not inherently a metric space, probability space, measure space, or differentiable manifold.
rows.statement: Working definition of Knowledge Space: a structured, potentially unbounded semantic/domain space containing entities, states, events, concepts, propositions, relations and institutional structures toward which knowledge can be directed; not inherently a metric, probability, or measure space, or a differentiable manifold -- a specialized regime may equip a selected region/representation with such structure.

rows.anchor: Lens / Source table: Williamson, Pritchard, Fagin et al., Gaerdenfors, Gelfond & Kahl, Brandom, Searle, Dretske, Floridi, Roberts, Aggoun & Elliott, Rudin -- What it contributed / Current architectural meaning
rows.statement: Synthesis table converting twelve prior external-lens research conclusions into current architectural meanings: Williamson (knowledge is factive, keep KnowledgeAttribution distinct from belief/evidence/probability/measurement); Pritchard (prevent epistemic state, knowledge and representation from being collapsed); Fagin et al. (participant and epistemic state are core candidates, projections are agent-relative); Gaerdenfors (knowledge/epistemic state is temporally dynamic and non-monotonic, via expansion/contraction/revision); Gelfond & Kahl (reasoning is regime-specific; historical inputs and derived conclusions must be separable); Brandom (knowledge-bearing content has inferential/normative relations, assertion is not knowledge itself); Searle (institutional meaning belongs to bounded contexts/regimes, not universally to Kernel); Dretske (information is an input relation, not automatically knowledge); Floridi (boundary and representation must remain distinct); Roberts (measurement governance must validate every quantitative regime, no arbitrary KnowledgeScore); Aggoun & Elliott (probabilistic filtering is a regime, not the definition of KnowledgeOS); Rudin (use the minimum mathematical structure justified by a regime, do not impose analysis on the Kernel).

rows.anchor: Domain / semantic space Omega_D ... Epistemic state space Omega_E ... They are related, but they are not the same mathematical object.
rows.statement: Separates the domain/semantic space Omega_D (entities, states, events, concepts, propositions, institutional structures) from the epistemic state space Omega_E (participant-specific states, commitments, hypotheses, beliefs, knowledge attributions): related, but not the same mathematical object.

rows.anchor: Epistemic state is a participant's current structured epistemic position ... Numerical confidence is not a Core primitive because its measurement scale is regime-dependent.
rows.statement: Epistemic state is defined as a participant's current structured epistemic position, potentially containing commitments, hypotheses, accepted/rejected propositions, inferential links and other contextual information; numerical confidence is explicitly excluded as a Core primitive because its measurement scale is regime-dependent.
invariants: numerical confidence is never a Core primitive

rows.anchor: Information, evidence and reliability must remain distinct. ... Do not store "reliability = 0.95" as an intrinsic property of Information unless a regime explicitly defines and measures it.
rows.statement: Information item (source, time, content reference, provenance, context), Evidence relation (EvidenceSupports(i,p,regime/context)), and Reliability assessment (Reliability_R(source, task/context)) must remain three distinct structures; reliability must never be stored as an intrinsic property of Information unless a regime explicitly defines and measures it.
invariants: reliability is never an intrinsic property of Information absent an explicit regime

rows.anchor: Candidate Core Vocabulary: Participant / Time / Context-Boundary / Information-Observation / Epistemic State / Knowledge Attribution / History-Provenance / Transition / Typed Relation -- Strong Core candidates; Confidence / Reliability / Metric / Probability / Measure / Conditional expectation / Entropy -- Regime-derived
rows.statement: Candidate Core vocabulary table classifying each concept as Core or regime-derived with a reason: Participant, Time/temporal reference, Context/Boundary, Information/Observation, Epistemic State, Knowledge Attribution, History/Provenance, Transition and Typed Relation are (strong or provisional) Core candidates; Confidence, Reliability, Metric, Probability, Measure, Conditional expectation, and Entropy/information gain are regime-derived, each requiring its own measurement/probability/metric semantics.

rows.anchor: Do not make KnowledgeOS a giant universal domain ontology. Treat the Kernel as a platform/substrate bounded context ... KnowledgeOS Core | +-- Epistemic Context +-- Evidence Context +-- Representation Context +-- Inference Context +-- Measurement Context +-- Institutional Context +-- Decision Context
rows.statement: DDD lens: do not make KnowledgeOS a giant universal domain ontology; treat the Kernel as a platform/substrate bounded context, with seven specialized bounded contexts (Epistemic, Evidence, Representation, Inference, Measurement, Institutional, Decision) owning their own concepts unless Zero Lens shows a concept is genuinely shared, identity-stable and regime-independent. Anti-corruption rule: a probabilistic context must not redefine 'knowledge' as posterior probability; a metric context must not redefine it as a point in a metric space; an institutional context must not redefine all knowledge as status functions.
invariants: specialized bounded-context mathematics/vocabulary must never redefine Core knowledge semantics

rows.anchor: Semantic necessity ... Reconstruction necessity ... Regime independence ... Context independence ... Representation independence ... Temporal identity ... Invariant significance ... Contradiction test ... Ownership ... Admission rule: "useful" is not enough.
rows.statement: Zero Lens Phase 1 Admission Test: nine criteria a candidate Core concept must satisfy -- semantic necessity (does the Core model fail without it?), reconstruction necessity (derivable from other preserved Core structures?), regime independence (survives removal of probabilistic/metric/logical/measurement/institutional regimes?), context independence (identity stable across bounded contexts?), representation independence (independent of SQL/graph/JSON/embeddings/language/UI?), temporal identity (needs persistent identity across time?), invariant significance (removing it makes an invariant unverifiable?), contradiction test (removal collapses semantically distinct cases?), and ownership (Kernel genuinely owns its lifecycle vs another bounded context). Admission rule: 'useful' is not enough -- a concept becomes a strong Core candidate only if its removal creates a genuine semantic/reconstruction boundary failure.
invariants: no concept is admitted to Core merely because it is useful

rows.anchor: Regime R = (DomainModel, Semantics, Mathematics, Inference, Measurement) ... Projection_R(CoreState, Context, Participant) -> RegimeModel -> DerivedResult
rows.statement: Defines a Mathematical Regime Model: a regime is a structure-adding interpretation over a Core projection, formalized as R=(DomainModel,Semantics,Mathematics,Inference,Measurement), with Projection_R(CoreState,Context,Participant) -> RegimeModel -> DerivedResult; nine example regimes are tabulated (Logical, Nonmonotonic, Metric/Topological, Probabilistic, Filtering, Measurement, Statistical, Causal, Institutional) each with its example mathematics and the question it answers.

rows.anchor: Empirical relation -> Representation theorem -> Scale type -> Uniqueness / admissible transformations -> Meaningful operations -> Measurement result. MeasurementResult = (Value, Status, Scale, Regime) ... Zero and UNKNOWN are different. ... Do not aggregate Coverage + Evidence + Confidence + Stability into a scalar unless a valid measurement construction justifies the scale operations.
rows.statement: Measurement Governance (Roberts Lens): before any metric becomes a KnowledgeOS analytical quantity, define the empirical relational structure first, following the chain Empirical relation -> Representation theorem -> Scale type -> Uniqueness/admissible transformations -> Meaningful operations -> Measurement result; MeasurementResult=(Value,Status,Scale,Regime) with Status in {VALID,UNKNOWN,NOT_APPLICABLE,NOT_COMPUTABLE}, and a valid measurement equal to zero is explicitly distinct from 'we do not know the value' (UNKNOWN). No universal KnowledgeScore: do not aggregate Coverage+Evidence+Confidence+Stability into a scalar unless a valid measurement construction justifies the scale operations; prefer a vector of measurable properties until a representation theorem supports aggregation.
invariants: zero and UNKNOWN are different measurement statuses
no scalar KnowledgeScore without a representation-theorem-justified aggregation

rows.anchor: Shani Invariants for the New Session: Historical integrity / Event identity / Factivity / Regime isolation / Provenance preservation / Information/knowledge separation / Measurement validity / Context isolation / State reconstructibility / Unresolved honesty
rows.statement: Ten named invariants for the next session: historical integrity (Core history is append-only/immutable, later interpretations do not rewrite earlier observations); event identity (multiple events may share a timestamp; identity must not depend on timestamp uniqueness); factivity (a knowledge attribution must not be semantically certified while its proposition is false under the applicable truth model); regime isolation (a specialized mathematical regime must not silently redefine Core semantics); provenance preservation (knowledge-bearing claims/attributions must have reconstructible provenance); information/knowledge separation (information, evidence, belief, knowledge and decision remain distinct types/relations); measurement validity (no numerical measurement accepted without declared semantics, scale and admissible operations); context isolation (bounded-context semantics do not silently become universal Kernel law); state reconstructibility (where reconstruction is promised, the relevant state is derivable from preserved history plus declared regime); unresolved honesty (UNRESOLVED means current evidence does not justify a unique conclusion, it is not evidence in favor of the unresolved claim).

rows.anchor: Do not define KnowledgeOS as a single metric, measure or probability space. Do not define filtration as knowledge ... Do not interpret martingale as stable knowledge, submartingale as learning, or supermartingale as forgetting. Do not interpret Radon-Nikodym non-existence as universal epistemic incomparability. Do not treat confidence/reliability as intrinsic Information properties ... Do not treat truth as a numerical measurement scale. Do not assume all time is a global total order ... Do not require all Contexts to be internally contradiction-free ... Do not use "productive tension" as a permanent substitute for typed distinctions ... Do not reopen the literature review unless Phase 1 encounters a genuinely new formal gap
rows.statement: Eleven explicit corrections to carry into the new session: do not define KnowledgeOS as a single metric/measure/probability space; do not define filtration as knowledge (it is information history in a probabilistic regime); do not define conditional expectation as knowledge (it is one projection operator in a filtering regime); do not interpret martingale as stable knowledge, submartingale as learning, or supermartingale as forgetting; do not interpret Radon-Nikodym non-existence as universal epistemic incomparability; do not treat confidence/reliability as intrinsic Information properties (they are regime-derived); do not treat truth as a numerical measurement scale; do not assume all time is a global total order (distributed systems may need partial/logical ordering); do not require all Contexts to be internally contradiction-free unless a specific logical regime requires it; do not use 'productive tension' as a permanent substitute for typed distinctions -- classify every tension by semantic level, context, question type and conditions; do not reopen the literature review unless Phase 1 encounters a genuinely new formal gap unresolvable from the current corpus.

lineage_claims.target: prior session reasoning that risked equating filtration/conditional-expectation/martingale-family constructs with knowledge itself
