rows.anchor: Phase 1 -- Core Formalization: establish the minimal, domain-independent relational and temporal structure ... 14.1 Phase 1A -- Architectural Convergence. Status: substantially complete. ... 14.2 Phase 1B -- Core Admission & Formalization. This is the active work for the new session.
rows.statement: Defines Phase 1 as Core Formalization (establishing the minimal domain-independent relational/temporal structure to represent, preserve and reconstruct knowledge-bearing activity while keeping specialized mathematical semantics outside the Core), split into Phase 1A Architectural Convergence (status: substantially complete) and Phase 1B Core Admission & Formalization (the active next-session work, converting the candidate architecture into a mathematically typed, DDD-bounded Core), with nine required Phase 1B deliverables: Core Relational Model, Core Admission Register, Ubiquitous Language, Relation Catalogue, State & Transition Model, Invariant Catalogue, Context Map, Regime Contract Catalogue, and Open Questions/UNRESOLVED Register.

rows.anchor: Proposed Core Admission Matrix: Participant / Temporal reference / Context-Boundary / Observation-Information reference / Epistemic State / Knowledge Attribution / History-Provenance / Transition -- Yes; Confidence / Reliability / Metric / Probability measure / Filtration / Conditional expectation / Entropy -- No; Truth valuation -- Semantic, not numerical Core field
rows.statement: Core Admission Matrix assigning each candidate a Core?/reason verdict: Participant, Temporal reference, Context/Boundary (split responsibility), Observation/Information reference, Epistemic State (provisional), Knowledge Attribution, History/Provenance, and Transition (provisional) are admitted to Core; Confidence, Reliability, Metric, Probability measure, Filtration, Conditional expectation, and Entropy are rejected as regime constructs; Truth valuation is semantic (preserve reference/assessment) but not a numerical Core field.

rows.anchor: Every Core concept has one controlled definition. ... No concept is Core merely because it is useful. No quantitative result is accepted without a measurement model. Every unresolved claim records evidence class and reasoning base.
rows.statement: Twelve Phase 1 Gate Criteria: every Core concept has one controlled definition; an explicit DDD type or relation type; every persistent concept has an identity rule and lifecycle semantics; every relation has source/target/semantics; every historical record has provenance and stable identity; every candidate Core concept has passed Zero Lens; every invariant is classified as Core/semantic/institutional/regime-specific; every mathematical construct has explicit regime ownership; no concept is Core merely because it is useful; no quantitative result is accepted without a measurement model; every unresolved claim records evidence class and reasoning base.

rows.anchor: Use one proposition and trace it end-to-end ... p = "Election E is valid." Trace: Observation -> Information history -> Evidence relation -> Epistemic state -> Belief/commitment -> Knowledge attribution candidate -> Truth assessment -> Logical measurement regime -> Probabilistic regime (if justified) -> Measurement (if justified) -> Decision -> Historical record.
rows.statement: Recommends a first concrete test: trace one proposition end-to-end through the full model rather than discussing the ontology abstractly, e.g. p='Election E is valid', through Observation -> Information history -> Evidence relation -> Epistemic state -> Belief/commitment -> Knowledge attribution candidate -> Truth assessment -> Logical measurement regime -> Probabilistic regime (if justified) -> Measurement (if justified) -> Decision -> Historical record; the same preserved substrate should be processed by more than one regime to test whether the proposed Core is genuinely regime-independent.

rows.anchor: Is Epistemic State an entity, value object or derived state? ... Is Context identical to a DDD bounded context? ... What exactly is Knowledge Attribution? ... What is the minimal relation set? ... Which transitions are Core vs regime-specific? ... Can the Core reconstruct a participant state? ... Which measurements are genuinely measurable? ... When does measure theory materially help?
rows.statement: Eight open questions the new session must resolve: is Epistemic State an entity, value object or derived state; is Context identical to a DDD bounded context (probably distinguish Knowledge Boundary from Bounded Context); what exactly is Knowledge Attribution (relation first, entity/record only if history/audit requires identity); what is the minimal relation set; which transitions are Core vs regime-specific; can the Core reconstruct a participant state (run a replay experiment); which measurements are genuinely measurable (apply Roberts, prove/reject each candidate metric); and when does measure theory materially help (only for uncertainty/integration/filtering/Lp cases).

rows.anchor: Do not create a universal KnowledgeScore. Do not make the Kernel a probability space. Do not make the Kernel an ontology of every domain concept. Do not put Kalman filtering, martingales, entropy or conditional expectation into Kernel law. Do not equate information coverage with knowledge. Do not equate confidence with knowledge. Do not equate truth with a measurement score. Do not treat "UNRESOLVED" as evidence for either side. ... Do not read another book merely because a new terminology gap appears
rows.statement: Ten explicit prohibitions for the new session: do not create a universal KnowledgeScore; do not make the Kernel a probability space; do not make the Kernel an ontology of every domain concept; do not put Kalman filtering, martingales, entropy or conditional expectation into Kernel law; do not equate information coverage with knowledge; do not equate confidence with knowledge; do not equate truth with a measurement score; do not treat 'UNRESOLVED' as evidence for either side; do not call two different abstraction levels contradictory without first aligning meaning/context/question type; do not read another book merely because a new terminology gap appears -- first test whether the gap can be formalized from the existing corpus.

rows.anchor: The research has reached the point where the main intellectual problem is no longer "What else can we read?" It is "Can we formalize the common substrate without accidentally importing the assumptions of one regime into the Core?" Senior recommendation: Proceed to Phase 1B Core Admission & Formalization.
rows.statement: Final transfer position: the central intellectual problem has shifted from 'what else can we read' to 'can we formalize the common substrate without accidentally importing the assumptions of one regime into the Core'; senior recommendation is to proceed to Phase 1B Core Admission & Formalization, keeping measure theory in scope as the preferred regime for probabilistic knowledge questions without making it the foundational ontology; success criterion is a Core small enough to survive multiple regimes, explicit enough to reconstruct knowledge-bearing history, and disciplined enough that new mathematics can be added without redefining KnowledgeOS's meaning.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Lens / Source table: Williamson, Pritchard, Fagin et al., Gaerdenfors, Gelfond & Kahl, Brandom, Searle, Dretske, Floridi, Roberts, Aggoun & Elliott, Rudin -- What it contributed / Current architectural meaning
rationale_evidence.statement: Synthesis table converting twelve prior external-lens research conclusions into current architectural meanings: Williamson (knowledge is factive, keep KnowledgeAttribution distinct from belief/evidence/probability/measurement); Pritchard (prevent epistemic state, knowledge and representation from being collapsed); Fagin et al. (participant and epistemic state are core candidates, projections are agent-relative); Gaerdenfors (knowledge/epistemic state is temporally dynamic and non-monotonic, via expansion/contraction/revision); Gelfond & Kahl (reasoning is regime-specific; historical inputs and derived conclusions must be separable); Brandom (knowledge-bearing content has inferential/normative relations, assertion is not knowledge itself); Searle (institutional meaning belongs to bounded contexts/regimes, not universally to Kernel); Dretske (information is an input relation, not automatically knowledge); Floridi (boundary and representation must remain distinct); Roberts (measurement governance must validate every quantitative regime, no arbitrary KnowledgeScore); Aggoun & Elliott (probabilistic filtering is a regime, not the definition of KnowledgeOS); Rudin (use the minimum mathematical structure justified by a regime, do not impose analysis on the Kernel).

aliases: Full Historical Genealogy and Reconciliation of the Transition Model

sources.note: Step 251's historical genealogy of at least 6 distinct transition-function formulations across the corpus (Q15's delta, Step 204's tau, Step 031's R, the 025-series Update, Steps 189/203's federated E->G->O, and Step 232's synthesis T), demoting Step 232 from canonical to synthesis-level status; introduces the 'layer conflation vs genuine contradiction' distinction as the explanation for much of the apparent historical inconsistency, while insisting some conflicts remain genuinely unresolved; also traces Transformation/State/Evidence/Observation term genealogies and identifies a missing epistemic-transition-function gap alongside the epistemic-status ladder.

rows.anchor: The corpus does not currently contain one transition algebra. It contains several transition formulations at different abstraction levels, plus genuinely unresolved competing models.
rows.statement: States the step's headline finding after tracing transition-function history: the corpus does not contain one transition algebra but several formulations at different abstraction levels plus genuinely unresolved competing models -- directly answering the question posed at the end of Step 250.

rows.anchor: delta: K x E -harpoonup-> K [Q15] ... This is structurally different from tau: S x C -> S [Step 204]. The former says an event transforms a knowledge state. The latter says a state plus context undergoes a contractually specified transition. ... delta != tau as a literal identity claim. At most delt
rows.statement: Distinguishes Q15's event-level transition delta:KxE-harpoonup->K from Step 204's context-contract transition tau:SxC->S as structurally different formulations answering different questions (an event transforming a state, vs a state-plus-context undergoing a contractually-specified transition), explicitly rejecting delta=tau as a literal identity claim while leaving open a weaker refinement relation delta~>tau.

rows.anchor: R(K_t,E_t,C_t,M_t,V_t,T_t) with epistemic outputs such as {Accepted, Unknown, Underdetermined, Conflicted, Invalid, RequiresValidation}. ... the epistemic output vocabulary types the result status, not the state. Therefore Step 031 should not be collapsed into Step 232's T. ... Reasoning/Assessment
rows.statement: Confirms Step 031's epistemic-reasoning function R(K,E,C,M,V,T) (6-valued status output: Accepted/Unknown/Underdetermined/Conflicted/Invalid/RequiresValidation) types a result status, not a resulting state, and must not be collapsed into Step 232's state-transition T -- reinforcing the Reasoning/Assessment != State-Transition separation independently reached in Step 250.

rows.anchor: T: S x E -> S union Error [Step 069] ... its codomain differs from delta:K x E -harpoonup-> K. ... T and delta may be representational variants of partial transition semantics. But equivalence is not yet proven in the corpus.
rows.statement: Compares Step 069's total-with-explicit-error-codomain transition T:SxE->S-union-Error against Q15's partial delta, hypothesizing they may be representational variants of the same partiality semantics (explicit Error value vs. undefinedness) but explicitly declines to claim equivalence without a formal encoding proof.

rows.anchor: Update(K_t,E_t,Omega,EC) [025-series] ... Revise / R / Update as possible epistemic-event instances of a partial transition: non-monotone current state + monotone history. This is a useful candidate unification. But it should remain PROPOSED RECONSTRUCTION rather than corpus fact.
rows.statement: Proposes classifying Revise/R/Update as instances of a partial-transition sub-family characterized by a non-monotone current state combined with a monotone history, explicitly kept as a PROPOSED RECONSTRUCTION rather than promoted to corpus fact.

rows.anchor: E_t -> G_t -> O_t [Steps 189/203] is different again. It is not obviously K_t -> K_{t+1}. Instead it looks like a federated processing architecture: Evidence -> Governance -> Outcome. ... It should not be forced into the same algebra.
rows.statement: Identifies Steps 189/203's Evidence->Governance->Outcome pipeline as a federated-processing architecture operating at a different layer from ordinary state transition, explicitly not to be forced into the same algebra as delta/tau/T.

rows.anchor: Step 232's K_{t+1}=T_t(K_t) is best understood as a later abstraction over several earlier strands. But the corpus has not yet demonstrated that T_t is a single operation capable of subsuming delta, tau, R, Update, Revise, ... without losing semantics. T_t is currently a synthesis-level abstraction.
rows.statement: Explicitly demotes Step 232's K_{t+1}=T_t(K_t) from historically canonical status to a synthesis-level abstraction over several earlier, semantically distinct strands (delta, tau, R, Update, Revise), since no proof shows T_t can subsume them without semantic loss.

rows.anchor: [Reconciliation matrix, 10 rows: Q15 compatible candidate; Q20 unresolved; Step 031 distinct; 025k possible sub-family; Step 049 placeholder; Step 069 unresolved equivalence; Steps 189/203 distinct; Step 204 compatible candidate; Step 205 partially unresolved; Step 232 not yet canonical]
rows.statement: Produces the mandated reconciliation matrix across 10 historical transition formulations, each scored on signature, primary layer, relationship to Step 232, and verdict (2 compatible candidates, 3 distinct, 2 unresolved, 1 placeholder, 1 partially unresolved, and Step 232 itself marked not yet canonical) -- deliberately avoiding a single unified verdict.

rows.anchor: The contradiction appears when these are treated as though they were the same function despite differing: domains; codomains; arities; semantics; failure models; context treatment. ... Transformation remains polysemous.
rows.statement: Traces the root cause of 'Transformation' polysemy to treating mathematically distinct functions (delta, tau, T, R) as though identical despite differing domains, codomains, arities, semantics, failure models and context treatment -- confirming and explaining the polysemy S1614 flagged as a term-overload problem.

rows.anchor: The corpus map records 7+ formalizations of Knowledge State and explicitly identifies state equality as undefined. Therefore we cannot yet assume K_t = S_t. At most S_t may be a state representation in one layer.
rows.statement: Traces the genealogy of the State symbol itself: the corpus records 7+ distinct formalizations of Knowledge State with state equality left undefined, so K_t=S_t (using two different historical notations interchangeably) cannot be assumed -- S_t may at most be one layer's state representation.

rows.anchor: evidence equivalence ~ is undefined and whether evidence belongs inside K_t remains unresolved. Therefore a transition delta(K,E) does not yet tell us whether E is: external input; part of K; lineage; provenance; or a separate evidence store.
rows.statement: Traces Evidence's genealogy across 4 named corpus sources (EXP-01 tuples, Step 031, Q14 structures, Steps 004/005 aggregation), finding evidence equivalence undefined and E's placement relative to K (external input, inside K, lineage, provenance, or separate store) unresolved even within the transition formulation delta(K,E).

rows.anchor: Observation != Evidence. This is explicitly ratified in the current non-collapse vocabulary. ... the chain World -Omega-> Observation should not be silently collapsed into World -> Evidence. That distinction matters for the transition genealogy.
rows.statement: Confirms Observation!=Evidence as an already-ratified corpus non-collapse, and shows it materially affects the transition genealogy since the World->Observation chain (via Omega:W->O) must not be silently treated as equivalent to a World->Evidence chain.

rows.anchor: status transitions follow the covering relation and cannot skip levels. The current corpus says this invariant is witnessed, but also explicitly identifies a missing transition calculus: the ladder tells us which states exist, but not yet what operation moves an item between them. ... Epistemic stat
rows.statement: Identifies a distinct gap in the epistemic-status ladder (invariant I-12, covering relation, no level-skipping): the corpus defines which epistemic states exist but not the operation that moves an item between them -- an epistemic transition function distinct from, and still missing alongside, the ordinary state transition delta/T.

rows.anchor: A state transition may actually contain at least two different transitions: Knowledge-object lifecycle (K -> K') and Epistemic-status transition (e_i -> e_j). ... K_{t+1}=T(K_t) may be too coarse to explain Status_t -> Status_{t+1}.
rows.statement: Argues 'state transition' actually conflates two distinct transitions -- knowledge-object lifecycle (K->K') and epistemic-status transition (e_i->e_j, constrained by the covering relation) -- concluding the abstract K_{t+1}=T(K_t) formulation may be too coarse to explain status evolution on its own.

rows.anchor: the different formulations appear to answer different questions [delta, tau, R, Update, E->G->O, K_{t+1}=T(K_t) each answering a distinct question]. Therefore the historical 'inconsistency' may partly be layer conflation, not necessarily theoretical contradiction. But we cannot declare all differenc
rows.statement: States the step's central methodological insight: the apparent proliferation of competing transition formulations partly reflects that each answers a genuinely different question (event application, contract-permitted transition, epistemic result of evidence, knowledge revision, federated outcome, abstract state evolution) rather than pure contradiction -- but explicitly refuses to let this insight excuse away the formulations that remain genuinely unresolved competing models rather than merely different layers.

rows.anchor: we must explicitly reject these unsupported equations: delta=tau; R=T; Validate=T; Event=Delta-K; K=S; History=Lineage; unless the corpus later provides the necessary definitions and mappings.
rows.statement: Lists 6 specific unsupported equations to be explicitly rejected pending corpus-provided mappings: delta=tau, R=T, Validate=T, Event=Delta-K, K=S, and History=Lineage -- the last consistent with the S1600/S1603/S1612 finding that provenance and lineage/history are distinct objects.

rows.anchor: The candidate kernel cannot yet contain merely (K,T). It must at least distinguish State from Transition from Assessment from Decision from Event and History/Lineage. Whether these are all primitives of one final mathematical object is still open. ... Transition System = typed family of related tran
rows.statement: States the step's final conclusion and the most important kernel-design consequence: the candidate kernel must distinguish at least 6 roles (State, Transition, Assessment, Decision, Event, History/Lineage) rather than collapsing to (K,T); the strongest current hypothesis is that the Transition System is a typed family of related structures, not one closed algebra, though final mathematical closure remains unproven -- directly aligning with the parallel verifier track's typed-family conclusion (S1603, S1612).

lineage_claims.quote: Step 252 should construct: Canonical Vocabulary / Polysemy Audit ... we cannot finalize K, T, or equality while their component vocabulary is itself polysemous.

rows.anchor: WORLD/SOURCES -> OBSERVATION/EVIDENCE -> INTERPRETATION/MODEL/HYPOTHESIS -> CLAIM/ASSERTION -> JUSTIFICATION/ASSESSMENT -> EPISTEMIC STANDING ... explicitly warns not to collapse layers merely because a mechanism can produce them. ... an observation may become evidence, but Observation not-equiv Evi
rows.statement: Situates Observation!=Evidence within a full 6-layer architectural pipeline (World/Sources -> Observation/Evidence -> Interpretation/Model/Hypothesis -> Claim/Assertion -> Justification/Assessment -> Epistemic Standing), explicitly warning against collapsing layers just because one mechanism happens to produce several of them in sequence.

rows.anchor: State currently has at least three meanings: Mathematical state S_t, Knowledge state K_t, Application/system state. These cannot be silently identified. ... State is currently polysemous. I would recommend that the final language use explicit qualifiers: Knowledge State, Epistemic State, Application
rows.statement: Names State the most dangerous overloaded word, with at least 3 distinct senses (mathematical S_t, knowledge K_t, application/system runtime state) that must not be silently identified; recommends explicit qualified terms (Knowledge State, Epistemic State, Application State, System State) as the fix.

rows.anchor: Calling all of them 'Transformation' produces semantic collapse [R for epistemic reasoning, delta for event/state transition, tau for context-contract transition, T for abstract state evolution]. ... Reserve Transformation as a mathematical umbrella only. Use more precise DDD names: Assess, Validate
rows.statement: Confirms Transformation as the most problematic overloaded term (already shown in Step 251 to cover 4 distinct functions R/delta/tau/T), recommending it be reserved only as a mathematical umbrella label while 8 more precise DDD operation names (Assess, Validate, Determine, Revise, Admit, Supersede, Apply Event, Transition Knowledge State) replace it in domain language -- explicitly a naming recommendation, not established vocabulary.

sources.note: The WorkItem aggregate root of BC-7, its lifecycle/authority parts, and the one-vs-two-aggregate question.

rows.anchor: Candidate A — Work Item Aggregate ... Result: passes every test. Critically, all four invariants are internal to it
rows.statement: WorkItem is tested and confirmed as the aggregate root: its identity, lifecycle, four invariants (I-1..I-4), and consistency boundary are all internal to a single JSON record, needing no cross-record data to enforce.

rows.anchor: Candidate B — Assignment Aggregate (rejected) ... I-1 is an invariant over the set of assignments, not over one.
rows.statement: Assignment is rejected as aggregate root because the single-mutation-owner invariant (I-1) spans the whole set of assignments and cannot be stated from inside one, and HANDOFF is atomic across two assignments, making Assignment an entity inside WorkItem, not a root.

rows.anchor: Candidate C — Workflow Aggregate (rejected — and reclassified) ... Workflow is a Value Object on the root, not an aggregate.
rows.statement: Workflow is rejected as aggregate root (it is a fixed classifier with no lifecycle or state of its own) and reclassified as a Value Object on the WorkItem root.

sources.note: Book chapter III.2 defines the EpistemicContract EC=eta(G,IdealState) as the goal-derived requirement set -- what must be known/satisfied for the inquiry to meet the Knower's standard -- the model's sole carrier of 'must' (Zero evaluates K_t against EC, nothing else holds obligations); requirements flow FROM goal-plus-standard TO contract, never back (an EC never edits its goal). Traces why the requirement carrier is needed at all, via the source's own reconstructed one-line argument 'Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone' and a three-line worked deployment example (rollback verified: unknown; firewall permitted: conflicting; architecture approval: missing) showing one goal can yield three DIFFERENT kinds of shortfall that a goal-as-evaluation-unit could never distinguish. Records the signature's history: the original ternary Zero(K,G,EC) was attacked by falsification (does G do any work inside Zero that EC doesn't already carry?), found no evidenced residual role, and was conservatively ruled to Zero(K,EC) (GN-19/R-2), retaining the ternary form only as historical lineage, with the underlying question held explicitly open rather than settled. States the resulting eta-totality open question (already indexed as OQ-1 in the open-questions-registry-oq1-12): neither totality (does G+IdealState fully determine EC?) nor a residual-G role is established by any evidence; closing acts named are a formal construction of eta or a demonstrated residual-consumer case; states the governing constraint that deeper explanation must never quietly settle an open architectural question.

rows.statement: TV-F-011 resolves eta's category status: as a function of (G,IdealState) alone, eta is provably NOT well-defined -- the same (G,IdealState) pair under different law/policy environments must yield different Epistemic Contracts, which the corpus's own richer form DeriveContract(G,S) (025e, with S drawn from Constitution/Policy/ADR/Rule/Scope/HumanInstruction/RiskModel/DomainModel/Law/Standard) already concedes by adding the source set S. Decomposes DeriveContract into source collection (a governance oracle), requirement extraction (computable for machine-readable sources, an oracle otherwise), a closure check Closed(EC) (computable, 025e supplies the checklist), and versioned publication (a governed act). Verdicts: eta(G,IdealState) total is REFUTED as a mathematical claim (a genuine category error, not merely unproven); DeriveContract(G,S)'s termination relative to its oracles is DERIVABLE BUT CONDITIONAL, provable in the T-K3 style once the oracle interface is fixed; uniqueness is explicitly NO, since contract versioning itself presupposes multiple legitimate contracts per goal. Proposes 'eta is a governance construction, not a mathematical function' as the disposition for OQ-1, sharpening GN-46's earlier 'totality relative to oracles' remark into a proven category distinction.

sources.note: Step 205's four rigorous DDD aggregate-derivation criteria (invariant ownership, atomicity required by an invariant, lifecycle containment, concurrency cost) and their application across ten candidate concepts, replacing noun-based aggregate grouping.

rows.anchor: We do not derive Aggregates from nouns. We derive them from invariants, transactional atomicity, identity, lifecycle and concurrency.
rows.statement: States the governing methodological rule for the whole step: aggregates must be derived from invariants/atomicity/identity/lifecycle/concurrency, deliberately resisting the temptation to create one aggregate per existing noun (EvidenceAggregate, AssessmentAggregate, DecisionAggregate, ...).

rows.anchor:
Agg=(I,O,B) ... B defines what must remain consistent atomically. Therefore: Aggregate
eq DatabaseTable. And: Aggregate
eq Entity. And: Aggregate
eq BoundedContext.
rows.statement: Defines an Aggregate as (Identity, OwnedState, InvariantBoundary), with the boundary B defining what must remain atomically consistent, explicitly distinct from a database table, an entity, or a bounded context.

rows.anchor: Owner(I_i)=Agg_j. If no aggregate can enforce the invariant locally, then one of three things is true: 1. the invariant is actually cross-context; 2. the model is missing a concept; 3. the proposed aggregate boundary is wrong.
rows.statement: First derivation criterion (invariant ownership): for each invariant, ask which object has enough information and authority to guarantee it; if none can, the invariant is cross-context, the model is missing a concept, or the proposed boundary is wrong -- far more rigorous than grouping objects by similarity.

rows.anchor: Atomicity must be required by an invariant. ... 'usually change together' is insufficient.
rows.statement: Second criterion (atomicity): two objects belong in one aggregate only if an actual invariant requires their atomic co-change, not merely that they usually change together.

rows.anchor: Lifecycle(B)\subseteq Lifecycle(A). This is evidence for containment. But lifecycle dependency alone is not enough.
rows.statement: Third criterion (lifecycle): if B cannot meaningfully exist without A, that is evidence for containment, but lifecycle dependency alone is insufficient if B has its own independent consistency boundary.

rows.anchor: ConcurrencyCost(A,B). An aggregate should be as small as possible while still protecting its invariants. Minimize aggregate size subject to Invariant preservation.
rows.statement: Fourth criterion (concurrency): frequently-independently-modified objects placed in one aggregate create contention costs; states the optimization principle of minimizing aggregate size subject to invariant preservation.

rows.anchor: Lifecycle(Proposition) \not\subseteq Lifecycle(Assessment). ... PropositionAggregate with assessments represented as separate knowledge objects or references.
rows.statement: Walks Proposition vs Assessment through the criteria: a proposition can exist before and receive multiple assessments over time, so its lifecycle is not contained by any one assessment's -- concluding PropositionAggregate is a candidate with assessments as separate objects/references, possibly owning only a CurrentAssessmentReference if a 'one active assessment per model/version' invariant exists.

rows.anchor: Evidence\neq Observation. ... EvidenceAggregate with: EvidenceSource and provenance information internally managed where the invariant requires it. ... I_E: Verified\Rightarrow Provenance\land Integrity.
rows.statement: Walks Evidence vs Observation: evidence can exist independently and originate from non-observation sources (documents, system records, external datasets, calculations), arguing against a universal ObservationWithEvidence aggregate; instead an EvidenceAggregate can own the verification invariant (Verified requires Provenance and Integrity).

rows.anchor: Reference is often preferable to containment.
rows.statement: States that Observation need not be owned by the Evidence Aggregate as a child entity, since Observation can have its own independent lifecycle (Captured->Corrected->Superseded) -- reference is often preferable to containment.

rows.anchor: I_A: Assessment \rightarrow (P,E,M,U,L). ... AssessmentAggregate may contain: EvidenceRef_1,...,EvidenceRef_n. This preserves aggregate independence.
rows.statement: Assessment is a strong aggregate candidate owning a TraceableBasis invariant (Assessment must reference Proposition, Evidence, Model, Uncertainty, Lineage), but must hold Evidence references, not embedded Evidence ownership, preserving aggregate independence.

rows.anchor: M_v\neq M_{v+1}. Thus: VersionedModelIdentity is required for reproducibility. This is especially important for AI models.
rows.statement: Model deserves its own independent aggregate/registry (ModelRegistry/ModelContext) rather than being embedded in Assessment, since multiple assessments can reference the same model and a referenced model version must never be silently mutated -- VersionedModelIdentity is required for reproducibility, especially for AI models.

rows.anchor: Uncertainty is a value/semantic component of Assessment, not automatically an Aggregate.
rows.statement: Concludes Uncertainty should not automatically become its own aggregate; at present it is a value/semantic component of Assessment, unless it independently develops its own lifecycle, calibration, or governance justifying separation.

rows.anchor: Policy should have identity/versioning independent from: Decision. A Decision should reference: PolicyVersion. It should not copy the whole mutable policy. ... ActionValid\Rightarrow ApplicablePolicyFound.
rows.statement: Policy is an independent aggregate candidate (its own versioned lifecycle, multiple decisions can depend on one version); a governed action's validity requires an applicable policy version found at that time, not a copied mutable policy.

rows.anchor: Authority_t\neq Authority_{t+1}. Therefore the decision record must preserve the authority basis at decision time. ... PresentAuthority\neq HistoricalAuthority.
rows.statement: Authority has its own independent lifecycle (an actor's authority can change over time), so a decision must preserve the authority basis at the time it was made -- PresentAuthority != HistoricalAuthority, a conditional aggregate candidate.

rows.anchor: I_D: FinalDecision \Rightarrow ValidDecisionBasis. ... Decision references Assessment; it does not own Assessment.
rows.statement: Decision is a strong aggregate candidate with invariant FinalDecision requires ValidDecisionBasis; explicitly references (never owns) Assessment, or Decision would become responsible for epistemic lifecycle, violating bounded responsibility.

rows.anchor: Action \xrightarrow{derivedFrom} DecisionRef. This preserves the distinction: Decision\neq Action. ... Action \rightarrow OutcomeObservation. ExecutionState\neq Outcome.
rows.statement: Action is a strong aggregate candidate (identity, target, authorization, status, execution info) that references rather than owns its originating Decision; Outcome is a low-confidence aggregate candidate since it may be produced by an external system, reinforcing ExecutionState != Outcome.

rows.statement: Identifies a governance-model gap: because AST-019's implementing session never registered a lane or recorded its runtime identity, the producer-verifier separation principle cannot be mechanically enforced for its future verification (no producer identity exists to exclude), and the operating model as written has no lane-shape at all for a human-authorized amendment slice landing on a STOPPED work item.

rows.statement: Observes that the accumulating list of barred identities across this multi-step governance saga has grown to 16 entries, to the point that the requirement for a genuinely fresh session (rather than any reused process) has become the sole remaining mechanism for fielding an eligible verifier at all -- recorded as a one-occurrence observation, not promoted to a general rule.

rows.anchor: Using an unverified capability to manufacture the authority to verify that capability makes the verification worthless. A PASS would rest on the subject's own correctness -- the thing in question.
rows.statement: States the circularity bar as a general governance principle: a candidate must never use the very capability it is appointed to verify (or any unauthorized capability) to manufacture its own activation, because doing so would make the eventual verification verdict rest on the subject's own unproven correctness -- self-identified independently by the candidate before any instruction forbade it.
invariants: verifier activation must never depend on the unverified capability under test

rows.statement: Extends the producer-verifier separation principle (R-34/EP-02) to defect remediation: the process that authored a governance defect may analyze it fully and recommend a remedy with grounds, but must not itself decide which recovery path (proceed with documented defect vs. discard and re-appoint) is taken -- that decision is reserved for the PO/ARB.

sources.note: The rigorous operator-typing discipline (S2269): typed kernel states, a seven-field operator contract, a state-preservation law, and five distinct kinds of operator preservation.

rows.anchor: We should not define operators merely because a Gītā concept sounds analogous. We need to define them so that every transformation K_t -op-> K_{t+1} is well-typed, mathematically valid, traceable, and preserves the invariants that make K_t a valid KnowledgeOS state. I would therefore separate operator semantics from the Gītā interpretation.
rows.statement: States the central methodological correction driving this file: operators must not be defined merely because a Gita concept sounds analogous; every transformation K_t --op--> K_{t+1} must be well-typed, mathematically valid, traceable, and invariant-preserving, with operator semantics kept strictly separate from Gita interpretation.

rows.anchor: E_t in E, S_t in S, ... R_t subseteq X x R x X ... K_t in K_valid where K_valid is the set of all valid KnowledgeOS states.
rows.statement: Requires each of the eight primitive components to carry a domain, type and validity constraint (E_t in calE, S_t in calS, etc., R_t subseteq X x R x X), so the real kernel state is K_t in K_valid, the set of all valid KnowledgeOS states -- the first mathematical requirement for a typed kernel state.

rows.anchor: Op = <Name, Input, Pre, Transform, Post, Inv, Evidence> ... Precondition Pre(K,x) ... Transformation T_op(K,x)=K' ... Postcondition Post(K,K',x) ... Invariants Inv(K')=true ... Evidence: why is the transformation justified? This last part is where the Gītā-inspired epistemic model becomes interesting, but it must not replace the mathematical contract.
rows.statement: Defines a seven-field operator contract Op = <Name, Input, Pre, Transform, Post, Inv, Evidence>: Input (what is consumed), Precondition Pre(K,x) (when allowed), Transformation T_op(K,x)=K' (the mapping), Postcondition Post(K,K',x) (what must hold after), Invariants Inv(K')=true (what must never be violated), and Evidence (why justified) -- the last field is where the Gita-inspired epistemic model may contribute, but explicitly must not replace the mathematical contract.

rows.anchor: K_t in K_valid implies op(K_t,x) in K_valid, provided the preconditions hold. In other words: Pre(K_t,x) and Inv(K_t) => Inv(K_{t+1}). This is the state-preservation law. An operator is therefore not allowed to arbitrarily modify knowledge.
rows.statement: States the state-preservation law: K_t in K_valid implies op(K_t,x) in K_valid provided preconditions hold, i.e. Pre(K_t,x) and Inv(K_t) implies Inv(K_{t+1}) -- an operator is not allowed to arbitrarily modify knowledge outside this constraint.

rows.anchor: Structural preservation: K_t in K_valid => K_{t+1} in K_valid ... Semantic preservation: K_t equiv K_{t+1} ... Provenance preservation: Pi_t -> Pi_{t+1} according to the provenance rules ... Monotonicity: K_t preceq K_{t+1}, but not every operator should be monotonic ... Information-changing operations: P_old -> P_retracted. That does not violate mathematics if the operator explicitly permits retraction.
rows.statement: Refines 'mathematical preservation' into five distinct kinds an operator may or may not guarantee: structural preservation (result stays in K_valid), semantic preservation (K_t equiv K_{t+1} under an appropriate semantic relation), provenance preservation (Pi_t -> Pi_{t+1} per provenance rules), monotonicity (K_t preceq K_{t+1}, explicitly not required of every operator), and information-changing operations (e.g. P_old -> P_retracted, which does not violate mathematics if the operator explicitly permits retraction).

rows.anchor: P_1 = System X is available. Later evidence indicates P_2 = System X is unavailable. The kernel should not simply overwrite P_1. ... P_1 -revision-> P_2 while preserving O_1,O_2,Pi,provenance and recording the relation R(P_1,contradicted-by,P_2) ... preserve historical truth about the knowledge process while changing the currently accepted state.
rows.statement: Worked example of the Revise operator: given P_1 ('System X is available') contradicted by later evidence P_2 ('System X is unavailable'), the kernel must not simply overwrite P_1; instead P_1 --revision--> P_2 while preserving O_1, O_2, provenance, and recording a relation R(P_1, contradicted-by, P_2), preserving historical truth about the knowledge process while changing the currently accepted state.

rows.anchor: Observe: Environment -> Observation ... Qualify: Observation x Context -> PropositionStatus ... Relate: KnowledgeElement^2 x RelationType -> Relation ... Revise: Proposition x Evidence -> Proposition' ... Act: Decision x Policy -> Action. This prevents type errors. And type errors are one of the strongest mathematical safeguards available to us.
rows.statement: Gives explicit typed signatures for five operators to prevent type errors (e.g. Action -> Entity being illegitimate unless explicitly defined): Observe: Environment->Observation; Qualify: Observation x Context -> PropositionStatus; Relate: KnowledgeElement^2 x RelationType -> Relation; Revise: Proposition x Evidence -> Proposition'; Act: Decision x Policy -> Action. States type-checking as 'one of the strongest mathematical safeguards available.'

rows.anchor: forall K_t,K_{t+1}: K_t -> K_{t+1} implies exists op, evidence ... No knowledge-state transition without an identifiable operation and justification. ... K1 -op +evidence+preconditions+provenance-> K2
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate core KnowledgeOS law -- 'no silent epistemic transition': for all K_t, K_{t+1}, K_t -> K_{t+1} implies there exists an identifiable op and evidence justifying it; an unattributed transition (K1 -> K2 with no op/evidence/preconditions/provenance) is invalid, described as exactly the deterministic assurance KnowledgeOS needs.

rows.anchor: Step 1 -- Define state types ... Step 2 -- Define validity invariants ... Step 3 -- Enumerate candidate operations ... Step 4 -- Give every operation a type signature ... Step 5 -- Define pre/postconditions ... Step 6 -- Define preservation laws ... Step 7 -- Define composability ... Step 8 -- Define reversibility/irreversibility ... Step 9 -- Define provenance effects ... Step 10 -- Only then map Gītā concepts onto the resulting algebra.
rows.statement: Proposes a rigorous ten-step research programme replacing philosophy-first operator discovery: (1) define state types, (2) define validity invariants, (3) enumerate candidate operations, (4) give every operation a type signature, (5) define pre/postconditions, (6) define preservation laws, (7) define composability, (8) define reversibility/irreversibility, (9) define provenance effects, (10) only then map Gita concepts onto the resulting algebra -- explicitly naming step 10 as critical (mapping last, not first).

rows.anchor: T_o: (K_t,D_t,V_t) -> (K_{t+1},D_{t+1},V_{t+1}) ... K_t in K_valid and Pre_o(K_t) implies K_{t+1} in K_valid. This is the fundamental preservation rule.
rows.statement: Formalizes a kernel operator as T_o: (K_t,D_t,V_t) -> (K_{t+1},D_{t+1},V_{t+1}), required to preserve mathematical validity: K_t in K_valid and Pre_o(K_t) implies K_{t+1} in K_valid -- the fundamental preservation rule.

rows.anchor: Input | What does Compare consume? ... State effect | How does K_t change? ... Primitive effect | Which of the 8 primitives change? ... Zero | Can it expose a gap? ... Buddhi | Is discrimination involved? ... Guna | Does operating mode affect it? ... Governance | Does authority enter the operation? That gives us an operator contract. ... O = <I,P,T,R,E,H,G> ... O: (K_t,X,C) -> (K_{t+1},E) subject to invariants.
rows.statement: Defines a Tactical Discovery questionnaire of 15 questions per candidate operator (Input, Output, Preconditions, Postconditions, State effect, Primitive effect, Evidence, Determinism, Idempotence, Reversibility, Provenance, Zero, Buddhi, Guna, Governance), condensed into a seven-field operator contract O=<I,P,T,R,E,H,G> [input state, preconditions, transformation, resulting state, evidence, history/provenance, governance constraints], more formally O: (K_t,X,C) -> (K_{t+1},E) subject to invariants -- a second, differently-shaped operator contract from the one in S2269.

rows.anchor: o: (K_t,X,C) -> (K_{t+1},E,H) ... Domain Dom(o), Preconditions Pre_o, Transformation T_o, Postconditions Post_o, Invariants I_o, Evidence E_o, History H_o. Then test: Closure, Determinism, Idempotence, Composability, Reversibility, Monotonicity where applicable.
rows.statement: Gives a further operator-contract variant o: (K_t,X,C) -> (K_{t+1},E,H), with seven fields to determine per operator (Dom, Pre, T, Post, I, E, H) and six algebraic properties to test where applicable (closure, determinism, idempotence, composability, reversibility, monotonicity).

rows.anchor: O_i = <Input, Precondition, Discrimination, Transformation, Postcondition, Evidence, History, Invariant> ... sources.note: Stephen Stigler's seven historical pillars of statistical reasoning used as an interrogation lens against a minimal Knowledge Kernel: statistical inference is about quantifying uncertainty, not eliminating it; central claims include that aggregation requires discarding information, information accumulates at a diminishing (root-n) rate, likelihood/P-values calibrate surprise rather than measure truth, intercomparison uses internal variation without external standards, regression/conditioning is directional (the Rule of Three is a trap), design/randomization creates the basis for inference, and residuals can be signal rather than noise.

rows.anchor: statistical inference is about quantification of uncertainty, not its elimination. ... A Kernel that treats knowledge as certainty (or even high confidence) may be missing the fundamental insight.
rows.statement: Most significant finding: the seven pillars are tools for managing uncertainty, not for 'knowing'; a Knowledge Kernel that treats knowledge as certainty or high confidence misses this.

rows.anchor: you gain information by discarding information. ... A Kernel that preserves all detail may be preserving noise, not signal.
rows.statement: Aggregation (Pillar 1): information gain sometimes requires data reduction (the mean discards individual variation to reveal signal); the architectural question is whether the Kernel preserves all data 'just in case' versus recognizing that discarding is sometimes required, and whether data reduction should be a first-class Kernel operation.

rows.anchor: the estimated accuracy varied as the square root of the number of trials. ... the second 20 observations are not as valuable as the first 20. ... each additional observation is worth less than the one before.
rows.statement: Information Measurement (Pillar 2): information accumulates at a diminishing root-n rate rather than linearly; a Kernel that assumes more data always equals proportionally more information misunderstands information accumulation and should weight information by marginal contribution.

rows.anchor: The P-value is not a measure of truth. It is a measure of surprise ... A Kernel that treats probabilities as 'truth values' or 'certainty levels' may be misrepresenting what statistical inference provides.
rows.statement: Likelihood (Pillar 3): the P-value calibrates surprise relative to a null hypothesis, not truth; a Kernel must distinguish calibrated probability (a comparison to a reference distribution) from probability treated as subjective belief or a truth value.

rows.anchor: Student's t-test uses only the data itself — the sample mean and sample standard deviation — to make inferences. No external standard is needed. This is radical self-reliance in inference.
rows.statement: Intercomparison (Pillar 4): statistical validity can be established from a data set's own internal variation without external criteria, but the analysis warns this 'radical self-reliance' can be abused ('in the wrong hands, as with most powerful tools'), raising the architectural question of when a Kernel should still require external standards.

rows.anchor: if you have two measures that are not perfectly correlated, and you select on one as extreme from its mean, the other is expected to be less extreme. This is not a biological phenomenon — it is a statistical necessity. ... The Rule of Three is a trap.
rows.statement: Regression (Pillar 5): the direction of conditioning changes the answer (regression to the mean as a statistical necessity, not a substantive phenomenon), and the ancient Rule of Three (proportional extrapolation) is systematically biased in the presence of variation and measurement error -- a Kernel assuming symmetric relationships or proportional extrapolation is architecturally flawed.

rows.anchor: The very act of randomization made possible valid inferences that did not lean on an assumption of normality or an assumption of homogeneity of material. ... Randomization creates a basis for inference. ... Design can even play a crucial role in passive observational science.
rows.statement: Design (Pillar 6): randomization itself creates the basis for inference (the randomization distribution induces a known null distribution) independent of modeling assumptions, and design as planned observation ('what data would you seek if you could generate it?') applies even to observational (non-randomized) studies -- a Kernel should store metadata about how data were generated/whether randomized, not treat data as merely 'given.'

rows.anchor: Complicated phenomena may be simplified by subducting the effect of known causes, leaving a residual phenomenon to be explained. It is by this process that science is chiefly promoted. ... The residual is not noise — it is the signal of something unknown.
rows.statement: Residual (Pillar 7): scientific progress often proceeds by subtracting known effects and examining what remains; a Kernel should distinguish explanatory residuals (signal, source of discovery) from random residuals (noise) rather than treating all residuals as error to ignore.

rows.anchor: Fisher's innovation was not just the formula but the theory that likelihood captures all relevant information in the data. ... a probability itself is a measure and needs a basis for comparison.
rows.statement: Likelihood is a theory (that it summarizes all relevant evidence in the data), not merely a formula; a probability requires a basis for comparison, so a Kernel must ask whether it treats likelihood as evidence-summary or as 'just another number.'

rows.anchor: a probability can be calculated for the simultaneous correctness of a large number of statements does not usually make that probability relevant for the measurement of the uncertainty of one of the statements. ... the garden of forking paths.
rows.statement: Multiple Comparison falsification question: does the Kernel treat multiple comparisons as independent, or account for the 'garden of forking paths' where joint-correctness probability is not the relevant uncertainty measure for any single statement?

rows.anchor: Stigler himself identifies the unresolved problem of the modern data/AI age as calibration and epistemic control when computation, dimensionality, exploratory paths and multiple comparisons become too large. That is almost exactly the problem KnowledgeOS is being designed to solve.
rows.statement: Main thesis: Stigler's book is a 'disciplined architecture for turning observations into defensible knowledge', arguably more important for KnowledgeOS than the Bayesian book, and KnowledgeOS should provide 'the epistemic infrastructure on which different reasoning methods can operate' rather than being 'the statistics system' or 'the Bayesian engine.'

rows.anchor: Probability is a measuring instrument, not a magic truth detector. ... likelihood can guide not only the conclusion but also: aggregation, analysis method, information accumulation. ... Inference should influence how evidence is acquired and represented.
rows.statement: Likelihood Lens: probability must never equal Truth in KnowledgeOS -- it is a calibrated measure tied to hypothesis/model/data-generating-assumptions/comparison class; and inference should feedback into evidence acquisition strategy (current hypothesis -> current uncertainty -> information need -> acquisition strategy -> analysis -> updated hypothesis), not just collect-then-analyze.
invariants: Probability is a measuring instrument, not a magic truth detector.

rows.anchor: Stigler's seven pillars are not seven independent modules. They form a loop. ... Aggregation changes what information is visible. That changes Information ... which generates new evidence. ... And Design controls how new observations enter the loop.
rows.statement: Reframes the seven pillars not as independent modules but as a feedback loop (Observations -> Aggregation -> Information Value -> Calibration -> Comparison -> Conditional Model -> Prediction -> Residual -> back to Observations), with Design controlling how new observations enter the loop, described as making KnowledgeOS resemble 'an epistemic operating system' (managing evidence/inference/state/access/lineage/primitives/agents the way an OS manages resources/processes/state/access/events/abstractions/applications).

rows.anchor: Knowledge is not the accumulation of information. Knowledge is the justified, calibrated, contextual and revisable reduction of uncertainty produced through an auditable process of observation, evidence acquisition, comparison, inference, model evaluation and learning.
rows.statement: Combined Chivers+Stigler candidate definition of knowledge as a justified, calibrated, contextual, revisable reduction of uncertainty produced through an auditable observation/evidence/comparison/inference/model-evaluation/learning process, feeding a full combined epistemic loop diagram surrounded by Time/Context/Relation/Scope/Governance/Traceability.

sources.note: A corpus seam of three files (step-012 identity/entity resolution/semantic equivalence, 2026-08-27; step-038 identity/entity resolution/equivalence/reference integrity, 2026-08-28; step-195 the identity-continuity model, 2026-08-29), the three highest equality-density files in the corpus, older than everything Step 288 v2 was built on. Contains: the context-relativized identity-transitivity invariant I_48 (first genuine equality-axis closure in the programme); a sixth relation 'Continuity' absent from every prior register; the theorem-shaped undecidability of semantic equivalence for arbitrary natural language (012 section 35); a four-codomain reconciliation via a Relation/Status product; the signature (but not body) for a family of partial epistemic functions Compare/Resolve/Normalize; a decision-theoretic asymmetric-loss framing of identity/equality resolution; and an architectural claim that KnowledgeOS is a federation of graphs (G_K, G_P, G_I, ...) rather than one graph.

rows.anchor: Identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context.
rows.statement: Resolves the standing transitivity problem for identity equivalence (cong_I), flagged unsafe by five independent loci (25J.27, 25S.6, 25S.29, 38.16, 38.47), via context-relativization: step-195's invariant I_48 states identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context, justified by 38.6/38.7/38.81's principle that RealWorldIdentity != DomainObjectIdentity and identity is contextual (KnowledgeOS must not globally impose a GlobalEntityIdentity where a domain has intentionally separate identities). Conclusion: cong_I is an equivalence relation within an identity context and is NOT one across contexts, so quotients exist per-context and are undefined globally -- described as the first genuine closure recorded on the equality axis by this research programme. Two provisos: (1) this resolves identity equivalence cong_I, not semantic equality (whether semantic equality is transitive within a semantic context remains open, though 25I.11's context-indexed relation is the same move); (2) 'identity context' itself is nowhere defined, so I_48 is well-formed with an unbound parameter, the same defect shape as other unbound relevance/observation parameters elsewhere in the programme. Step 195.15 also names the violation pattern A cong B and B cong C and A not-cong C as an 'identity consistency violation', proposed as a candidate checkable invariant.

type_signature.domain: reference x reference (within a fixed identity context)

invariants: I_48: identity equivalence transitive within a defined identity context
identity consistency violation: A cong B and B cong C and A not-cong C (195.15)

rows.anchor: three concepts, three questions, three answers ... Continuity appears in NONE of the five registers reconciled in Step 288
rows.statement: Recovers 'Continuity' as a sixth relation absent from every register the programme had reconciled: Identity ('is it the same entity?'), Continuity ('does the history of one connect meaningfully to the other?'), and Similarity ('how much does it resemble the other?') are three distinct, non-collapsible concepts (195.21), with Similarity always evidence FOR identity or continuity, never either itself (195.21, 38.77: Similarity != Identity). Continuity is functionally defined: Continuity(x,y) = f(IdentityRelation, TransitionLineage, DomainRules, Evidence) (195.51) -- a relation between entities across a lineage, distinct from history-relating relations and reference-relating relations. 195.24 (boxed): Identity and Lineage are ORTHOGONAL (same identity/different states; different identity WITH continuity; different identity/no continuity), agreeing independently with a separately-cited Step 261.9 finding that Identity and Provenance equality are independent dimensions. Consequence: the equality-family register is nine relations, not eight, and Continuity is unique in having a functional definition rather than a predicate one.

invariants: Identity and Lineage are orthogonal dimensions (195.24)
Similarity is evidence for Identity/Continuity, never identical to either (195.21, 38.77)

rows.anchor: Without locale/context, normalization is ambiguous -> Normalization is itself an epistemic operation ... Canonicalization must follow evidence, not precede it
rows.statement: Downgrades structural equality's decidability: Step 288 had placed '=' at Level 5 (decidable) throughout, qualified only by the id/mutable-state contradiction. Three loci show the decidability is itself conditional: 38.53 gives an ambiguous date string ('03/04/2026', 3 April or 4 March) showing normalization is itself an epistemic operation requiring locale/context; 38.85 states canonicalization must follow evidence, not precede it; 012 section 27 states canonicalization is not truth. Conclusion: '=' is decidable only relative to a fixed canonicalization, which the corpus forbids fixing a priori; the same defect applies to exact equality (defined as canonical serialization plus hash, 25J.2). Corrected count: zero state-level relations are unconditionally at Level 5, more severe than Step 288's own prior claim that one relation reaches Level 5.
invariants: canonicalization must follow evidence, not precede it (38.85)

lineage_claims.target: Step 288's claim that '=' unconditionally reaches Level 5
lineage_claims.quote: Corrected level: `=` is Level 5 CONDITIONAL ON a canonicalization that is not established

rows.anchor: G-62 Compare undefined ... 012 section 46 defines it: Compare: P x P x C x Omega -> Q, with two companions, both partial: Resolve, Normalize
rows.statement: Closes (narrows, not fully) the standing gap G-62 'Compare undefined': step-012 section 46 supplies a signature, Compare: P x P x C x Omega -> Q with Q = {Equivalent, Compatible, Contradictory, Related, Independent, Unknown}, plus two partial companion functions Resolve: R x C -\-> X and Normalize: R x Omega -\-> P. G-62 moves from OPEN-undefined to DEFINED(signature)-body-still-absent -- a signature is Level 3, not Level 6, so the gap narrows rather than closes. This reframes the programme's single named blocker 'Qualify' as one instance of a family of four partial epistemic functions (Qualify, Resolve, Normalize, Compare), all partial, all typed, none with bodies -- a better-posed problem (a discipline for partial epistemic functions) than a lone blocker.

rows.anchor: Semantic equivalence is generally not fully decidable ... equiv can NEVER reach Level 5 in the Boolean sense. This is a theorem-shaped limit, not a work item.
rows.statement: Strengthens the Level-5 verdict on semantic equality (previously marked undecidable only for the weak reason 'no procedure specified'): step-012 section 35 gives the strong reason -- for arbitrary natural language, semantic equivalence P1≡P2 is not generally decidable, so KnowledgeOS cannot promise it will always determine whether two arbitrary sentences mean the same thing. This is framed as a theorem-shaped limit, not a work item: semantic equality can never reach a total Boolean decision procedure. Section 35 draws the corollary that the system must be able to say 'I don't know whether these mean the same thing' as a feature, not a failure -- the same rule independently found at three other loci (Step 224.11, 25S.4, 38.22), now four independent loci agreeing.
invariants: semantic equality can never reach a total Boolean decision procedure for arbitrary natural language (012 section 35)

rows.anchor: FOUR rival codomains ... The relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty. ... SC = (P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status)
rows.statement: Corrects a prior count of two rival equality-decision codomains to four: 25S.3 {Same,Different,PossibleSame,Unknown}; 38.10 {Unknown,Candidate,Probable,Confirmed,Rejected,Contextual}; 012 section 35 {Determined,Supported,Candidate,Unknown}; 012 section 36/46 {Equivalent,Compatible,Contradictory,Related,Independent,Unknown}. Step 012 section 36 supplies the sorting principle: 'the relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty' -- distinguishing a Relation dimension (what holds) from a Status dimension (how well we know it); 25S.3 is flagged as conflating the two (Same/Different are relations, PossibleSame/Unknown are statuses). Corpus product forms are recovered (012 section 36/47): SC=(P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status), ComparisonResult=(Relation,Basis,Confidence,Context,Provenance), ResolutionResult=(CandidateEntity,Status,Evidence,Provenance) -- equality decisions return epistemic objects, not verdicts. A non-corpus reconciliation is offered (marked DERIVED, not corpus, not adopted): Decide_equiv: K x K -> (Relation x Status), noting three of the four corpus codomains are flattenings of this product -- the same defect shape independently noted for Sigma's ten-value flattening of five axes, a second (still unpromoted) occurrence of that pattern.
invariants: the relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty (012 section 36)

lineage_claims.target: Step 288 section 12's count of two rival codomains
lineage_claims.quote: Step 288 section 12 reported two. There are four.

rows.anchor: 038 treats equality as a classification problem with asymmetric loss ... Cost(FalseMerge) != Cost(FalseSplit) ... identity thresholds should be domain-specific
rows.statement: Recovers a decision-theoretic layer entirely absent from Step 288: identity/equality resolution is framed as classification under asymmetric loss -- false merge (38.18: wrong evidence aggregation, false conflicts, contaminated statistics) versus false split (38.19: duplicated knowledge, missed contradictions, fragmented provenance), with Cost(FalseMerge) != Cost(FalseSplit) implying identity thresholds should be domain-specific (38.20), a precision/recall tradeoff favoring conservative (high-precision) identity policies (38.21), and two invariants: UnknownIdentity should generally remain Unknown rather than being silently merged (38.22), and probabilistic identity must not silently become confirmed identity (38.23, 38.80). Explicitly flagged as well-posed but entirely unparameterized: no loss function, threshold, or calibration is specified, and it inherits the standing gap of no probability space (Omega, F, P) (G-22/MT-1), so a stated posterior like 'P(Same)=0.98' (38.23) has no measure-theoretic referent in this theory.
invariants: UnknownIdentity should generally remain Unknown rather than being silently merged (38.22)
probabilistic identity must not silently become confirmed identity (38.23, 38.80)

The defect's status as real is unchanged; only the credit for identifying the failure class moves to the corpus.

rows.anchor: 38.41-42 — a closure operation absent from my O discussion: Closure(Identity) ... KnowledgeOS = G_K + G_P + G_I + TemporalState + EpistemicControl (38.88)
rows.statement: Two further recoveries: (1) an identity closure operation absent from the operation discussion, Closure(Identity) computing AffectedKnowledge(x) (38.41-42), with identity merge/split/reassignment required to preserve lineage (195.53/I_50) and identity merge called 'a high-impact transition' (195.36), split called 'epistemically expensive' (38.40); (2) the kernel is architecturally a graph federation, not one graph: KnowledgeOS = G_K + G_P + G_I + TemporalState + EpistemicControl (38.88), with G_I/G_T/G_E/G_C/G_G forming 'a federation of semantic graphs over a common lineage model' that must interact but must not be collapsed (195.43, 38.87/38.88). This conflicts with the canonical kernel's single relational structure R (already reduced to 3 fields elsewhere in the programme): either R is a union of graphs the theory forbids collapsing, or the kernel is missing a component -- recorded as a structural question outside this step's scope, with an explicit caution (195.44) against reading this as a mandate for five separate graphs (risk of over-engineering).
missing: resolution of whether G_I is a separate kernel component or folded into R

rows.anchor: | transitivity unestablished -> quotients may not exist | RESOLVED for cong_I ... | | NINE — Continuity ... | zero unconditional Level-5 state relations
rows.statement: Net-effect summary on Step 288: transitivity RESOLVED for identity equivalence within a context (I_48, still open for semantic equality); relation count corrected from eight to NINE (Continuity was missing); '=' reaches Level 5 DOWNGRADED to conditional on an unestablished canonicalization, leaving zero unconditional Level-5 state relations; semantic-equality undecidability STRENGTHENED from 'no procedure specified' to 'not fully decidable, never reachable in the Boolean sense'; rival codomains corrected from two to FOUR, sorted by the Relation-vs-Status principle; 'Qualify is the irreducible blocker' REFRAMED as one of four partial epistemic functions; G-62 Compare NARROWED (signature given, body absent); the five-notion identity matrix gains contextual scoping and orthogonality to lineage; the grantId collision reclassified as corpus-anticipated; a new decision-theoretic layer and a new Closure(Identity)/G_I graph requirement are added. One thing is explicitly recorded as having gotten worse: '=' no longer reaches Level 5 unconditionally.

rows.anchor: ✅ **This is the one place the equality/identity problem admits a real narrowing:** `≅_I` **is** an equivalence relation within an identity context and **is not** one across contexts. Quotients exist per-context.
rows.statement: Restates and situates I_48 within the identity register: identity is context-scoped (38.6/38.7/38.79/38.81: RealWorldIdentity != DomainObjectIdentity; KnowledgeOS must not globally impose GlobalEntityIdentity; identity is contextual), giving I_48 (195.16) as the one place in the whole equality/identity programme that admits a real narrowing -- cong_I is an equivalence relation within an identity context and not one across contexts, so quotients exist per-context. Explicitly flags this as BOUNDED, not established, since 'identity context' is defined nowhere, and notes I_48-I_51 are numbered invariants in a research step with no adoption record.

rows.anchor: `38.76`: $\boxed{Identity\ is\ itself\ knowledge}$ ... `38.88`/`195.43` **`G_I` is a SEPARATE graph** that *"must not be collapsed"* — yet the canonical kernel has one `ℛ`, reduced to 3 fields.
rows.statement: Recovers that identity is itself a form of knowledge requiring its own epistemic machinery (38.76), with a status codomain IdentityStatus in {Unknown, Candidate, Probable, Confirmed, Rejected, Contextual} (38.10), a non-silent-promotion invariant (38.80: probabilistic identity must not silently become confirmed identity; 38.22: unknown identity should remain unknown), and an identity closure operation Closure(Identity) with AffectedKnowledge(x) (38.42). Notes the tension (also recorded in the identity-continuity seam) between G_I as a required separate graph (38.88/195.43, 'must not be collapsed') and the canonical kernel's single, three-field relational structure ℛ.
missing: resolution of whether G_I is a separate kernel component

rows.anchor: ## §15 THE RESULT DOMAIN — "decidable" vs "always returns a decision" ... $$\boxed{\text{A procedure that answers } Unknown \text{ is NOT a complete equality decision procedure.}}$$
rows.statement: Restates the four rival result-domain codomains (25S.3, 38.10, 012 §35, 012 §36/46) and the Relation-vs-Status sorting principle (012 §36), applying the mandate's own distinction between 'decidable relation' (a total procedure that returns TRUE/FALSE correctly) and 'procedure that always returns a decision' (a total procedure may legitimately answer Unknown without deciding); boxes the resulting principle that an Unknown-returning procedure is NOT a complete equality decision procedure, and reiterates 012 §35's theorem-shaped result that semantic equality can never reach a total Boolean procedure, agreeing with three other independent loci (224.11, 25S.4, 38.22) that this is a feature, not a failure.
invariants: a procedure that answers Unknown is not a complete equality decision procedure

rationale_evidence.anchor: Identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context.
rationale_evidence.statement: Resolves the standing transitivity problem for identity equivalence (cong_I), flagged unsafe by five independent loci (25J.27, 25S.6, 25S.29, 38.16, 38.47), via context-relativization: step-195's invariant I_48 states identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context, justified by 38.6/38.7/38.81's principle that RealWorldIdentity != DomainObjectIdentity and identity is contextual (KnowledgeOS must not globally impose a GlobalEntityIdentity where a domain has intentionally separate identities). Conclusion: cong_I is an equivalence relation within an identity context and is NOT one across contexts, so quotients exist per-context and are undefined globally -- described as the first genuine closure recorded on the equality axis by this research programme. Two provisos: (1) this resolves identity equivalence cong_I, not semantic equality (whether semantic equality is transitive within a semantic context remains open, though 25I.11's context-indexed relation is the same move); (2) 'identity context' itself is nowhere defined, so I_48 is well-formed with an unbound parameter, the same defect shape as other unbound relevance/observation parameters elsewhere in the programme. Step 195.15 also names the violation pattern A cong B and B cong C and A not-cong C as an 'identity consistency violation', proposed as a candidate checkable invariant.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Semantic equivalence is generally not fully decidable ... equiv can NEVER reach Level 5 in the Boolean sense. This is a theorem-shaped limit, not a work item.
rationale_evidence.statement: Strengthens the Level-5 verdict on semantic equality (previously marked undecidable only for the weak reason 'no procedure specified'): step-012 section 35 gives the strong reason -- for arbitrary natural language, semantic equivalence P1≡P2 is not generally decidable, so KnowledgeOS cannot promise it will always determine whether two arbitrary sentences mean the same thing. This is framed as a theorem-shaped limit, not a work item: semantic equality can never reach a total Boolean decision procedure. Section 35 draws the corollary that the system must be able to say 'I don't know whether these mean the same thing' as a feature, not a failure -- the same rule independently found at three other loci (Step 224.11, 25S.4, 38.22), now four independent loci agreeing.

rationale_evidence.anchor: FOUR rival codomains ... The relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty. ... SC = (P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status)
rationale_evidence.statement: Corrects a prior count of two rival equality-decision codomains to four: 25S.3 {Same,Different,PossibleSame,Unknown}; 38.10 {Unknown,Candidate,Probable,Confirmed,Rejected,Contextual}; 012 section 35 {Determined,Supported,Candidate,Unknown}; 012 section 36/46 {Equivalent,Compatible,Contradictory,Related,Independent,Unknown}. Step 012 section 36 supplies the sorting principle: 'the relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty' -- distinguishing a Relation dimension (what holds) from a Status dimension (how well we know it); 25S.3 is flagged as conflating the two (Same/Different are relations, PossibleSame/Unknown are statuses). Corpus product forms are recovered (012 section 36/47): SC=(P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status), ComparisonResult=(Relation,Basis,Confidence,Context,Provenance), ResolutionResult=(CandidateEntity,Status,Evidence,Provenance) -- equality decisions return epistemic objects, not verdicts. A non-corpus reconciliation is offered (marked DERIVED, not corpus, not adopted): Decide_equiv: K x K -> (Relation x Status), noting three of the four corpus codomains are flattenings of this product -- the same defect shape independently noted for Sigma's ten-value flattening of five axes, a second (still unpromoted) occurrence of that pattern.
